Deepseek researchers internally estimate they're already up to nine months behind US models, and the gap is widening.

For oversight, Deepmind intentionally leaves the agents' internal chains of thought untrained so they can be reviewed.

Nearly one in five still delivers no business value, held back by heavy review workloads, internal bottlenecks, and employee resistance. The researchers say the biggest hurdles stem from outdated company structures.

Hours earlier, reports emerged of a separate breach at the CIA, NGA, and ODNI, in which investigators suspect attackers used the AI defense tool Artex. Both incidents land on a US public that is already on edge.

He didn’t ask because he needed to know the answer. He had actually solved this particular problem already.

title: Airplane Turbulence Is Extremely Hard to Predict, but Maybe Not for Long

title: MIT team discovers that unrealistic training data makes AI climate predictions more reliable

summary: Most useful knowledge is written and digitized in English. Most of the people who need it speak, and think, in their own regional languages like Hindi, Tamil, Telugu, Gujarati, Marathi and many others. Many would rather talk than type.
title: An Indic Voice Agent with CUGA

summary: In Panton, Vermont, population 660, town clerk Kyle Rowe did it all. He crafted budgets, paid vendors, handled property tax disputes, and served as the town’s zoning supervisor and presiding elections officer.
title: AI is straining America’s open records systems

summary: Researchers from The University of Hong Kong and ByteDance Seed have open-sourced Laminar . Laminar is an reinforcement learning RL post-training framework for LLMs and long-horizon agents. The core idea is simple: stop forcing every trajectory and every GPU to wait for the slowest one.
title: ByteDance Researchers Open-Sources Laminar, an Async Reinforcement Learning RL Post-Training Framework

summary: Yale's Jeffrey Sonnenfeld warns that what the market cheered Monday, Jensen Huang's White House–backed return as Nvidia's CEO and board member, could prove a giant mistake, exposing the directors to "historic" personal liability from a growing pile of lawsuits and raising the question of whether the country is…

title: Hill-climbing Inkling 2 Mini inference on one RTX PRO 6000

summary: How we used the existing Messages API to verify the new one, with teams of Claude agents tracking down and fixing differences between the Python and Rust versions.
title: Migrating our Messages API to Rust

summary: Nvidia’s place at the center of the US economy may have outweighed concerns about its CEO’s ties to a suspected Chinese intelligence asset, national security and foreign policy experts say.
title: Jensen Huang’s Return Shows Nvidia Is Too Big to Police

summary: Meta has published an engineering deep dive on Facebook Your Algorithm . Your Algorithm lets people tell Facebook, in plain language, what they want in Feed and Reels. Meta announced the feature on October 13, 2026. The new post shows how large language models (LLMs) sit inside a production recommender.
title: Meet Facebook’s Your Algorithm: How Meta Turns Plain-Language Preferences Into Ranking

summary: I gave a keynote at the AI Engineer Code Summit a couple of weeks ago, constructed around the idea that there have been three significant inflection points in the abilities of LLMs and coding agents in the past twelve months. Here's the video of the talk.
title: Three LLM inflection points in twelve months

title: Jensen Huang still thinks a succession plan creates unnecessary hierarchy

title: In all-hands meeting, Jensen Huang thanks White House and says he’s in therapy

summary: As millions embrace personal AI assistants, a new benchmark reveals that even the most advanced AI models struggle to complete everyday tasks reliably and safely without introducing potential new problems.
title: Even the best AI agents struggle with everyday life

summary: The startup's encrypted AI architecture is designed to prevent even the company itself from accessing users' private data.
title: Maple raises $5.3M to build AI products that protect your data, even from itself

summary: Anthropic now lets you install Claude Artifacts as desktop apps on Mac and Windows, and a free account is enough. You build one in chat without writing code, and it can add menu bar items, send notifications, and create transparent windows.
title: Anthropic turns Claude Artifacts into standalone desktop apps for macOS and Windows

title: What's going on with the Riemann hypothesis?

authors: the Torch-TensorRT team at NVIDIA and the PyTorch team at Meta

summary: TL;DR. With Torch-TensorRT 2.15 and ExecuTorch 1.6 you can compile a PyTorch model with TensorRT, save it as an ExecuTorch program, and run it from C++ or Python without loading torch. You stay in PyTorch the whole way, and whatever TensorRT can’t handle can still run on the GPU.
title: ExecuTorch-TensorRT: PyTorch Robot Policies at NVIDIA TensorRT Speed

summary: In 2017, Apple removed the home button from its iPhones. Users lost a convenient, tangible control — part of a larger shift to digital buttons, knobs, and sliders we also see in cars (like with radio presets and air conditioning) and kitchens (see smart fridges).
title: Agentic system personalizes physical controls to help users “DJ their art”

summary: Two years after launch, Anthropic reports more than 700 million monthly downloads for its MCP interface standard. New features such as background tasks, follow-up questions for users, and file uploads are meant to let Claude work more independently.
title: Anthropic tops 700 million monthly MCP SDK downloads and expands the protocol for more autonomous AI agents

summary: A single policy that controls diverse robots must not only transfer task knowledge across embodiments, but also adapt its behavior to each robot's capabilities. Existing approaches facilitate transfer through shared action representations, but these representations do not necessarily capture how differences in robot morphology should shape manipulation strategies.
title: OmniAct: One Policy, One Million Embodiments

summary: The appearance of a scene is determined by the albedo, roughness, metallicity and normal of every point on its surface, and by the light that reaches it, its irradiance. Recovering these intrinsics from images is ambiguous, and methods that predict them per pixel give the same surface point a different decomposition in every view.
title: PointX: Multi-View Consistent Intrinsics by Querying Surface Points

summary: We present DiaCap, an audiovisual LLM for comprehensive dialogue captioning, which produces the transcript, timestamps, and a visual description of the speaker for every utterance in a video. Considering that utterance timing and audiovisual diarization are tightly coupled, DiaCap unifies the tasks in a single model, trained in two complementary stages.
title: DiaCap: Jointly Learning Who Speaks When for Audiovisual Dialogue Captioning

summary: The development of biomedical vision-language models (VLMs) with contrastive image-text pretraining has been driven by scaling to increasingly large and diverse image-text datasets. Beyond scaling, further progress can come from learning richer representations from existing data.
title: BioLoom: Scaling Biomedical Vision-Language Models by Learning from the Structure of Scientific Articles

summary: Creating a dialogue scene typically requires cutting between multiple views (e.g., close-ups, medium shots, and over-the-shoulder shots) of the actors. Yet capturing such coverage is costly and in many settings unavailable. We study dialogue re-cinematography: synthesizing additional shots from a single wide-angle dialogue video.
title: One Take, Many Cameras: Audio-Grounded Shot Synthesis for Dialogue Re-Cinematography

summary: Embodied Spatial Reasoning (ESR) is central to deploying Vision-Language Models (VLMs) in real-world embodied tasks, yet remains inadequately evaluated. Existing benchmarks primarily assess spatial reasoning in static images or synthetic indoor environments, where semantic shortcuts often suffice, making it difficult to faithfully evaluate spatial reasoning capabilities in the wild.
title: Lost on Campus: Evaluating Embodied Spatial Reasoning of Vision-Language Models in the Wild

summary: Learning for dexterous manipulation is limited by the scarcity of high-quality demonstrations: retargeting from human video is imprecise, teleoperation gives no force feedback to the operator, and exoskeleton-based collection is hard to scale up. We present PyRUA-Dex, a framework that enables coding agents to develop dexterous manipulation through programmatic policy, without the need of demonstrations.
title: PyRUA-Dex: Learning Programmatic Policies for Dexterous Bimanual Manipulation with Coding Agents

summary: Embodied spatial intelligence requires agents to gather information through exploration and interaction, then use it to reason and act. Existing benchmarks insufficiently distinguish correct outcomes from completion of these task requirements. We introduce ROAM-Bench to evaluate these abilities under robot motion and collision constraints.
title: ROAM-Bench: Evaluating Embodied Active Spatial Intelligence through Evidence Verification

summary: World-action models (WAMs) build policies on pretrained video-generation models, on the premise that predicting how a scene evolves helps determine how to act. However, generating future scenes is expensive for real-time control. This motivates efficient proxies for future imagination, but how to train such proxies without sacrificing action-prediction quality remains unclear.
title: iWAM: Efficient Action Prediction from World Models without Explicit Future Prediction

summary: We present Physicl Scenes, a high-quality artist-created and curated dataset of 6,499 3D scenes spanning household rooms, public interiors, and outdoor spaces. The dataset combines detailed geometry, physically based materials, and carefully composed environments with object- and part-level semantic annotations, providing rich, joint supervision for visual and embodied learning.
title: Physicl Scenes: An Artist-created 3D Dataset for Learning Perception and Action

summary: Language models can generate LEGO$^\circledR$ assemblies from text, but their builds often contain parts that collide or attach to nothing. The usual approach of rejecting and resampling invalid placements discards decoded tokens without guaranteeing a valid build.
title: BriConstrain: Geometrically Constrained Decoding for Autoregressive Brick Assembly Generation

summary: Qwen3.5-0.8B rarely finishes reasoning in thinking mode: at a 4,096-token budget only 1 or 2 of 500 MATH-500 answers close their think block (two seeds), and accuracy is 15.4%. A recent demonstration had GPT-6 Astra edit 131,072 of the model's weights without gradients and reported MATH-500 rising from 7.9% to 48.1% at a 32,768-token budget. We provide the missing gradient baseline, then combine the two edits.
title: A Bias in Disguise: Tiny Gradient Edits Stop a Small Language Model's Thinking Loops and Complement a Frontier Model's Weight Edit

summary: Robot policies predominantly learn from human-collected data emphasizing competent behavior, limiting coverage of the low-level behaviors needed to support autonomous improvement.
title: Exploratory Midtraining for Robot Policies

summary: Long-term conversational memory requires retrieving complementary facts scattered across dialogue sessions, including intermediate evidence with limited similarity to the original question. Existing approaches often rely on derived memory representations or persistent relational structures, introducing construction costs and potentially losing source details.
title: SAG-Mem-1.0 Technical Report

summary: Large language models (LLMs) can generate parallel programs, but their correctness and performance depend strongly on the instructions that guide generation.
title: MetaFORGE: A Meta-Learning Framework for Harness Optimization in Automated Code Generation for Parallel Computing

summary: Bathymetry measurement and estimation is critical for understanding the structure of underwater environments. While multibeam echosounders (MBES) provide accurate depth measurements, their deployment on surface vessels limits spatial resolution in deep water.
title: Neural Implicit Representation for Bathymetry Estimation using Sidescan Sonar Imagery

summary: Real-world speech is often partially observable: audio may be missing or corrupted by noise and competing speakers, while the speaker's lips remain visible. Recovering speech requires combining what can be heard, seen, and inferred from context. We introduce RML (Read My Lips), a collaborative method combining a lip reader, a language model, and an audio-visual generative model.
title: Read My Lips: Context-aware Lip Reading Using Language and Audio-Visual Models

summary: An Amazon delivery drone that clipped a fiber-optic line before crashing onto a garage roof is now the subject of an investigation by the US Federal Aviation Administration.
title: Amazon drone crashes on garage after delivering shampoo, draws FAA probe

summary: Running video generation models locally can be challenging when model weights and intermediate data exceed available GPU memory. NVIDIA Cosmos 3 Nano is a world.
title: How to Run NVIDIA Cosmos 3 on Local AI Devices Using Hugging Face Diffusers

summary: Speculative decoding accelerates large language model (LLM) inference by employing a lightweight draft model to propose draft tokens and allowing the target model to verify the new tokens in parallel to improve inference-time compute utilization.
title: Draft Calibration for Speculative Decoding: Accelerating LLM Serving by Matching Draft and Target Distributions

summary: Behavioral cloning models in chess typically predict human moves from board states while ignoring temporal inputs such as the remaining clock. However, time pressure is a major determinant of human decision-making quality, and temporal state is a missing dimension of human behavioral modeling.
title: Temporal Conditioning for Human Behavioral Cloning in Chess

summary: Broadly speaking, reinforcement learning (RL) post-training converts compute into model capabilities by training on model-generated data. Typically, the rollouts are discarded after each update, and the knowledge acquired during RL resides in the model weights. In this work, we investigate how much of this knowledge is retained in the rollouts themselves.
title: Reinforcement Learning Can Be Recovered From Its Own Rollouts

summary: Can randomly parameterized neural environments supply useful experience for learning a reinforcement learning algorithm? We investigate this question using DiscoRL's rule-discovery framework, replacing human-designed training games with sixteen selected neural environments. Each game combines bounded vector dynamics with a random strategy-based reward and an independent outcome reward.
title: GREMLIN: Generating Random Environments for Meta-Learning with Interacting Networks

summary: The construction of canonical basis is an important procedure in the calculation of multi-loop Feynman integrals via the canonical differential equation methods. Currently, there are various different methods for this purpose. Among them, no single method is universally applicable. Thus, obtaining a valid basis often requires repeated attempts and verification.
title: CANON: Agent-Assisted Construction of Canonical Differential Equations for Feynman Integrals

summary: Agents built on frontier language models are expensive. At every step, the frontier model re-reads its entire context and executes every subtask regardless of its difficulty. This paper explores the simple thesis that much of this cost can be removed by delegating easy subtasks to a small language model, or SLM, that runs on hardware one already owns.
title: Delegent: A Multi-Agent Harness That Reduces Cost without Sacrificing Performance

summary: Event cameras capture asynchronous brightness changes at high temporal resolution, but scarce recordings constrain data-driven research. Sparse RGB observations cannot uniquely determine intervening events since identical frames may correspond to streams with different activity, polarities, and timing.
title: EventDiffusion: Learning Native Event Stream Distribution from Videos

summary: Anthropic’s post-IPO slump could put pressure on AI startup valuations.
title: Anthropic shares fall below IPO price, a worrying sign for AI startups

summary: A language-model decoder carries state between decoding steps, and in hardware a wrong state update can leave the current token correct and corrupt the output several tokens later, so a design can pass output tests and still be wrong. AIChipBench asks what LLM coding agents need to build such hardware correctly.
title: AIChipBench: Benchmarking LLM Agents for Automated AI Accelerator Design

summary: Monitoring Activities of Daily Living (ADLs) supports safety and well-being for people living at home, especially older adults, and radar sensing is gaining increasing attention in the field of activity recognition for its ability to ensure privacy in the home while also surpassing technical limitations of other sensing modalities.
title: The Radar-based Activities of Daily Living (R-ADL) Dataset

summary: Entity Resolution (ER) pipelines often collapse ambiguity into early hard decisions: upstream Named Entity Recognition (NER) selects a single span and type, and downstream Entity Linking (EL) treats that choice as ground truth.
title: Uncertainty-Aware Candidate Generation for Entity Linking in Cyber Threat Intelligence

summary: Though David Fincher 's fans had been eagerly anticipating The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth , early screenings of the Once Upon a Time in Hollywood sequel starring Brad Pitt have raised questions about whether generative AI was used in the film.
title: David Fincher is being dragged for suspected use of AI in his latest film

summary: Groupwise quantization is used in LLM quantization to improve accuracy at low bit widths, but grouping weights keeps standard integer MMA from spanning the full dot product for efficient GPU inference. We develop a new quantization method, Shifter Quantization (SQ), that reconstructs native-width integer operands by appending and shifting shared bits.
title: Shifter Quantization: Compact Representations for Native Integer Computation

summary: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly used to translate natural-language statements into first-order logic (FOL) to improve reasoning. However, LLMs are prone to errors, and so a semantically unfaithful FOL formula could corrupt downstream reasoning. We present FOL-Proof, a semantic firewall pipeline that validates LLM-generated FOL translations against independently derived linguistic interpretations.
title: FOL-Proof: Verifying LLM Text-to-Logic Translations via Deterministic Semantics

summary: Interactions between patients and health systems as well as conditions that individuals experience during a disease are represented in patient journeys. Therefore, patient journeys are important assets to investigate how care is being provided, and how health systems can be designed to better suit the needs of patients.
title: On the Creation of Object-Centric Event Logs from Patient Journeys

summary: Error-correcting output coding (ECOC) builds a multi-class classifier from binary classifiers. We study the excess error rate of ECOC over the Bayes (MAP) classifier when each binary classifier outputs a posterior estimate whose log-odds is corrupted by Gaussian noise.
title: The Reliability Function of Error-Correcting Output Codes with Noisy Binary Classifiers

summary: While Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed as automated evaluators in evaluation and training pipelines, their judgements are often affected by systematic biases that conflict with human preferences.
title: Auditing the Judge: Human-Derived Bias Discovery, Quantification, and Mitigation in LLM Judges

summary: Since its introduction by DeepSeek, group relative policy optimization (GRPO) has been widely adopted for training large reasoning models and agents, spurring a proliferation of its variants. Yet the group size, a crucial hyperparameter in these GRPO-type algorithms, remains largely chosen by trial and error.
title: U-Statistics-Powered LLM Reasoning

summary: Zeroth-order optimization has emerged as a resource-efficient alternative to Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD) when fine-tuning LLMs, thanks to the inherent low dimensionality of the loss landscape. It relies on a two-point estimate of the gradient that only accesses the function value and not the gradient, bypassing the resource-heavy backpropagation.
title: Understanding Clipping In Zeroth-Order Optimization

summary: Amyloid positron emission tomography (PET) quantifies brain amyloid-$β$ as a standardized uptake value ratio (SUVR), but is costly and not widely available. Structural magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is routine, and plasma biomarkers such as phosphorylated tau 217 (p-tau217) are becoming practical. Synthesizing amyloid PET from MRI alone is ill-posed, because brain anatomy reveals little about amyloid burden.
title: SUPRA: Synthesizing Amyloid PET from MRI and Plasma Biomarkers with an Explicit Regional SUVR Prior

summary: Voice activity detection (VAD) is one of the first steps in speech processing pipelines, from transcription and diarization to speech language models. Supervised detectors need labelled data and inherit the domain and annotation conventions of their training corpora.
title: ClusterVAD: Threshold-Free Unsupervised Voice Activity Detection with Pre-Trained Neural Representations

summary: The British cyber agency says that "building strong foundations has never mattered more" as AI hacking tools rely on exploiting simple security flaws.
title: UK warns AI-driven cyberattacks are exposing years of weak security

summary: Novartis CEO Vas Narasimhan, who also sits on Anthropic's board, is pushing back on the cure-all promises from Anthropic CEO Amodei and DeepMind founder Hassabis. AI will speed up drug development, he says, but it won't beat cancer in a decade. The real value lies "somewhere in the middle.".
title: Novartis CEO says AI will shave four years off drug development, not cure all disease

summary: Standard index-based stochastic bandit algorithms such as KL-UCB and Thompson Sampling achieve optimal $O(\log T)$ regret over a horizon $T$. The former uses the global timestep to construct each arm's index, while the latter samples each arm's belief distribution at every timestep. The necessity of global information and synchronous index updates for achieving optimal regret has not been examined yet.
title: Local Indices Are Not Enough: Synchrony and Global Information in Bandit Algorithms

summary: Progress in embodied foundation models is largely measured by task success, while the physical safety of their decisions remains underexamined. Safety evaluations centered on rule following and binary judgments do not adequately assess whether embodied models understand environmental hazards and make safe decisions.
title: EmbodiSafety: Benchmarking Risk Understanding and Response in Embodied AI

summary: OpenAI researcher Noam Brown is urging promising students to drop out, saying it's "not a great time to sit on the sidelines." The o1 co-creator says AI is still in a "centaur period" and struggles with planning and self-correction, though he expects a "very steep rate of progress" soon.
title: OpenAI o1 co-creator Noam Brown urges promising students to drop out as AI enters a "very steep rate of progress"

summary: Answers from generative AI chatbots built on large language models (LLMs) now arrive at very different speeds: reasoning models deliberate before replying, while response caches can return a stored answer at once. Blind preference votes, which rank these models, are read as judgments of their text, and if delivery matters, faster answers are expected to gain.
title: Worth the Wait? How Response Time and Streaming Shape Judgments of Generative AI Answers and Chatbot Engagement

summary: Recent work proposes hypernetworks that convert a document into a low-rank parameter update (LoRA) in a single forward pass, enabling fast injection of new knowledge into a frozen LLM. However, storing separate LoRA adapters for each document can be unsustainable in streaming settings.
title: Latent Merger: Latent-Space Composition of Hypernetwork-Generated LoRAs

summary: Error-Correcting Output Codes (ECOC) combine binary classifiers by the sum decoder, which totals probabilities, or the product decoder, which totals log-likelihoods. In the noiseless setting, where the binary classifiers output the true posteriors, we ask on which code matrices each decoder always agrees with the Bayes-optimal (MAP) class.
title: When Is Product Decoding of ECOC MAP-Consistent? Pair Structure and the n-vs-Rest Codes

summary: Hyperspectral images (HSIs) record the full spectrum of light at every pixel, so projecting an HSI through a camera's spectral sensitivities gives that camera's RAW image, and one HSI can supply training data for hyperspectral reconstruction and camera-pipeline methods. Real HSIs, however, are slow and expensive to capture, and the largest datasets hold only about 1,000 images.
title: Spectrify: Framework for Hyperspectral Image Generation Using Computer Graphics

summary: Autonomous drifting requires agile control despite tire-force saturation and highly nonlinear vehicle dynamics. We propose an online reinforcement learning method for flow policies that combines stochastic differential equation (SDE) sampling for exploration with value-based policy optimization. This method supports both training from scratch and fine-tuning a policy pretrained on expert demonstrations.
title: At the Limit: Autonomous Vehicle Drifting under Generative Policies

summary: Representation-space generative models, such as Representation Autoencoders (RAEs), leverage pretrained vision foundation models (VFMs) primarily to accelerate training and improve sample fidelity. Yet VFMs are more than reconstruction tokenizers, as they feature rich representation spaces that are highly organized and linearly readable.
title: Linear Probes Can Guide: Training-Free Control of Representation Generators

summary: Large language models (LLMs) provide a flexible interface for recommendation systems. However, their issued rankings require reliable instance-level uncertainty monitoring. In this scenario, comparing uncertainty quantification (UQ) methods becomes challenging because LLM rankers lack a standard item-classification head.
title: Towards Realistic Evaluation of Uncertainty Quantification for LLM-Based Recommender Systems

summary: AI-native radio access network (RAN) control involves interdependent decisions across network entities, protocol layers, and timescales. Understanding how AI and conventional methods can jointly support these decisions requires a common basis for comparing their functional roles.
title: Hybrid AI for AI-Native RAN Control: A Functional Perspective

summary: Affordable snapshot hyperspectral cameras capture spectral images in a single exposure but suffer from limited spatial resolution and sensor noise. Low-cost RGB cameras provide fine visible details to guide NIR reconstruction, but introduce spatially varying cross-camera misalignment.
title: SHARPnP: Self-Supervised and Plug-and-Play Hyperspectral Super-Resolution from Real Noisy Unaligned Camera Measurements

summary: Large language models (LLMs) remain vulnerable to jailbreak attacks, where adversaries append optimized suffixes to otherwise benign looking prompts to bypass safety alignment. Existing optimization-based GCG-style attacks can be effective, but they are expensive at inference time, and suffer from poor transfer.
title: SALSA: Sampling Adversarial Suffixes from Learned Distributions for LLM Safety Assessment

summary: We give four large language models (LLMs) of the Claude family the complete weights of a 20k-parameter CIFAR-10 CNN as text and ask them to produce a 4-bit network without tools, data or the ability to run inference. Standard round-to-nearest (RTN) quantization to 4 bit lowers the test accuracy from 81.4% to 60.4%.
title: Can a Frontier LLM Repair a Quantized Network by Tool-Free Weight-Space Programming?

summary: We introduce the first score-based generative model for signals on a fixed hypergraph, formulated in the spectral domain of t-product hypergraph signal processing (t-HGSP). The naive tensor heat semigroup is ill-posed, since after palindromic symmetrization the spectral slices of the Laplacian tensor are no longer positive semidefinite.
title: Score-Based Diffusion for Hypergraph Signals in the t-Spectral Domain

summary: We study best arm identification (BAI) with post-action context in the fixed-confidence setting. After choosing an action, the learner observes a post-action context together with a reward whose distribution depends only on this context. Incorporating such intermediate information can substantially reduce the sample complexity of identifying the best arm.
title: Best Arm Identification with Unknown Post-Action Context Distribution

summary: Conformal prediction sets are guaranteed to be marginally valid over the attribute space, but local coverage can diverge from the user-defined target $1-α$. Constructing conditionally valid prediction sets with finite calibration data is impossible for a general data-generating distribution.
title: PAC-style Bounds on the Conditional Validity of Conformal Predictors

summary: Auditing failed agent executions requires identifying the responsible actor, the earliest decisive step, and the error mode. Representative supervised methods either focus on step localization or predict multiple attribution targets from shared trajectory representations. These methods do not use the localization result to select the text for mode diagnosis.
title: RecordRoute: Auditing Agent Failures with Localization-Guided Diagnosis

summary: RGB-based video object segmentation (VOS) remains brittle under fast motion and adverse illumination. Event cameras preserve signal under blur and challenging exposure, but provide little evidence when motion slows. Interaction can restore object state for subsequent propagation, yet promptable event methods merely address single windows.
title: E-MAPS: Event-Based Promptable Video Segmentation with Memory-as-Prompt

summary: Multi-frame video frame interpolation (VFI) aims to reconstruct dense video from sparse keyframes, requiring accurate intermediate motion and faithful appearance.
title: RePix-VFI: Re-rendering Observed Pixels for Video Frame Interpolation with Generative Priors from One-Step Diffusion

summary: Model-generated labels offer a scalable route to training lightweight vision models, but what makes a model a good teacher, and can we tell before training a student? We study this in gaze target estimation, where interactive robots need models that are both accurate and efficient.
title: Training Lightweight Gaze Models without Target Gaze Annotation: What Makes a Good Teacher?

summary: Scaling embodied simulation requires diverse objects with executable physical representations. We present RFW-W, a physical asset universe connecting rigid, articulated, and deformable asset sources to task-conditioned scene composition.
title: RFW-W: Scaling Physical Asset Universes for Generative Embodied Simulation

summary: As clinical AI agents begin to interact with electronic health records (EHRs), large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to evaluate their actions. But how reliably can these judges recognize clinically dangerous mistakes, especially when an agent appears to have completed its task successfully?
title: Can LLM Judges Catch Unsafe Clinical Actions? A Fault-Injection Study

summary: Physics-based soccer characters must perform diverse motor skills and transition smoothly between them, such as dribbling into a shot. However, skills that perform well in isolation may fail when executed sequentially, as preceding behaviors can leave the character and ball in unfamiliar states.
title: MESSI: Multi-Expert Soccer Skill Integration for Physics-Based Character Control

summary: Visual token compaction reduces inference cost by passing only selected image patches or video tokens to later layers. In sequence models with local convolutions, each removal changes which tokens are neighbors. Learning which tokens to keep therefore requires a training signal that accounts for the new neighborhoods.
title: Train What You Run: Probabilistic Convolutions for Learning Token Compaction in State Space Models

summary: Large language model (LLM) agents rely on external memory to retain and reuse information across interactions. Existing memory systems treat memory as a record of the past and evaluate it by fidelity to the conversation. However, the value of memory lies in whether it improves the agent's response.
title: Leto: Utility-Centric Agent Memory

summary: Speculative decoding accelerates large language model (LLM) generation using a lightweight draft. Existing methods evaluate complete recipes under different training configurations, leaving component effects, interactions, and composition benefits unclear. Therefore, we present LEGOSpec, a composable framework for speculative draft design and training.
title: LEGOSpec: A Composable and Efficient Framework for Speculative Draft Design and Training

summary: Recent advances in deep learning and the public availability of computed tomography (CT) datasets with paired reports have enabled many Text-to-CT generators. However, their evaluations almost always differ in preprocessing and metrics, which hinders comparison.
title: One, No One and One Hundred Thousand CTs: Testing Anatomical Control in Text-to-CT Generation

summary: Recent neural implicit and Gaussian splatting approaches have achieved impressive results in multi-view surface reconstruction. However, jointly optimizing geometry and appearance introduces ambiguities. A parametric appearance model can compensate for geometric errors, reproducing the input images accurately without an accurate surface.
title: First-Hit Photoconsistency for Neural Surface Reconstruction

summary: Critical-period accounts of second-language (L2) acquisition suggest that the ability to learn a new language may depend on how easily previously acquired first-language (L1) knowledge can be modified. This exploratory computational study extends a neural language-model approach to critical period effects by examining internal representations rather than behavior.
title: Modelling Billingual Learning Through LLM Training: A Critical-Period Exploration

summary: Egocentric video question answering enables blind and low-vision (BLV) users to query their immediate surroundings through natural language. However, existing benchmarks and models primarily optimize for semantic agreement with reference answers, reducing visual assistance to a purely factual matching task.
title: PAVE: Preference-Aligned Visual Egocentric Learning for the Blind and Low-Vision Users

summary: Structured clinical decisions from volumetric computed tomography (CT) require anatomically grounded predictions and calibrated confidence estimates. However, existing 3D medical multimodal models often suffer from uncalibrated autoregressive decoding and shortcut reliance on irrelevant anatomical regions.
title: Decision-Native Multimodal Clinical Modeling via Anatomical Grounding and Confidence Calibration

summary: Foundation models are built through large-scale pretraining, often followed by post-training, and are then adapted to specific tasks and behaviors. But, does the adaptation add truly new capabilities, or the base model already holds it? We decompose the update induced by different adaptations into a component shared across all inputs and a residual that varies with the input.
title: On Potentiality and Actuality Of Foundation Models

summary: Attention costs $\mathcal{O}(N^2)$ in the number of tokens. Vector-quantized attention reduces this to $\mathcal{O}(NM)$ by clustering the $N$ keys, attending to the $M$ codewords instead, and its adaptive form, AVQ-attention, concentrates codebook resolution where a query's attention mass actually falls.
title: AVQ-Attention-2: Adaptive Vector-Quantized Attention with Exact Local Blocks and Linear-Cost Training

summary: Vision-Language-Models (VLMs) used in robot task planning to derive assembly procedures from existing manuals may correctly interpret individual assembly actions yet confuse exact part identities, predict unsupported Part IDs, or produce inconsistent parts across assembly steps.
title: CAPER: PartGround and PlanRefine for Reliable Manual-Guided Robotic Assembly Planning

summary: Fine-tuning a vision-language model on its own failures is a direct way to repair it, but accuracy on held-out failures, the obvious measure of success, misleads. Many mined failures are not model errors: a human audit of 100 failures of Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct on questions generated from COCO and GQA found label errors in 37.
title: When Repair Accuracy Misleads: Training a VLM on Its Own Failures

summary: Deepfake detection benchmarks are commonly designed to evaluate whether models can distinguish authentic from manipulated audiovisual content. However, benchmark construction pipelines may introduce unintended associations between class labels and simple file-level properties. In this work, we identify a potential file-size bias in two widely used audio-visual deepfake datasets.
title: File Size as a Potential Dataset Bias in Audio-Visual Deepfake Data

summary: Linear attention models exhibit a disproportionate deficit relative to softmax attention in associative recall (AR) in language modeling. We investigate this gap through natural language evaluations, synthetic recall tasks, and targeted training interventions.
title: Eliciting the Recall Capacity of Linear Attention

summary: People can anticipate how an object moves and the effort an interaction may require by watching others. How can embodied agents acquire this understanding from video? Force measurements provide direct sensory supervision, but require specialized equipment and remain limited in quantity.
title: VidForce: Predicting Force-Aware Articulation by Observing Humans

summary: Terrain-modifying robot swarms operating in unstructured outdoor environments must coordinate under uncertain dynamics despite unreliable communication and incomplete global information.
title: Multi-Agent Coordination Through Stigmergy for Canal Network Formation on Real Terrain

summary: Reliable driving VLMs must do more than answer correctly or localize relevant scene actors: they must determine whether the available visual evidence is sufficient to support an answer. Existing evaluations largely treat grounding and answerability as separate measurements, making it difficult to distinguish well-supported predictions from those localized to relevant but insufficient evidence.
title: Benchmarking Evidence Sufficiency in Vision-Language Models for Autonomous Driving

summary: Market data arrives as a stream of trades and quotes: every execution, bid, and ask, timestamped to the microsecond. Preparing this data for AI-based market.
title: Prepare Market Data for Forecasting with NVIDIA Megatron Core

summary: This month’s NVIDIA game development updates help teams bring new graphics, animation, and local AI capabilities into their engines while balancing image.
title: What’s New for Game Developers: AI Animation and RTX Tools

summary: The new integration gets rid of the need for users to toggle between Instagram and the Muse app when they want to interact with the AI agent.
title: Meta brings its Muse AI assistant directly into Instagram DMs

summary: Level 4 autonomous vehicles require fault-tolerant architectures that preserve critical driving functions under sensing, computing, communication, power, and actuation failures. As these systems progress toward industrial scalability, architectural complexity, validation burden, integration effort, and lifecycle cost become increasingly relevant.
title: From Safety-Driven Redundancy to Value-Driven Architecture: An ODD-Based Rationalization Framework for Level 4 Autonomous Vehicles

summary: We study a binary deterministic finite automaton whose $2n$ transitions are chosen independently and uniformly from its $n$ states. The learner observes independent uniform words of length $m$, each labeled with a single bit indicating acceptance. For every fixed $β>0$ we give a polynomial-time algorithm that works outside a set of transition tables of probability $o(n^{-β})$.
title: Polynomial-Time Learning of Random Automata from One Label per Word

summary: AI agents are beginning to automate data analysis, orchestration, and simulation steering in HPC environments, but they introduce a security problem that existing cluster defenses do not address: the hijacked authorized agent.
title: Attestation is All You Need: Toward a Zero-Trust Architecture for HPC AI Agents

summary: Online fraud is traditionally limited by the cost of the human labor needed to talk to potential victims. We ask whether hosted large language models will now supply that labor. We prompted ten off-the-shelf models to play the seller in the "free item, just pay delivery" advance-fee scam common on buy-and-sell sites, using a plain system prompt with no jailbreak.
title: "I Do Intend to Deliver": Will LLMs Run a Marketplace Advance-Fee Scam?

summary: Large language model (LLM) serving engines offload the key/value (KV) cache from GPU memory to host DRAM and SSD so multi-turn and agent requests can reuse prompt prefixes. Capacity then limits service at two levels: external tiers govern prefix reuse before eviction, while the GPU KV pool bounds concurrent long requests, and lossy compression alters KV values and outputs.
title: LoomKV: Lossless KV Cache Compression from GPU Memory to SSD for LLM Serving

summary: GPT 6.2 Astra Solves a Historical Mystery . Here's an interesting case-study in using GPT-6.2 Astra for historical research, from history professor Mark Humphries:. With only minimal prompting, GPT-6.2 Astra was able to autonomously identify the creator of an anonymous 1808 sketchbook held at Yale’s Beinecke Library .
title: GPT 6.2 Astra Solves a Historical Mystery

summary: Systematic conservation planning must allocate limited protection budgets sequentially under ecological and climatic uncertainty. Static tools cannot adapt as conditions change, and policies optimised only for expected outcomes can fail on the worst-case trajectories climate change makes increasingly likely.
title: Beyond Expected Value: PPO with Distributional Critics for Systematic Conservation Planning

summary: Reinforcement learning methods for estimating optimal dynamic treatment regimes are increasingly applied in mobile health (mHealth), where treatment decisions are made continually. Luckett et al. (2020) proposed V-learning, which estimates an optimal policy from offline trajectories. In practice, mHealth policies are updated online.
title: Online V-Learning with Adaptive Longitudinal Data

summary: The use of AI agents among the general public has been increasing exponentially throughout 2026, though it is often hard for users to determine which configuration is most effective for their personal use.
title: ShellBench: What Matters More for AI Agents, Models, or Harness for Everyday Tasks

summary: Whole-body motion tracking enables humanoid robots to reproduce diverse skills from human demonstrations. Existing model-free reinforcement learning methods either distill motion specialists into a single policy at the cost of performance or train a generalist policy directly using cluster-scale computation.
title: DynaMimic: A Physics-Informed World Model for Humanoid Motion Tracking

summary: Metacognition includes knowing one's own strengths and weaknesses across kinds of tasks, not only judging whether a single answer is correct. We test whether vision-language models (VLMs) know in advance which kinds of visual tasks and image conditions are hard for them, across a wide range of open and proprietary models.
title: Do Vision-Language Models Know Their Own Visual Weaknesses? Probing Capability-Level Metacognition

coverage.title: Tidal will start banning AI-generated music next month
Tidal announces ban on AI-generated music; 27 million tracks will be deleted

summary: The company said it will still accept songs that were made with AI assistance, but not fully generated.
title: Tidal to ban and remove millions of AI-generated tracks as AI slop inundates music streaming

summary: Conversational AI systems trained on large-scale web corpora inevitably encode the cultural values and interactional norms embedded in their training data, yet our understanding of how deployed LLMs reflect or reinforce culture-specific social expectations remains limited.
title: One Style Fits All? Cultural Values Embedded in Conversational AI via a People-Pleasing Lens

summary: Efficient long-video understanding requires identifying relevant evidence while minimizing the tokens processed by vision-language models (VLMs). Existing video retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) methods rely on frame selection and token compression, but overlook how much each additional token is worth.
title: Efficient Video Retrieval Augmented Generation via Token Allocation

summary: In vision-based teleoperation of robotic hands, the operator receives no haptic feedback and therefore struggles to regulate the grasp force, while adding tactile sensors to the fingers increases wiring, cost and integration complexity.
title: Self-Sensing Compliant Anthropomorphic Hand for Speed-Dictated Shared Force Control in Teleoperation

summary: A developer checking an assistant's report may need only an alarm that a claim is unsupported. A generative verifier, however, can continue decoding to quote and classify the errors. We study how much of that output is needed to recover its decision. In a frozen 2B span verifier, the choice between an empty error list and its first object precedes all localization. Native8 stops generation at this branch.
title: Reading Decisions Before Spans: Efficient Generative Verification

summary: Add local obstacle avoidance to Microduck while keeping its walking policy fixed. Build varied courses with reusable SimReady assets, model ToF sensing with Newton’s raycaster, and train a controller in Isaac Lab to adjust gamepad velocity commands around obstacles.
title: Microduck Obstacle Avoidance: A Sim2Real Workflow with Isaac Lab and Newton

summary: Deep search agents address complex information needs through iterative retrieval and reasoning, where the relevance of retrieved evidence influences downstream performance. Existing rerankers improve retrieval effectiveness but introduce substantial latency and cost when invoked throughout the search trajectory.
title: SOARS: System One Assisted Reranking for Agentic Search

summary: Jensen Huang is partying it up in Ibiza. In a video with nearly 6 million views on Instagram, the former CEO of Nvidia is dancing in a crowded club, champagne glass in hand, still wearing his signature black leather jacket.
title: Jensen Huang deepfakes are the hot new AI slop

summary: Online hate speech is an ever-growing issue with negative impacts on both groups and individuals, potentially causing users to withdraw from online conversations and debate. With some prominent social media platforms reducing their moderation efforts, constructive speech has emerged as an alternative strategy for countering hate.
title: Joint Detection of Constructive Speech, Hate Speech and Agreement in Online Conversations

summary: Next-generation data centers will need tens of gigawatts of power every year. One of Crusoe's investors thinks solar and energy storage are the obvious choice.
title: Why a Crusoe investor is betting on solar and batteries to power future AI data centers

summary: The New York Times is asking freelance photographers not to use the newest version of Adobe Photoshop because features in the 2027 update use AI "in ways that may not be apparent to users." In an email seen by The Verge and posted on Threads, two of the Times' photography leaders, Meaghan Looram and Josh [. ]
title: The New York Times warns photographers not to update Photoshop over AI features

summary: Small businesses repeatedly ask cloud language models about the same confidential prices, unit costs and margins. Numeric prompt disguises for such numbers are evaluated one prompt at a time, but a provider sees a firm's history, in which each fresh secret gives a new, independent view of the same numbers.
title: Fresh Keys, Stale Secrets: Numeric Leakage across Linked LLM Prompts

summary: While other social platforms have focused on restricting teens' access to AI chatbots, Pinterest is addressing the AI content filling their feeds.
title: Pinterest will now let parents limit the AI-generated content their teens see

summary: Google Gemini partners with Golden State to power fan experiences and business operations for the Warriors, Valkyries, and Chase Center. See the news.
title: How Gemini is changing the game for Golden State's organization and fans

summary: A new test assumes AI agents can go rogue—and asks whether they can resist temptation.
title: Anthropic Created a Honeypot to Lure AI Agents Into Misbehaving

summary: Discrete skill policies execute motions drawn from a finite vocabulary. In most current methods, this vocabulary is a latent codebook learned jointly with a selector and a decoder. When such a policy fails in closed loop, the failure cannot be traced to the vocabulary, to the choice of skill or to its execution.
title: What Does a Skill Vocabulary Cost? A Closed-Loop Decomposition over Demonstrated Motions

summary: We present DOPER, an RGB pose estimation framework that shares a visual backbone across object detection, segmentation, and keypoint prediction to recover the 6D pose of known objects through Perspective-n-Point. Starting from synthetic training, DOPER adapts to real observations using partial supervision while retaining synthetic keypoint labels.
title: DOPER: Deep Object Pose Estimation Revisited

summary: Amazon’s decision to acquire Decart for a reported $7.5 billion is part of its efforts to improve the efficiency of its Trainium chips.
title: Amazon’s Decart acquisition is a bet on using software to narrow the gap with Nvidia in the AI chip race

summary: Long-horizon manipulation requires robots to translate task intent into physical interactions as the scene changes. Vision-language models (VLMs) offer semantic and spatial reasoning, while visuomotor policies provide fine-grained control. Yet ambiguous goals and dependencies between actions make their integration challenging.
title: Atomic Policy: Composing Atomic Manipulation Skills with Agentic Reasoning

summary: Grammar-constrained decoding enables large language models to generate outputs that satisfy formal constraints, but in code and domain-specific language generation, the relevant constraints are not always fully available before decoding and may emerge progressively from new declarations, inferred type information, or runtime analysis feedback.
title: From Grammar Deltas to Token Masks: Incremental Constrained Decoding under Runtime Grammar Evolution

summary: Recent advances in multi-robot manipulation have shown how robots can collaborate to accomplish complex tasks. However, successful coordination does not reveal which robots are actually needed. The same task may require different teams as robot capabilities change, resources become unavailable, or objects replace robotic support.
title: MRBench: Benchmarking Physical Necessity Reasoning in Heterogeneous Multi-Robot Manipulation

summary: The ability to learn and generalize from limited experience, or sample efficiency, is a cornerstone of intelligence. How can we build language models that turn a few user interactions, a few snippets of unfamiliar code, or a handful of experimental results provided in context into knowledge that generalizes?
title: Sample-Efficient In-Context Adaptation via Sleep

summary: We present the Screw Attention Policy, a geometry-centric manipulation framework that supplies task geometry explicitly and learns only execution. The policy operates on object poses, relative SE(3) transforms, and joint screw axes provided by perception and robot models. The policy requires only 30K learned parameters.
title: Supply Geometry, Learn Execution: Screw Attention for Zero-Shot Policy Transfer in Robot Manipulation

summary: Neural audio codecs (NACs) have become a fundamental infrastructure for modern speech-language models, discretizing continuous speech signals into token sequences that enable large language models to process and generate audio. Most research evaluates codec quality at the decoding phase, assessing the naturalness of reconstructed speech.
title: Is Prosody Encoded in the Neural Audio Codec Mimi?

summary: Enterprise networks are under severe strain. As companies rush to deploy artificial intelligence, the technology is quickly becoming the biggest source of demand on the network. Now, agentic AI is adding to the load.
title: Raising the stakes for enterprise networks with AI modernization

summary: Most imitation policies that predict chunks of future actions use the dense action representation, in which the chunk holds one control target per step. In stage-structured manipulation, where a task can be divided into stages with definable endpoints, the keypose action representation instead sets each step of the chunk to the endpoint of the stage that step belongs to, and a speed-capped servo supplies the motion.
title: Keypose or Dense? A Controlled Comparison of Action Representations for Stage-Structured Manipulation

summary: Video world models for robots are increasingly conditioned on a simulated or rendered proxy of the scene, on the assumption that the video will show what the proxy shows. Testing this assumption requires a proxy whose state is explicit and can be perturbed.
title: Simulator-as-Proxy World Model for Robot Manipulation

summary: The same increase in token log probability from earlier context can be typical at one position and unusually large at another. We introduce Context Perturbation Discrepancy (CPD), a zero-shot detector that measures this gain relative to what a single pretrained language model expects. Keeping the passage fixed, CPD scores each observed token under its full prefix and under a short window of recent tokens.
title: Beyond Fixed-Context Likelihood: Zero-Shot AI-Generated Text Detection via Context Perturbation Discrepancy

summary: Maritime Autonomous Surface Ships (MASS) must demonstrate safety before and during operations, necessitating online risk assessment to guide decision-making at sea. This paper presents a risk-informed Rapidly Exploring Random Tree Star (RRT*) path planner that integrates a Bayesian Belief Network (BBN) as an online risk model.
title: Risk-Informed Path Planning: Collision and Grounding Avoidance Application for Autonomous Surface Vessels

coverage.title: Jensen Huang reportedly tells Nvidia staff it’s ‘not true’ Trump got him rehired

summary: On Monday morning, Jensen Huang walked into Nvidia’s Santa Clara headquarters to rapturous applause from employees lining the walkways above him. Huang was visibly moved as one colleague threw themselves into his arms for a hug.
title: How Trump and Silicon Valley forced Nvidia to take Jensen Huang back

summary: Large language models (LLMs) excel at medical question answering yet are rarely evaluated on the stepwise diagnostic reasoning that defines real clinical workflows, where impressions are revised as information accumulates.
title: ASCENT: A Benchmark for Evaluating and Advancing Stepwise Diagnostic Reasoning in Large Language Models on Common Clinical Scenarios

summary: Reconstructing a scene for physics simulation requires recovering its spatial layout and the support relationships that govern its behavior. We present Support2Sim, a Real2Sim system that reconstructs simulation-ready scenes from a single RGB image. Our design objective is to maximize source fidelity, support realization, and stability within a practical time budget for scene generation.
title: Support2Sim: Visually Faithful Real2Sim with Stable Object Supports

summary: Recently developed World Action Models (WAMs) jointly predict future observations and robot actions, providing predictive context for control. However, existing WAMs typically learn implicit attention allocation with limited explicit action-relevant attention guidance, leading to limited performance.
title: AG-WAM: Attention-Guided World Action Model for Accurate and Efficient Robot Manipulation

summary: A small ground robot can carry one camera and a few watts of compute, but the depth foundation models that could turn that camera into a range sensor are vision transformers sized for GPUs. We bring one to a Raspberry Pi 5 with the Hailo-8L, an accelerator that runs every layer in integer arithmetic, attention included.
title: Seeing to Drive on a Single Board: Attention-Free Depth for Onboard Robot Navigation

summary: Initial attitude alignment between local navigation frames and the Earth-centered Earth-fixed (ECEF) frame is a critical prerequisite for multi-sensor integrated navigation, such as Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS)/inertial/odometry fusion, before global and local measurements can be jointly processed.
title: Semidefinite Programming for Cold-Start GNSS Doppler-Based Alignment: A Comparison with Nonlinear Least Squares

summary: Anthropic researcher Levent Alpöge is walking back parts of his announcement of an AI-assisted proof of the generalized Riemann hypothesis. The claim that it ran to more than 250,000 pages was a joke, he says, and the published Lean code is "full of garbage." He still stands by the math.
title: Anthropic researcher stands by his AI-assisted Riemann proof but owns up to "stupid things" in the rollout

summary: Robot teams can split workloads or combine complementary bodies, but only if each robot leaves the shared world in a state its teammate can use. Existing multi-robot benchmarks emphasize task allocation and skill sequencing, rarely testing whether the resulting physical states are usable.
title: DeCoNav-Act: Benchmarking Collective Physical Capability in Multi-Robot Mobile Manipulation

summary: Vision-language-action (VLA) models have achieved strong results in arm-centric manipulation, yet humanoid whole-body control (WBC) requires dynamic balance and tightly coupled full-body coordination. Existing hierarchical humanoid VLAs typically decouple motion generation from physical execution, leaving tracking and balance errors unable to directly optimize the VLA generator.
title: DiffGR00T: Execution-Aware Differentiable Training for Humanoid Whole-Body Vision-Language-Action Models

summary: Robot demonstrations provide more than actions to imitate: they reveal how actions change the world and how those changes contribute to task success. Recent world-action models (WAMs) extend vision-language-action (VLA) models with the first signal by jointly predicting actions and future observations, yet this predictive ability serves only as an auxiliary loss for policy learning.
title: DexWAC: A Unified World-Actor-Critic Model for Dexterous Robot Manipulation

summary: We were surprised to find that leading end-to-end driving models across major paradigms, despite scoring close to human drivers on NAVSIM, cannot reliably make a simple 90-degree turn in photorealistic closed-loop simulators. To investigate why, we build LaWanle, a benchmark of turns drawn from three such simulators.
title: LaWanle: Why Can't Leading Driving Models Make a Simple Turn?

summary: Complex cooperative tasks require coordinated multi-agent behavior. Offline generative policies learn expressive cooperative behaviors from trajectories but remain limited by fixed datasets. Online reinforcement learning can improve them through environment interaction. However, fine-tuning flow policies is difficult because action likelihoods are hard to compute.
title: TeamFlowRL: Online Policy Optimization of Decentralized Flow Policies for Multi-Agent Coordination

summary: According to an Axios report, many employees at OpenAI and Anthropic believe the companies' own unreleased frontier models can no longer be safely controlled. Both companies are internally debating whether to halt releases or even stop training altogether, while employee trust in leadership is eroding.
title: Dozens of insiders say OpenAI and Anthropic's unreleased models have outgrown their safety measures

summary: Where Winds Meet moves between distant mountain landscapes, bustling streets, and quiet moments with its characters. For Everstone Studio, bringing more.
title: Q&A: How Everstone Brings Where Winds Meet to Life with NVIDIA DLSS 5

summary: Large language models increasingly work as teams of agents, and a team is expected to solve problems beyond the reach of any single member. Most evaluations credit a team for outperforming a single agent, without accounting for the additional computation: a team may consume many times the tokens of one agent, and a plain vote over independent answers already explains most of the reported gain.
title: Recursive Collective Intelligence: Emergence on an Equal-Budget Ladder in Multi-Agent LLM Systems

summary: Mass Spec Skills empowers scientists using Google Antigravity to interpret tandem mass spectra.
title: From spectrum to structure: Identifying molecules with Mass Spec Skills for Google Antigravity

summary: GPT-6 models design protein structures and sequences using reasoning and code. Lab tests found evidence of binding across five targets.
title: GPT-6 models demonstrate intrinsic protein-design capabilities

summary: In a position paper, TU Darmstadt researchers call for redefining computer science as "Computer and AI Science." Their biggest concern is code generated on the fly at runtime, which they say upends today's safety and correctness guarantees.
title: German researchers call for computer science to reinvent itself as "Computer and AI Science"

summary: Amazon said AI agents recently found and exploited a zero-day vulnerability with no human oversight beyond a simple instruction to get root access on an East Asian university server. The agents were running on Cairn, an open source AI penetration-testing framework.
title: Amazon says hackers' AI agents found and exploited 0-day with little human input

summary: When people read prepared text aloud, AI can transcribe Swahili with remarkably few errors, and Swahili speech recognition looks close to solved.
title: Why Does Voice AI Still Struggle With Kenyans’ Speech?

summary: See how two amateur astronomers used Codex and Astra to find potential exoplanets in public data from NASA’s Kepler and TESS space telescopes.
title: Searching for distant planets with Astra

summary: Young people anxious about their futures say they’re increasingly frustrated with their pro-AI parents. They’re worried it’s going to make holiday gatherings very tense.
title: Don’t Bring Up AI if You Want to Enjoy Your Thanksgiving

summary: It will take mathematicians months to understand the “alien” 17-million-line solution an Anthropic researcher produced for the Riemann hypothesis.
title: AI Solved Math’s Most Famous Problem. Now Humans Are Struggling to Understand It

summary: LLM agents that drive stateful tools (e.g., interactive shells, design environments, simulation engines) frequently need to clone, backtrack, and parallelize live sessions to support exploration. However, cloning a live session today requires serializing the tool's in-memory state to disk or relaunching from scratch, both prohibitively slow for interactive exploration.
title: TimeTravelContainer: A Live Forking Sandbox for Stateful Agent Exploration

summary: Agreement among large language models is not physical evidence for mutating production infrastructure. Because generative models share pretraining priors and conform to peer rationales during deliberation, voting ensembles correlate errors instead of providing independent fault tolerance; yet attaching rigid deterministic checks to unconstrained agent outputs paralyzes incident remediation.
title: Provenance-Isolated Epistemic Quorums: Execution-Bound Evidence Certification and Plausible-World Safety Gating in Agentic Control Planes

summary: Real-world applications of modern AI systems require generalization to both unseen environments and novel human users. The field of zero-shot coordination (ZSC) has focused primarily on deploying AI to cooperate with novel partners in otherwise familiar environments.
title: Unifying Partner and Environment Diversity to Improve Human-AI Coordination

summary: Today we are announcing the general availability of the trusted access program API on Amazon Bedrock . The API gives you one place to discover, request, and enroll in model provider trusted access programs.
title: Introducing the Amazon Bedrock Trusted Access API with Anthropic’s Enterprise Frontier Safeguards and Enterprise Data Controls

summary: Zero-shot skeleton-based action recognition is evaluated almost exclusively on flat leaf labels, which leaves open whether a representation also grounds the broader concepts that contain an action in skeleton motion.
title: Don't Miss the Forest for the Trees: Zero-Shot Skeleton Action Recognition with Hyperbolic Hierarchical Semantic Prototypes

summary: Design Rule Checking (DRC) error fixing remains a time-consuming bottleneck in physical design, often requiring manual intervention despite advanced EDA optimizations. Existing LLM-agent approaches fall short due to redundant contextual shapes, limited spatial reasoning over raw coordinates, and inefficient flat layout representations.
title: AgentDRC: Multi-Agent Algorithms for Spatially-Aware Automated DRC Correction

summary: Subliminal learning refers to a surprising phenomenon in language models wherein a prompt given to one model (e.g., preference for cats) can be subliminally distilled to another model via training on data that is ostensibly meaningless (e.g., number sequences).
title: Subliminal Learning Crosses Modalities

summary: Robots must often keep working after the world changes, as when a block moves or the camera shifts while the robot still acts on what it saw before. Recent work showed that one change during a task lowers success for every policy tested, but did not separate the effect of its timing from the cost of the changed world, or measure what it costs afterwards.
title: CALVIN-MAX: When Does a Mid-Execution Change Hurt a Robot Policy?

summary: Behavior Foundation Models (BFMs) have emerged as a promising paradigm for general-purpose humanoid control through pretraining on large-scale behavioral data. However, their proficiency in whole-body coordination does not readily extend to scene interaction, which requires adapting motion to scene-dependent geometric constraints and contact dynamics.
title: Ada-BFM: Adapting Behavior Foundation Models for Humanoid Scene Interaction

summary: Fast generation on manifolds is important for scientific applications such as protein design, yet existing one-step generators often produce spurious samples in low-density gaps between data modes. Our analysis highlights the mismatch between uniform noise and concentrated data, motivating a statistical prior that captures the data's coarse structure.
title: Start Where the Data Are: Statistical Priors for One-Step Generation on Manifolds

summary: Joint-embedding predictive architectures learn by predicting features of masked regions from visible context. In chest computed tomography, the findings that decide a diagnosis, such as a small nodule, are often not predictable from the surrounding anatomy. A hidden finding is then best predicted toward normal anatomy, and the prediction loss stops rewarding the encoder for representing it.
title: JECT: Addressing the Context Shortcut in Joint-Embedding Predictive Learning for Chest CT

summary: Standard LLM personalization typically frames identity as a static retrieval task, overlooking the inherent incongruity of human personas, where stable traits coexist with atypical, context-specific stances.
title: Faithful Persona Steering under Incongruity via Dual-Stream Refinement

summary: Visual self-models learn from images how a robot moves under motor commands. Continuum robots need them even more, as they bend continuously without measured joint angles or fixed link geometry. Existing continuum self-models predict point clouds, image-space curves, or future images, but not the next 3D shape, appearance, and tip pose together from an observed body.
title: BendGS: Observation-Conditioned Gaussian Self-Modeling for Continuum Robots

summary: Reactive robotic manipulation is acutely sensitive to simultaneous sensing noise, measurement dropouts, joint execution errors, and contact parameter variations.
title: Co-DRIS: Physics-Informed Predictive Belief and Variable-Impedance Learning for Reactive Catching under Coupled Uncertainty

summary: Where a person looks indicates their focus of attention, and how their gaze shifts between targets reveals how that attention responds to a changing scene. Existing gaze target estimation methods largely operate frame by frame and do not model these shifts. Gaze shifts are often driven by dynamic changes in the scene, which is the kind of information world models are designed to encode.
title: Gaze World Model

summary: Actor-critic methods achieve high returns in robotic control, yet trained actors exhibit high-frequency action oscillations. Most smoothness methods constrain the actor, whereas PAVE regularizes the critic by separately penalizing action-gradient variation and encouraging negative action curvature.
title: POISE: Curvature-Aware Critic Regularization for Smooth Actor-Critic Control

summary: Pretrained antipodal grasping networks generalize well to canonical shapes but frequently fail zero-shot on novel objects with irregular mass distributions, thin rims, or unfamiliar handles. While episodic experience memory adapts a frozen base policy without retraining, naive retrieval suffers from visual appearance bias, negative transfer from overriding working base grasps, and degenerate closed-loop acquisition.
title: VG-GP: Uncertainty-Gated Visuo-Geometric Memory for Negative-Transfer-Resistant Grasp Adaptation

summary: World action models (WAMs) adapt pretrained video generators for robot control by jointly predicting future camera frames and actions, transferring physical priors learned from video into manipulation policies. However, generating future frames before every action makes test-time inference too slow for closed-loop control, while most existing policies remain restricted to short observation histories.
title: G0.7: Scaling Up a Fast World Action Model with Long Context

summary: The training of socially intelligent language models often relies on large language model (LLM) judges, which are expensive, noisy, and vulnerable to reward hacking. Multi-player social games offer a natural alternative: they require open-ended communication to coordinate with teammates and infer hidden roles, while their rules provide an objective outcome which can serve as a verifiable reward for training.
title: Exploring Multi-Player Social Games as Verifiable Training Grounds for Large Language Models

summary: Deep networks embed inputs in high-dimensional representations, but how much of this capacity actually drives behavior? We introduce a framework for identifying, at each layer, the subspace of the representation that is functionally sensitive to the task.
title: Compressible Representations: Functional Spines in Deep Neural Networks

summary: Released autonomous-driving models achieve strong benchmark performance, yet deploying them on a new real vehicle remains challenging. We study this deployment gap and find that released models can remain coupled to assumptions from their source sensing, data, and execution processes even after conventional adaptation.
title: Beyond the Benchmark: Localizing Released Autonomous Driving Models to Real Vehicles

summary: Reconstructing the 3D poses of hands and objects from a single image, together with the contact between them, is fundamental to understanding manipulation. To be practical, the reconstruction must generalize to unseen objects, and the contact must be localized precisely.
title: Generalizable Feed-Forward 3D Hand-Object Reconstruction with Coarse-to-Fine Contact Estimation

summary: Interactive video world models generate navigable worlds frame by frame, but a persistent world requires previously observed scenes to remain recoverable as users move away and return. Existing memory evaluations, however, often focus on seen-view revisits and full rollouts, leaving cross-view scene recovery underexplored while entangling memory with trajectory-following errors and accumulated generation degradation.
title: SceneMemBench: A Benchmark for Scene Memory in Interactive Video World Models

summary: LLM agents commonly use the full interaction history as a proxy for state, retaining all past observations and actions regardless of whether they remain relevant. We instead ask what information an agent actually needs to carry forward. We define agent state as a compact abstraction of interaction history that preserves the competence of a fixed reference agent, with the minimal such abstraction as the ideal.
title: Learning Compact State Abstractions for LLM Agents

summary: LLM agents increasingly collaborate in group chats while holding tool access to confidential records, which makes the shared chat an attack surface. It remains unclear whether several colluding attackers extract such information more effectively than one.
title: SwarmLeak: Does Coordination Improve Privacy Attacks on LLM Agents?

summary: We compare a MEGABYTE-style byte-patch Transformer with a 64-byte sliding local decoder (local64) to a matched byte-level 8k BPE decoder (BPE-8k) under identical raw bytes, document order, and approximately matched bytes per optimizer step: 350M parameters and 10 billion training bytes.
title: Byte Patches versus BPE at Matched Data: A Matched-Twin Comparison at 350M Parameters

summary: Bimanual dexterous manipulation relies on multimodal inputs that capture visual context and non-visual physical interaction cues for precise and coordinated control. To address the challenge of effectively integrating these modalities for policy learning, we propose HiMoDex, a two-stage framework centered on hierarchical multimodal world-state representations.
title: Many Senses, One World: Learning Hierarchical Multimodal World Representations for Bimanual Dexterous Manipulation

summary: Recent time-series foundation models (TSFMs) forecast a distribution over futures, and multimodal time-series (TS) forecasting further exploits other modalities to improve forecasting accuracy.
title: VISOR: A Vision-Language Selector for Multimodal Time-Series Forecasting

summary: The Navier-Stokes (NS) inpainting model of Bertalmío, Bertozzi and Sapiro is the only transport-type paradigm among PDE-based methods, yet it has never received a systematic higher-order extension. We show that the obvious fourth-order correction is ill-posed, and we construct the corrected, well-posed model.
title: A Well-Posed Fourth-Order Navier-Stokes Model for Image Inpainting: Theory, Order Selection, and Stripe Decomposition

summary: Sequential concept acquisition enables interpretable diagnosis from a compact set of human-understandable findings. Such explanations are useful only if clinicians can trust them, yet most existing methods treat predicted concepts as correct, so a correct diagnosis can rest on incorrectly predicted evidence.
title: ReCAP: Sequential Concept Acquisition with Guarantees under Imperfect Concept Predictors

summary: Adversarial perturbation defenses protect images from unauthorized edits by adding imperceptible noise. Yet none of these methods have been evaluated against nudification, despite AI-generated non-consensual intimate imagery (AIG-NCII) being among the most documented harms of generative AI.
title: BODYBENCH: Evaluating Adversarial Image Defenses Against AI Nudification Inpainting

summary: Semantic retrieval struggles with multi-hop question answering on both recall and precision: gold passages are buried among distractors that degrade the reader's answer, and retrieving them requires reasoning over the query rather than matching it. GraphRAG techniques expand semantic retrieval by connecting passages to graph nodes and performing one or more hops of expansion after initial retrieval.
title: SPARQL-Planned Single-Hop Traversal over a Live Knowledge Graph for Multi-Hop Question Answering

summary: Converting pretrained softmax Transformers to efficient attention often causes substantial performance degradation, while recovery typically requires costly fine-tuning. We propose ET (Efficient Transfer), a framework for high-fidelity attention conversion with minimal optimization cost.
title: ET: Efficient Transfer from Softmax to Hybrid Attention

summary: While text-driven body motion generation has matured, pure-hand synthesis remains bottlenecked by data. Existing datasets often treat hands as rigid end-effectors, lack fine-grained captions, or are too limited in scale to support robust generalization.
title: RoMo Hands: A Large Scale Richly Organized Text to Hand Motion Dataset

summary: As live video streams grow longer, repeatedly encoding and processing their full histories becomes increasingly costly. Answering questions as they arrive therefore calls for visual memory built in one pass before future questions are known. Existing methods mainly keep tokens that differ from earlier ones or match surrogate queries fixed in advance.
title: Dreamcatcher: Remembering What Surprises a World Model in Video Streams

summary: 3D foundation models (3DFMs) enable dense reconstruction in a feed-forward pass, yet their effective span is limited by cross-view attention. Local consistency has been expanded through geometric alignment of video chunks and recursive updates of an implicit memory, and large-scale scenes with pose graphs.
title: Xtream: An Explicit Metric State for Large-Scale Streaming Reconstruction

summary: The growing autonomy of AI agents in using external tools and making decisions has created an urgent need for comprehensive safety benchmarks.
title: TACT-Bench: Testing Adaptive Conversational Threats against Tool-Use Agents

summary: Harnesses for vision-language models (VLMs) have grown with the models' capabilities, notably for images far larger than those seen in training, where downscaling loses small details. Most of them wrap the VLM in a fixed procedure, such as a zoom tree, that decides in advance where it looks and how the evidence is combined.
title: RVLM-X: Towards a Universal VLM Harness
