summary: Joint attention precedes vocabulary acquisition. How can attending to the same object help two people with different sensory experiences come to use a shared word? In a free-energy principle account, marginalizing the common object induces a statistical dependence between private perceptual states.
title: From joint attention to shared symbols: A free-energy principle account

summary: Reinforcement learning policies are often trained with static domain randomization for real-world deployment. However, real-world environments often exhibit unmodeled dynamic variations, such as payload changes or friction shifts, that lie outside the randomization distribution, leading to performance degradation upon deployment.
title: Beyond Domain Randomization: Real-World Policy Adaptation in Learned Dynamics for Legged Robots

summary: In this expository paper, we explain how quality engineers can use large language models (LLMs) and vision-language models (VLMs) for structured data extraction. We introduce the relevant concepts, discuss structured extraction from a measurement-system perspective, and demonstrate its implementation in R and Python.
title: What Quality Engineers Need to Know About Generative AI: Structured Data Extraction

summary: Chinese military researchers fear that AI advances could give the US an edge in the nuclear balance of power. The article Chinese military fears AI could let the US find and destroy its nuclear missiles appeared first on The Decoder .
title: Chinese military fears AI could let the US find and destroy its nuclear missiles

summary: Enterprise customer experience company Sierra, co-founded by former Salesforce co-CEO Bret Taylor, said on Monday that it has raised $1.75 billion in a Series F round.
title: Sierra doubles valuation to $30B within six months as demand for AI in CX takes off

summary: Trallie is an open-source framework that leverages large language models (LLMs) to perform information extraction (IE) from natural language sources with or without user guidance. Unlike conventional approaches that rely on extensive labeled datasets or domain-specific training, Trallie enables the conversion of unstructured data into structured formats with minimal or no representative examples.
title: Trallie: from Free-Form Text to Structured Data with LLMs

summary: Reinforcement learning policies for robot manipulation degrade when the number of objects N in the scene grows beyond the training range. This is a covariate shift that also changes the dimension of the state. We propose WAVE (Warping Actions and Views of an Expert), which extends a pretrained single-object skill to many objects without updating its weights. WAVE has three parts.
title: Object Count Generalization Is an Interface Problem: Warping a Frozen Skill Instead of Retraining It

summary: Nvidia's board of directors has reinstated Jensen Huang as president, CEO, and board member, effective immediately. The article Nvidia tried life without Jensen Huang and it lasted about two weeks appeared first on The Decoder .
title: Nvidia tried life without Jensen Huang and it lasted about two weeks

coverage.title: Jensen Huang Is Back, and So Is Nvidia’s Stock

summary: The stunning reversal was supported by senior officials in the U.S. government.
title: Nvidia reverses course and brings Jensen Huang back as CEO

summary: Reference trajectories are widely used to evaluate odometry and simultaneous localization and mapping systems. However, local inconsistencies in benchmark reference poses can bias such evaluations. This paper presents a place-revisit consistency evaluation method for reference poses in mobile sensing datasets.
title: Place-Revisit Consistency Evaluation of Reference Poses

summary: Welcome to Import AI, a newsletter about AI research. Import AI runs on arXiv, cappuccinos, and feedback from readers.
title: Import AI 482: Huawei kernel benchmarks; airborne drone detection; and a national lab's AI science benchmark

summary: Multilingual search agents can access the global Web, yet may remain trapped in a language environment with insufficient evidence; we refer to this failure as a language information cocoon. However, existing search benchmarks largely operate within a single language, especially English, overlooking entity connections across multiple languages.
title: CocoonBench: Can Multilingual Search Agents Escape Language Information Cocoons?

summary: Meta's Chief AI Officer Alexandr Wang sees the recent AI-assisted proof sketch of the Riemann Hypothesis as a clear sign that superintelligence is right around the corner. The article Meta's Alexandr Wang warns the AI industry isn't ready for what's coming after Riemann breakthrough appeared first on The Decoder .
title: Meta's Alexandr Wang warns the AI industry isn't ready for what's coming after Riemann breakthrough

summary: We present a dataset and evaluation setup for a problem in creative machine translation: translating culturally loaded passages that carry much of a text's meaning and humor that may depend on subtle or implicit discourse. We study Soviet comedy quotations that function as memes in Russian-language communication.
title: Hard to Translate, Harder to Detect: Human Analysis Remains Essential in AI Meme Translation

summary: When RL learns from the reactions of many users, the policy usually cannot see what each user wants. We ask what it learns from users who privately want validation: to validate them alone (targeting), or to lower its bar for endorsing everyone (a threshold shift).
title: Lowering the Bar for Everyone: Hidden Validation-Seeking Goals in Empathetic RL

summary: US intelligence agencies tracked contacts between Alice Huang and China's Ministry of State Security for over a year, the New York Times reports. The surveillance ran parallel to her secret affair with then-Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang.
title: US spies tracked Nvidia scandal figure's ties to Chinese intelligence for over a year

summary: Speech synthesized by text-to-speech engines is a low-cost substitute for recorded test sets in automatic speech recognition, yet an off-the-shelf synthetic test set is worth only a few dozen real recordings for estimating the real error rate of a recognizer. This paper examines which properties of real recordings are missing from synthetic speech and how much of the gap can be closed.
title: Synthetic Twins: Closing the Gap Between TTS Test Sets and Real Recordings in Turkish ASR Evaluation

summary: In-context learning (ICL) enables language models to adapt to new tasks from demonstrations, but repeatedly including multiple examples increases context length and inference cost. Many existing implicit ICL methods encode demonstrations as fixed vectors, limiting adaptation of the intervention to individual queries and token positions.
title: Learn the Effects, Not the Examples: Implicit ICL via Attention Patching

summary: Medical post-training raises benchmark accuracy, but accuracy does not show which internal components a model's decisions depend on, or whether components that support one benchmark also support another. We apply the weight-space intervention paradigm of ROME and MEMIT at the granularity of one MLP down-projection column.
title: Empirical Margin Sensitivity: An Interventional Neuron-Level Probe of Post-Trained Medical LLMs

summary: Brain-computer interface company Paradromics is using Nvidia’s computing hardware and software to process brain data.
title: Nvidia Is Powering Brain-Computer Interfaces Now

summary: Software engineering (SE) agents can complete diverse engineering tasks by interacting with the development environment via tools that access files, run commands, and download resources. Unfortunately, the same ability that makes SE agents useful also makes them prone to performing unintended malicious actions through prompt injections, malicious tools, or supply-chain attacks.
title: AgentBouncer: Defending Software Engineering Agents via Dynamic System-Call Mediation

summary: OpenAI's GPT-6.2 Astra independently produced a machine-verifiable Lean proof of Smoktunowicz's gap theorem, the first of its kind according to Vals AI. The model chose its own approach because key foundations were missing from Mathlib. On Autoform-Hard, Astra now leads the leaderboard with 49 of 56 tasks solved.
title: GPT-6.2 Astra solved a math theorem no other AI could crack, then invented its own proof strategy

authors: Sandra Upson, Steven Levy, Lauren Goode

summary: Experts agree that AI, in one way or another, poses real danger. Will the industry do anything about it? Join our livestream on December 2 to hear your questions answered.
title: Submit Your Questions: Will Anyone Keep You Safe From AI?

summary: Buying a new computer in the last few years has meant wading through all manner of AI branding nonsense . Most of the AI pitches for laptops are little more than marketing hype, but the launch of Nvidia RTX Spark could bring a meaningful improvement in AI capabilities to the device you use every day.
title: Review: The Asus ProArt P16 offers a glimpse of a future powered by local AI

title: Meta Muse can do your Black Friday shopping at Walmart

summary: AI now sits on both sides of the security fight, and the vocabulary has changed with it. IBM’s 2026 Cost of a Data Breach Report found that 1 in 4 malicious breaches were AI-enabled, up 56% year over year. Those breaches cost an average of $6 million, about $1 million above the $4.99 million global [. ].
title: 27 Cybersecurity Terms to Prepare You for the Age of AI

summary: Architect Labs has introduced Frostbite , an AI-designed CPU with a new instruction set built around interaction nets. The company states that its AI agents designed Frostbite from interaction net theory down to final GDS. In pre-silicon tests, it reports 4.59x the performance per watt of a modern in-order CPU core.
title: Architect Labs Unveils Frostbite, an Interaction Net CPU Designed by AI

summary: The last thing you should ever read—and the last thing I may ever write—about the craft of coding.
title: Goodbye, World: The End of Programmers

summary: Meta has published a detailed report on TLX (Triton Low-Level Extensions) . It is the GPU compiler extension behind Meta’s production ML kernels. Meta TLX is a Triton extension that exposes warp groups, barriers, TMA and clusters to Python kernels.
title: Meta TLX Brings Warp-Group GPU Control to Triton on Hopper, Blackwell, AMD

summary: Watch OpenAI’s Stacey Wang and Craig Bruney, Mary O’Carroll of LECG, and Cooley’s Richard Segal explore how AI can help in-house legal teams connect business context, build reusable workflows and get more from outside counsel.
title: Connected intelligence for in-house legal

summary: Richpanel uses GPT-6 Astra and GPT-6.1 Sol to equip its AI support agents with tools and procedures, and GPT-6 Luna for their conversations.
title: Richpanel helps companies automate 50% of support in 30 days

summary: Autonomous AI agents that coordinate and collaborate among each other have become pervasive across domains ranging from scientific research to finance and engineering. The opportunity to share messages and build upon each other's work also creates the potential for misaligned behaviors to spread across AI agents.
title: Causal Evidence for the Emergence and Spread of Reward Hacking in AI Agent Swarms

summary: A new technique developed by MIT researchers could help engineers use artificial intelligence to streamline the design and innovation of analog integrated circuits, semiconductor chips that perform vital functions like communication and power management in electronic devices.
title: AI-driven technique could help engineers design analog chips faster and with less expense

summary: With the growing demand for ESG disclosure and evaluation, constructing high-quality datasets for automatically extracting ESG-related information from large-scale documents has become essential. However, ESG annotation remains challenging due to strong context dependence, ambiguous label boundaries, and the need for domain expertise, resulting in high annotation cost and limited scalability.
title: TRAE: Trustworthy Automated ESG Annotation via Multi-Agent Consensus and Confidence Assessment

summary: Three significant backers share what gave them conviction to bet billions on Anthropic.
title: How Notable Capital, GIC, and Baillie Gifford bet big on Anthropic before its IPO

summary: Release: datasette-charts 0.1a0 . I've been thinking about this problem for over a year now, but on Sunday I finally fired up Claude Fable 5.2 to build an initial prototype. The prototype went so well that this is now a full plugin. You can try it out in Datasette Lite here . It looks like this:.
title: datasette-charts 0.1a0

summary: A streaming video system must decide in a single pass what evidence to retain under bounded frame storage, before it knows which details a future question will require. Recent recursive self-improvement methods automate the design of the harness that stores and retrieves this evidence.
title: MORSE: Optimizing Streaming Memory Design via Open-World Auto-Research

summary: LLMs typically solve complex tasks with chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning, which is also the main tool for monitoring them for misaligned behavior. However, standard transformers can also solve tasks with complete latent reasoning (CLR), carrying out the whole task internally and outputting only the final answer.
title: Can Latent Reasoning Drive LLM Outputs Without a Trace?

summary: Robot leading requires executing a route while continuously adapting to a designated follower. Existing robot-leading systems often mediate follower understanding and physical route execution through explicit states, planners, or modular interfaces; directly learning this coupling through end-to-end trajectory prediction can instead entangle route execution with follower response.
title: LeadVLA: Learning Follower-Aware Route Execution for Robot Leading

summary: Feedback tools and research on learner writing need transcriptions of handwritten essays that keep exactly what the student wrote: misspellings, line breaks, struck-through words and insertions. Vision-language models (VLMs) read handwriting well, but they also tend to rewrite it into correct language.
title: Escriba-OCR: A 1B Vision-Language Model for Error-Preserving Transcription of Handwritten Portuguese Essays

summary: Learned image captioning metrics are trained and tested on human judgments, so their reported correlation is a claim about generalization. We audit this claim for the three most recent collections of such judgments, Polaris, Nebula, and Spica, matching images at the pixel level.
title: Do learned image captioning metrics generalize? Auditing duplicated samples in human-judgment benchmarks

summary: Large and diverse video sources, such as egocentric human video and heterogeneous robot recordings, carry rich dynamics but come either without actions or without a shared action space. Latent action models (LAMs) can recover these dynamics, but they train their inverse- and forward-dynamics models (IDM, FDM) from scratch, trading off pixel reconstruction against latent capacity and accuracy.
title: World Models as Native Latent Action Models

summary: Animating arbitrary 3D assets from instructions requires both structural inference and motion control, yet existing motion benchmarks mostly cover conventional human or animal skeletons with simple instructions.
title: 3AGameFactory-Motion: Agentic Rigging and Reliable Complex Motion Generation for Diverse 3D Assets

summary: Long-horizon embodied tasks involve physical dependencies that may only become clear through interaction. As task understanding deepens, past trials can reveal new information for adaptation and transfer.
title: ReWeave: Emergent Physical Task Topologies for Embodied Harness Optimization and Cross-Task Meta-Distillation

summary: Learning robot manipulation from egocentric human videos requires accurate metric 3D hand motion. Recent methods leverage pretrained video diffusion model (VDM) priors to recover occluded hands directly from full-frame videos, but their appearance-based depth regression generalizes poorly to unseen cameras.
title: ViDiHand2: Unifying Video Diffusion Priors and Hand Geometry for 3D Hand Motion Reconstruction in the Wild

summary: Reinforcement learning (RL) trains coding agents on software tasks whose hidden tests decide the reward, yet task collections check these tests only against the reference fix. We ask what makes a task good training data, focusing on the correctness of its reward labels. We audit SWE-Gym with two LLM families, and a suspected error counts only if execution reproduces it.
title: What Makes Good Data for Training Coding Agents? A Systematic Study on SWE-Gym

summary: Text-to-image models can learn from their own mistakes by distilling a self-teacher conditioned on a vision-language critic's revised prompt. However, such self-teachers barely improve alignment, and both they and their hindsight-contrast variants absorb the critic's unintended additions to the scene, such as lighting or scenery.
title: Distill the Correction, Not the Rewrite: Hindsight Twins for Self-Improving Text-to-Image Models

summary: Dense-embedding retrievers can fail adversarially: when a query is answered by a document A and reversed by a near-copy B that differs from A by a small meaning-changing edit (a "trap"), raw cosine over E5-Large-v2 places B in the top-10 for 82-100% of queries at a pool of 5,000. We study two things.
title: Small Learned Projections for Semantic-Reversal-Aware Retrieval with Spectral Acceleration: A Four-Domain Empirical Study

summary: The physical world is open-ended, dynamic, and partially observable. While foundation models have advanced embodied intelligence, standalone models struggle with long-horizon execution, and simply integrating models with agents may lead to inconsistencies between planning and physical control. To support reliable and adaptive behaviors in the physical world, we introduce Innata-0, a native embodied world system.
title: Innata-0: A Native Embodied World System with Model-Agent Co-Design

summary: Generative Pre-Training (GPT) represents a profound milestone in natural language processing, serving as the foundation for most of today's state-of-the-art large language models.
title: WorldLatent: A Unified 4D Latent Space for World Perception and Generation

summary: Cheap language-model raters grade chain-of-thought reasoning at scale, yet systematic step-rating errors can skew reasoning audits and solution rankings. We introduce LUCID (Loop for Unbiased Calibration via Inference-time Diagnosis), which pairs prompt self-correction with Design-based Supervised Learning (DSL).
title: LUCID: Statistically Grounded Self-Correction for LLM Reasoning Evaluation

summary: Effective real-time, full-duplex multimodal interaction requires systems to understand not only what users say, but also the communicative needs conveyed through prosody, facial expressions, gestures, and context, and to generate audiovisual responses that appropriately address those needs.
title: UUBench: Understanding the Unspoken toward Full-Duplex Multimodal Interaction

summary: Long-horizon, real-time controllable motion generation is essential for interactive animation and humanoid robotics, where an agent must respond to changing instructions and spatial goals while moving. Existing autoregressive diffusion methods generate motion incrementally, but bounded attention caches limit access to distant history, while repeated denoising introduces substantial inference overhead.
title: Motion Mamba 2.0: Autoregressive Diffusion Mamba for Long-Horizon Humanoid Control

summary: Foundation models can reason about complex physical tasks, yet translating this intelligence into reliable robot execution remains challenging. We argue that a critical, often overlooked factor is the robot-use interface (RUI), which determines how agents express and execute physical actions.
title: RUIBench: What Makes a Good Robot-Use Interface?

summary: AI agents accumulate conversations, images, and documents through long-term interactions with users. Answering later questions often requires connecting evidence across these records, yet the resulting understanding is rarely retained, allowing mistakes to recur on related questions.
title: MMMem: Self-Improving Agents with Task-Aware Multimodal Experience Consolidation

summary: Human demonstrations provide a rich source of bimanual dexterous skills, yet transferring them to robot hands remains challenging. Existing methods primarily optimize object trajectory tracking, often overlooking how human hands interact with the object. Even with accurate tracking, robots may contact incorrect object parts or slide their fingers, resulting in unstable manipulation.
title: DexDuet: Learning Contact-Preserving Bimanual Dexterity from Human Demonstrations

summary: 4D occupancy forecasting predicts the 3D semantic occupancy of a driving scene seconds ahead. Over a few seconds, the scene changes little while the vehicle moves, so most of the space ahead has already been seen.
title: Write, Evolve, Read: Streaming Cameras into a Persistent World State for 4D Occupancy Forecasting

summary: We interviewed people at 58 companies that use Claude about how AI is changing their work. They described few layoffs but reduced hiring, and said the most valuable uses of AI often involved reorganizing roles and workplaces around it.
title: Working with AI

summary: AI systems can now operate Blender, follow instructions in complex video games, and manipulate objects with robot arms. What range of physical goals can today's AI systems achieve autonomously? Answering this question requires testing systems on tasks that demand different combinations of perception, memory, planning, and action.
title: WorldLeague: Benchmarking Physical Agency

summary: Computer-use agents (CUAs) are rapidly improving, yet their evaluation remains largely static. Existing benchmarks provide a strong foundation, but fixed difficulty ceilings, limited feature coverage, and coarse aggregate scores progressively weaken their discriminative and diagnostic value.
title: Self-Evolving Evaluation Environments for Computer-Use Agents

summary: Reinforcement learning (RL) has become an important component in large language models (LLMs). However, existing RL approaches focus on final outputs or textual solution trajectories, leading to coarse-grained rewards and unreliable reasoning. Such paradigms focus mainly on what the model outputs while overlooking how the model internally reasons.
title: From Rewarding What Models Say to How They Think: Attention Process Reward Model for LLM Reinforcement Learning

summary: AI evaluations help shape which systems people build, adopt, and trust. An evaluation gives a system tasks, checks its answers or actions, and produces a score.
title: How to build and maintain an agentic evaluation

summary: Visual creation demands expressive imagery together with precise control over text, layout, and structure. We introduce Nemotron-Labs-VisualCreation, an agentic framework that connects these capabilities through Pixel as Code. Raster images are represented by learned discrete visual tokens, while structured artifacts use explicit programs.
title: Nemotron-Labs-VisualCreation: Pixel as Code for Agentic Visual Creation

summary: Interactive intelligence requires agents to act on observations and adapt to the consequences of actions. Studying these abilities calls for diverse, challenging tasks under controlled conditions. We introduce GameDojo, a controllable interactive gameplay benchmark of 120 boss encounters across 20 games for evaluating model capabilities, learning algorithms, and agent harnesses.
title: GameDojo: Benchmarking Real-Time Interactive Agents in Video Games

summary: Proprietary news archives assign stories to firms, so reproducing a financial study often requires access to both the articles and the vendor's assignments. CCFinance lets researchers reconstruct firm coverage under different selection rules by recording which version of a story was captured, which issuers it names and how often each appears.
title: CCFinance: Reconstructing Financial News Samples from Web Archives

summary: Depth-recurrent (Looped) models raise effective depth by applying a shared stack of blocks several times. Scaling them usually requires pipeline parallelism, but commonly used interleaved 1F1B is drawn for an acyclic stage graph in which each micro-batch enters each stage once.
title: A Pipeline-Parallel System for Depth-Recurrent Models

summary: Robot policies must adapt to the speed of moving objects, yet existing benchmarks rarely measure this ability across diverse tasks and speeds. We introduce SWEEP-Bench, a simulation benchmark with 80 conveyor-belt manipulation tasks spanning 16 skill categories, each evaluated at 13 belt speeds (0.10-0.40 m/s). Objects are transported through physical contact with a visibly moving belt.
title: SWEEP-Bench: Do Embodied Policies Act on the Speed They See?

summary: We present OWE-Bench (OpenWorldEngineer-Bench), a benchmark of 26 long-horizon engineering tasks written by domain experts in software engineering, physical engineering, machine learning, and scientific computing. Tasks range from optimizing kernels and designing an aircraft, to identifying the faults responsible for an earthquake.
title: OWE-Bench: A long-horizon benchmark for measuring real-world engineering

summary: Generating 3D indoor scenes requires a representation that captures object semantics, instance identity, height structure, and orientation while respecting room geometry.
title: RoomTokens: Masked Diffusion over Structured Tokens for Indoor Scene Synthesis

summary: Pretrained vision is a common start for robot learning, but most comparisons still score one pooled vector from a third-person image. Bimanual policies instead read dense patch tokens from cameras on the robot. We introduce HIVE-Bench: one shared flow-matching policy reads 20 encoders from seven families on 24 egocentric bimanual tasks, across adaptation, task sharing, and sweeps of data, model size, and layer.
title: HIVE-Bench: Evaluating Patch-Level Visual Representations for Egocentric Robot Manipulation

summary: Frontier multimodal models exhibit extraordinary generalization in generating robot actions from observations and instructions, enabling a new paradigm in which they serve directly as policies within closed-loop robotic harnesses. However, the design principles of such harnesses, and the capabilities underlying their strong performance, remain unclear.
title: Embo-Harness: Towards Understanding Frontier-Model-as-Policy Harness

summary: Skill internalization offers a way for agents to learn useful behaviors from skills and use them without explicit guidance in context at inference time. A common approach is to generate demonstration trajectories with the skill in context and then fine-tune the same model on its own trajectories with the skill removed.
title: Context-Grounded Skill Internalization for Vision-Language Agents

summary: Recent advances in video generation have made automated advertising production increasingly feasible. However, an effective advertisement must faithfully represent the product and communicate its selling points through compelling visual storytelling, which requires more than visual synthesis: it calls for deeper product understanding and strategic decisions about how to present product value.
title: AdProducer: Towards Agentic Advertising Video Generation

summary: Exploring a scene from as little as a single photo requires generating a long, camera-controlled walkthrough that extends far beyond what was captured, yet remains consistent upon return. Memory-based video generation methods preserve what they have already seen, but have no anchor beyond it, where the camera drifts from its path and a text prompt can name objects but not place them.
title: Lyris: Layout-Guided Long Video Generation with Persistent 3D Memory

summary: We present WeMM-Ecom, a family of multimodal large language models that deliver frontier e-commerce capabilities while achieving state-of-the-art general-purpose performance at their respective scales. The family spans five sizes, from a 0.8B dense model to a 35B mixture-of-experts model with 3B active parameters.
title: WeMM-Ecom: Advancing Multimodal Content Understanding for WeChat E-Commerce

summary: Recent multimodal search agents use reasoning, vision, and live web search across many turns to answer questions beyond parametric knowledge by orchestrating a small library of hand-crafted search and visual tools. However, the library is laborious to create and maintain, and frozen when new query types, evidence formats, and failure modes are encountered in the wild.
title: ToolSmith: An Automatic Tool-Generation Framework for Multimodal Search Agents

summary: Vision-language-action (VLA) models leverage pretrained vision-language representations for instruction-conditioned robot control, yet their understanding of task-relevant 3D relations and how these relations evolve during manipulation remains largely implicit.
title: WeaveVLA: 3D Relational Grounding for Vision-Language-Action Models

summary: GUI grounding requires precise clicks at low latency. Recent models such as GUI-Decisions and GUI-Swift predict coordinates in one forward pass using fixed global bins with local refinement. However, screenshot downsampling removes detail needed to locate small controls, while fixed bins cover larger pixel ranges at higher resolutions.
title: PixelOne: From Options to Pixels in a Single Forward for GUI Grounding

summary: We propose loom attention, which allows a Transformer to dynamically rewire its circuits at every token by interweaving a head's vertical attention over the outputs of earlier heads (to obtain its query, key and value) with its horizontal attention over tokens.
title: Rewirable Circuits in Transformers with Loom Attention

summary: Over the last week or so, we have seen a nationwide FAA ground stop, a multi-day Outlook outage that brought entire companies to a standstill, and a banking outage at JPMorgan Chase. But the consensus is that there are more to come.
title: We haven’t seen the last of the major tech outages

summary: These notes describe how generative AI is now used to solve and to check research-level mathematics, with a focus on agents and their harnesses. For the proving agents Rethlas, Danus, and Pharos and the verification agent OSVerify, we explain the design principles, compare each with its base model, present case studies, and show how to use and contribute to them.
title: Notes on Generative AI for Mathematical Research

summary: To establish a speed limit on AI development, you need to agree on how to measure speed.
title: OpenAI’s chief scientist has thoughts on how to limit AI development

summary: An AI agent can satisfy every individual safety check and still give rise to a population that violates a collective safety limit. This risk arises in open multi-agent systems, where agents copy themselves, modify their successors, and change system membership during a run. Selection then shifts the population toward traits outside the developers' optimization targets.
title: Evolutionary AI Control: Population-Level Safety Under Reproduction, Heredity, and Selection

summary: NVIDIA has released Alpamayo 2 Edge , a compact reasoning vision-language-action (VLA) model for autonomous driving. Alpamayo 2 Edge is a 2B-parameter model that plans trajectories and explains them inside the vehicle. It targets NVIDIA DRIVE AGX Thor , not a datacenter GPU.
title: NVIDIA Releases Alpamayo 2 Edge: A 2B Reasoning VLA for DRIVE Thor

summary: In his new book “Hyperscale,” journalist Paris Marx investigates the impact of data centers and generative AI, taking readers inside the data centers themselves and explaining how computing infrastructure that goes back decades recently became a political landmine.
title: Why data centers are at the center of the Big Tech backlash

summary: The Binding of Isaac: Repentance Plus has spent the last few days getting review-bombed on Steam after it was discovered that a particular segment of the game used AI music. Reddit user ShweetsStuff discovered the songs used during a Grand Theft Auto-themed section.
title: Binding of Isaac developer removes AI music from Repentance Plus

summary: As privately owned agents become increasingly capable, collaboration in open agent networks is limited by partial topology knowledge, ownership boundaries, and the risk of exposing or contaminating private context.
title: AEP:Towards Trustworthy Agent Communication, Networking, and Collaboration

summary: Multi-agent LLM evaluations and social simulations create many agents from one model and treat them as independent replicates, even after the agents interact. This assumption remains untested with matched controls. We introduce SocCogEval, a controlled-clone assay for Social Cognitive Transfer (SCT).
title: Social Interaction Breaks Replicate Independence in Controlled-Clone LLM Agents

summary: Coordinating large robot fleets, from warehouses to quadrotor swarms, requires collision-free trajectories that satisfy dynamic constraints and stay within speed and acceleration bounds. Existing kinodynamic multi-agent planners enforce these bounds during the search or through trajectory optimization after it, which limits fleet size and speed.
title: Real-Time Kinodynamic Multi-Agent Motion Planning

summary: A new real-world test puts AI coding agents in a simulated developer job with colleagues, project boards, and incomplete handoffs, where they have to keep developing software on their own and reliably close open tickets in a messy daily workflow.
title: AI coding agents ace isolated tests but complete fewer than one in ten tasks in a simulated workplace

summary: Perplexity is launching a Monitor API that searches the web on a schedule and alerts agents via webhook only when relevant changes occur. Its own decision model filters out unimportant results.
title: Perplexity's new Monitor API turns web search from a one-off query into a nonstop watchdog

summary: METR reports that leading AI models like Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra are improving rapidly at research tasks but getting harder to measure. Current data can't rule out a dangerous acceleration in AI development, the organization warns, though it also says common tests may overestimate what the models can actually do.
title: AI is getting better faster than experts can reliably test whether new systems are safe, METR warns

summary: This is The Stepback , a weekly newsletter breaking down one essential story from the tech world. For more on the vibe-hacking of everything, follow David Pierce . The Stepback arrives in our subscribers' inboxes on Sunday at 8AM ET. Opt in for The Stepback here . How it started.
title: The vibe-coding revolution is coming to all the gadgets

summary: Recent Multi-Agent Systems (MAS) increasingly use shared memory to store and reuse successful collaboration records, enabling teams to improve across tasks. However, this memory introduces a new attack surface for malicious insiders.
title: When Successful Collaboration Becomes an Attack Surface: Insider Memory Poisoning in Multi-Agent Systems

summary: Security researchers at Dragos used two million fake AI requests to uncover serious vulnerabilities in the AI supply chain, finding at least three compromised providers, hundreds of stolen AWS keys, and marketplace resellers who were simply reading customer requests.
title: Security researchers show how cheap AI inference providers steal keys and snoop on users

summary: The Lean and Mathlib community has officially confirmed Levent Alpöge's proof of the Riemann hypothesis as correct. Dozens of independent verifiers checked the 17 million lines of computer code.
title: Lean and Mathlib community officially confirms Levent Alpöge's proof of the Riemann hypothesis is correct

summary: A personal AI agent runs continuously, keeps memory across sessions, and acts inside your apps. You talk to it in a chat app, by email or by voice. It keeps working after you close the window. The category started small. OpenClaw began in November 2025 as Clawdbot, a weekend project by Peter Steinberger.
title: Best Personal AI Agents in 2026: OpenClaw, Hermes Agent, Gemini Spark and More, Compared on Memory, Security and Cost

summary: OpenAI's GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol give much shorter, more direct answers than their predecessors, but they are also less willing to admit uncertainty. Anthropic's Claude models score well ahead on transparency.
title: GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol get to the point faster but score lower on transparency than Claude

summary: Experimental platforms that enable multiple participants to engage in spoken dialogue and perform physical actions concurrently in a shared environment are important for studying cooperation between humans and embodied AI agents. In this paper, we propose EMIP (Embodied Multi-Party Interaction Platform), a virtual environment platform built on Minecraft.
title: EMIP: Embodied Multi-Party Interaction Platform

summary: Adding a singing voice to an existing piano recording requires decisions about melody, syllable placement, pronunciation, timing, and vocal register. ARRANGE organizes this work as a sequence of agent skills with readable intermediate artifacts and composer approval checkpoints.
title: ARRANGE: Agentic Skills for Layering Vocals

summary: Marketers have never had more data to act on. Take an apparel brand that advertises on Meta technologies: campaign results live in Meta Ads Manager, briefs and creative assets in shared storage, and inventory, customer lifetime value, and in-store purchases in a data lake.
title: Meta ads is now available in AWS Quick

summary: Researchers from Columbia University and CertiK have introduced TensorLean , a framework for formal verification of GPU kernels at the PTX level. TensorLean is a Lean-based verifier that proves compiled kernels match a tensor-level math spec.
title: A Team of Researchers from Columbia and CertiK Introduce TensorLean for Formal Verification of GPU Kernels

summary: Cache-sharing multi-agent systems can retain every evidence token's representation while preventing cross-worker access during encoding. We test whether this coverage recovers joint-encoding quality using attention masks over two logical workers in frozen Qwen3-4B, Qwen3-8B, and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct models. Tokens, positions, and answer-time access remain fixed within comparisons.
title: Beyond Evidence Coverage: Encoding-Time Access in Multi-Agent Systems

summary: Animal re-identification (Re-ID) must distinguish individuals across species and capture conditions. We introduce ApexID, a hierarchical SphereFace2-based loss that integrates global identity discrimination with balanced animal-category supervision.
title: ApexID: Hierarchical Learning for Multi-Species Animal Re-Identification

summary: How perplexity measures progress in AI models, and why it could help developers establish a shared approach to evaluating emerging capabilities.
title: Perplexity and Intelligence

summary: Efficient AI computation depends on hardware that evolves over time, shifting the strategies needed to implement performant code. For CPU kernels, a key evolving factor is the set of available architectural extensions, which expose specialized hardware instructions that change the techniques used to optimize kernels.
title: KernelShift: Benchmarking Kernel Optimization Across Evolving Hardware

summary: Visual agents navigate whole-slide images through magnified observations associated with claimed locations. However, a visually plausible observation does not necessarily originate from its claimed location, particularly across magnifications and in regions with similar tissue structures.
title: Can an Agent Trust Its Own Zoom? Cross-Magnification Provenance Verification for Whole-Slide Images

summary: Most LLM agent frameworks build a crew that runs a task and exits. Physical environments (e.g., homes, labs, factory floors) need agents that stay up for months, survive their own bugs, and run on whatever hardware is already next to the sensors.
title: Wactorz: Self-Writing LLM Agents That Discover, Repair, and Migrate at the Edge

summary: Physical counterfactual video editing turns a source video and a language-specified physical edit at a given execution frame into a counterfactual video that shows how the scene would evolve after the edit.
title: PhyCoVE: Benchmarking Physical Counterfactual Video Editing across Diverse Material Dynamics

summary: Recently, GPT-6 Astra demonstrates strong generalization in robot control, yet limited disclosure of its training leaves open how such capabilities can be reproduced.
title: A Glimpse of Training VLMs as Foundation Models for Robotic Manipulation

summary: Vision-language models have become a new kind of describer, writing about almost anything people see, and their descriptions now shape how cultures are known by people and by other models. Descriptions of cultures tend to turn particular things into types, and what a description loses shows what its describer lacks.
title: Polytropos: What Do Vision-Language Model Descriptions Make of a Cultural Object?

summary: AI-driven game development holds the potential to transform diverse human inspirations into interactive experiences. However, existing systems and benchmarks primarily focus on explicit development specifications, with limited support for adapting multimodal references and evaluating actual gameplay experiences.
title: GameAnything: From Any Inspirations to Playable Game Worlds

summary: Representation alignment markedly accelerates diffusion training, but one-step generators raise a question that diffusion does not: which training path should receive the loss? A one-step generator sees two kinds of inputs. Corrupted real images come with their clean counterpart, which provides an instance-paired target.
title: Align the Pair, Not the Sample: Representation Alignment for Faster and Better One-Step Generato

summary: Understanding a scene requires both geometry and semantics: geometry recovers its spatial structure, and semantics separates it into objects. Current models obtain the two from separate networks or separate passes. We present PINE, a one-step Omni Diffusion Transformer that predicts the point map, the surface normals, and the instance map of an image in one forward pass.
title: PINE: Point, Instance and Normal Estimation in One-Step Diffusion Model

summary: Current MLLM methods largely focus on whether models attend to the right visual regions, implicitly treating spatial attention map as the primary key of effective visual perception. To examine this assumption, we introduce a medical VQA dataset with paired non-contrast (NC) and contrast-enhanced (CE) images that share corresponding anatomy while providing different cues.
title: Beyond Attention Maps: Understanding and Improving Medical MLLMs via Visual Values

summary: Touchard and the author asked whether every valued hyperfield, in Krasner's sense with the norm axiom, is of the form H_ρ(K): a valued field K read up to relative error ρ. The question turns on the norm axiom. If a valued hyperfield is a quotient K^times/Tcup{0} of a field, the norm axiom forces T=1+m_ρ for a valuation on K.
title: The norm axiom and factor hyperfields

summary: Motivated by discussions with an electronics contract manufacturer about decision support, Factory-simulator provides a deterministic manufacturing environment for controlled research on the business performance of large language model-based multi-agent systems (LLM-MAS). Equal delivery performance can arise from decisions with different financial consequences, complicating evaluation through delivery metrics alone.
title: Factory-simulator: A process-oriented environment for evaluating manufacturing decisions against optimisation-based references

summary: Large language model (LLM)-based agents are increasingly deployed in settings where they must collaborate to make joint decisions. We investigate how this collaboration unfolds under risk, asking whether agents adjust their choices to accommodate their partners, how they assign responsibility for shared outcomes, and whether responsibility attribution shapes subsequent adjustment.
title: Do LLM Agents Compromise Like Humans? Risk and Responsibility in Dyadic Decision-Making

summary: Signal is limiting users' ability to take screenshots in both its Android and iOS apps.
title: Signal restricts mobile screenshots as it confronts ‘existential threat’ of AI surveillance

summary: We got two very different pictures of Nvidia — the company’s latest earnings report vs. the tech executives loudly calling for Jensen Huang’s return.
title: A tale of two Nvidias

summary: One of the items on the agenda for UN diplomats meeting in Geneva this week was working towards rules regarding the use of autonomous weapons, or so-called "killer robots." Eventually, representatives left the meetings agreeing to "start discussing options" after a largely fruitless week of negotiations.
title: The UN fails to agree on rules regulating ‘killer robots’

summary: We created a list of the most notable AI agents that can live in your text messages, from general assistants to agents designed for families, travel, and work.
title: Here are the top AI agents that can live in your text messages

summary: Nvidia researchers argue that language models often don't need their full context windows—which are slow, expensive, and prone to errors—and propose an alternative. In tests, periodic summaries and targeted keyword search usually matched full-context results at a fraction of the cost.
title: Nvidia researchers argue huge AI context windows are a dead end

summary: A Buddhist monastery in Vermont called Maple wants to establish itself as Silicon Valley's spiritual authority while creating its own AI god. According to a New Yorker report, leader Soryu Forall's group records every breath its members take to train an AI in his image.
title: Silicon Valley's growing obsession with AI doomsday is turning parts of the tech industry toward cult-like devotion

summary: An actor has licensed his face to a microdrama startup — in a trend that's already popular in China. Experts question the long-term consequences if this becomes a trend in Hollywood, too.
title: Is selling an AI version of your face to this microdrama startup the future of Hollywood?

summary: Today, I’m talking with Hayden Field, The Verge ’s senior AI reporter, about the Anthropic IPO for the third and final episode in our series about AI in real life. The AI lab behind Claude went public on the Nasdaq last Thursday.
title: Can Anthropic afford to put safety first?

summary: Chess.com is ready to go a lot bigger than chess. After launching Gambit, a gambling-free poker site, earlier this year, the company is now adding 10 more games: backgammon, checkers, go, hearts, mahjong, shogi, sudoku, solitaire, xiangqi, and a Scrabble alternative called word.
title: Chess.com’s next move is a new hub for classic games, from mahjong to sudoku

summary: OpenAI has released new prompt templates for GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol meant to fix common model behaviors such as overly brief answers, unnecessary follow-up questions, and excessive testing when coding.
title: OpenAI shares new prompting tips for GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol to fix brief answers and unnecessary questions

summary: AI is forcing companies to patch their systems faster as attackers race to exploit newly discovered vulnerabilities. Welcome to internet outage hell.
title: The Outages Are Just Getting Started

summary: Thinking Machines Lab has released Inkling 2 Mini , an open-weight looped transformer with 26.4B total parameters. The model reuses its middle layers 3 times per token instead of adding more weights. That keeps the checkpoint near 20GB, small enough for a 32GB Mac or 1 NVIDIA DGX Spark.
title: Meet Thinking Machines Inkling 2 Mini: 26B Looped MoE Runs on a 32GB Mac

summary: Water governance conflicts stem not only from material scarcity, but from power asymmetries, institutional distrust, and the discursive frameworks through which actors assign meaning to water, infrastructure, and legitimate authority.
title: Who Speaks for the Water? Simulating Discursive Closure and Power Asymmetries in Hydrosocial Governance

summary: OpenAI has made GPT-Live-1.1 available in its API under the model ID gpt-live-1.1 . The GPT-Live-1.1 voice model is a full-duplex model for multilingual conversations. It can listen while it speaks.
title: OpenAI Ships GPT-Live-1.1 for Voice Agents, Cuts Idle Cost to $0.02/Min

summary: Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge says he used Claude to prove the Riemann hypothesis, math's most famous open problem for 167 years, with a proof formalized in Lean that spans over 250,000 pages.
title: Hours after Anthropic claims a Claude proof of the Riemann hypothesis, Stanford releases an all-human competing draft

summary: Thinking Machines has released Inkling 2 Mini, an open looped transformer that runs 12 of its 24 layers three times per token. This lets the model reason internally for longer without generating extra text. On Artificial Analysis's Intelligence Index, it ties with Qwen3.8 27B at roughly six times lower cost.
title: New open model Inkling 2 Mini thinks in loops to solve problems with fewer words and still runs on a laptop

summary: The Nasdaq 100 has slipped into a bear market after its worst weekly loss since the Covid-19 crisis. Nvidia plunged 14 percent as the SEC reviews its accounting, and Anthropic lost nearly all of its gains a day after its record IPO.
title: US technology stocks suffer their worst weekly loss since the pandemic as AI doubts pile up

summary: Bytedance and several US universities introduce Axion 1.0, an AI agent that rivals top commercial models from OpenAI and Anthropic on benchmarks after just three training phases. The researchers attribute the gains to carefully curated training data rather than ever more training steps.
title: Bytedance argues most AI training phases are unnecessary and backs it up with a competitive open model

summary: Multi-agent systems (MAS) usually coordinate heterogeneous models and tools to solve complex tasks, creating a growing need for reliable evaluation. However, a multi-agent workflow that is fastest in one serving environment can lose its advantage in another, even when its models, prompts, and task remain fixed. This makes a benchmark result conditional on how the workflow is executed.
title: The Evaluation Substrate Matters: Benchmarking Multi-Agent Serving Substrates

summary: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed in multi-agent systems for collective decision-making, such as multi-agent debate and consensus games, in which agents exchange messages and update their answers over multiple rounds and a resolution mechanism aggregates them into a final outcome. Most multi-agent LLM frameworks assume that every participant shares the system objective.
title: Persuasion from Within: Model-Based Insider Attacks in Multi-Agent LLM Debate and Consensus

summary: Top News. Anthropic’s record IPO lands well as the market around it falls into a correction. Sources:. Anthropic Debuts on Wall Street as a $2 Trillion Company . Nvidia, AMD, Micron Sink as Anthropic Closes 17% Above IPO Price . Anthropic shares fall 8% in premarket amid AI selloff as Nvidia, AMD shares drop .
title: Last Week in AI #348 - IPO->Correction, new GPTs and Geminis, Nvidia’s Fate

summary: In plant phenotyping, crop disease diagnosis has traditionally relied on expert assessment of visible symptoms and on models tailored to specific crops or diseases, and both are difficult to scale across field conditions.
title: MACE: Memory-Augmented Crop-Disease Evaluation of Frozen Vision-Language Models

summary: Baseten has released bison-1 and groundhog-1, 2 open-weight decision models built on Google’s Gemma 4 . Decision models do not write text. They return calibrated probabilities for yes/no, choice and score questions. The Baseten bison-1 decision model scores 76 on the Artificial Analysis Decision Index v2.1 .
title: Baseten Releases Bison-1 and Groundhog-1, Topping Decision Model Index

summary: Digital twins of agent networks need to flag unreliable forecasts and help users choose interventions. Both decisions depend on what happens over several steps: an error can spread through the network, and an edit whose trajectory is easy to predict may still yield a poor collective outcome.
title: Digital Twins for Multi-Agent Systems: When to Trust, What to Change

summary: Turn one person’s process into your team’s process, get more done in the Quick web app, and get more complete answers from agents working together. AWS Quick is the AI workspace built only for work. Today, we are releasing updates that help your team get more of its everyday work done:.
title: New in AWS Quick: More capable flows, an updated web experience, and agents that work together

summary: Customers increasingly self-host large language models (LLMs) on GPUs for control over cost, accuracy, and latency. However, self-hosting often means paying for redundant GPU work because small, isolated caches on each server can’t hold or share the growing context AI agents and chat applications resend.
title: Cut self-hosted LLM cost and latency with the distributed KV caching agent skill

summary: Vision Banana showed that a closed image generator, instruction-tuned to paint perception outputs as RGB images, becomes a generalist vision model. Does this carry over to open generators, and if not, what fails?
title: Open Vision Banana: An Open Framework for Unified Visual Perception through Generation in RGB Space

summary: Latent generative models typically rely on three separate networks: an encoder that tokenizes pixels, a generator that models the latent distribution, and a decoder that maps latents back to pixels. UNITE recently merged the first two into a single generative encoder trained in one stage, but its decoder remains a separate network.
title: Single-Transformer Latent Diffusion

summary: How much interaction experience is needed to distill a capable visual agent? We study learning from few tasks and recorded interaction histories. Our framework selects representative trajectories using skill-context coverage and ordered visual-decision similarity. On-policy distillation (OPD) learns through fresh interaction on selected tasks or fresh student responses at fixed histories.
title: Distilling Visual Agents from Limited Interaction Experience

summary: We present KMed-31B, a medical large language model post-trained from an open-weight model for on-premises deployment with limited hardware. Post-training a model for diverse medical tasks remains difficult, because improving one kind of task can lower performance on another. We attribute this to differences between tasks in expected output and available feedback.
title: KMed-31B Technical Report

summary: Computer-use agents (CUAs) built on vision-language models are increasingly entrusted with long-horizon tasks in live desktop, web, and mobile environments, where the screen keeps changing on its own.
title: Don't Sleep, Keep Watch: Proactive Perception for Computer-Use Agents

summary: Multimodal large language model (MLLM) agents have shown promising capabilities in task-oriented environments. However, they still struggle when queries are deferred until after exploration, requiring them to retain visual evidence before knowing which details will matter.
title: EvoViM: Recursively Self-Evolving Visual Agents for Exploration with Deferred Queries

summary: Asking a vision-language model (VLM) to think step by step often makes it worse at spatial questions, even though the image stays in context. We show that short chain-of-thought (CoT) turns a perception problem into a transcription problem.
title: Seeing Right, Writing Wrong: Where Short Chain-of-Thought Breaks Spatial VQA

summary: The decay exponent α in KV-cache eviction is an intrinsic property of the model: calibrated once on a single corpus, it transfers directly across domains.
title: NoHairCache: Calibrate-Once KV Cache Eviction with One Power-Law Exponent

summary: Spatial intelligence, the ability to reason about 3D space from visual observations, becomes essential as multimodal large language models (MLLMs) move into the physical world. Beyond perceiving each view, it rests on two cornerstones of human cognition: fusing multiple views into one coherent 3D scene and mentally transforming that scene to new viewpoints as reasoning unfolds.
title: S-Mind: Internalizing Multi-View Geometry for Spatial Intelligence

summary: Frontier language models can now read and edit the weights of a neural network much like code and thereby improve a small model, an approach known as Weight-Space Programming (WSP). We further explore applying WSP to a language model itself, which we call Self-WSP. Specifically, Qwen3.5-0.8B reads its own weights, proposes an edit, and then continues with the edited weights as both problem solver and editor.
title: Self-WSP: Can Language Models Improve Themselves Through Weight-Space Programming?

summary: Yossi Matias, Vice President, Google & GM, Google Research, Yaniv Leviathan, Google Fellow, Google Research, and Janet Zhou, Group Product Manager, Google Maps
title: How Google Duplex evolved to also call businesses for you in Gemini

summary: The blockbuster game makes no secret of its contempt for law enforcement. Real police departments using it to recruit new members and scold the public apparently didn’t get the memo.
title: Cops Are Pushing Extremely Corny ‘Grand Theft Auto 6’ Slop

summary: Keeping a shared Slurm cluster for foundation model development in sync entails keeping several separately maintained pieces of configuration matched to what’s running on the nodes.
title: Introducing managed cluster extensions for observability and user management in Amazon SageMaker HyperPod Slurm

summary: During a traffic peak, a request can sit in a queue on a saturated HyperPod cluster while GPUs on another cluster, sometimes in another AWS Region, sit idle. You have already paid for that capacity, but your requests can’t reach it.
title: Introducing Amazon SageMaker HyperPod Global Inference Gateway: One endpoint across Regions and clusters

summary: Persistent societies of large language model agents now make empirical claims about their own collective behaviour, yet the fate of such claims is rarely observable. We document one claim, from registration to death, on AITRAP, a multi-agent platform whose public, append-only ledger records every action.
title: How a Prediction Dies: A Challenge-Driven, Rule-Bound Self-Refutation in an LLM Agent Society

summary: Building hydrogen station networks, electric vehicle charging grids, or vaccine distribution systems requires coordinating two separately operated graphs, demand-side facilities and the supply-side networks they depend on, where each operator's payoff depends on the other's choices.
title: Coupling-Aware Reinforcement Learning for Co-Evolving Graph Games

summary: Meta’s executives are rethinking the company’s original goal of achieving net-zero emissions by 2030.
title: Meta reconsiders 2030 net-zero goal amid record emissions from AI data centers

authors: Lauren Hinkel | MIT-IBM Computing Research Lab

summary: Humans experience and interact with the world through sensory information. This could mean learning correspondences between the sound of bird chirps and the word “robin,” or being able to visually identify and follow your friend “Sarah” in a crowd of people.
title: Q&A: Enabling more human-like interactions and understanding in multimodal foundation models

summary: Researchers planted 2 million digital tripwires in requests sent through a sprawling network of AI services to find out what happened to sensitive information entrusted to them. What they discovered was an ecosystem that leaked highly sensitive data like a sieve.
title: Researcher plants 2m canaries into the AI supply chain. A privacy disaster surfaced

summary: This post is co-written with Tala Qraitem from AWS and Jörg Fischer from Standard Bank Group . Having an AI policy is one thing. Proving, one use case at a time, that AI systems follow it is another. Every new generative AI application adds one more system to prove.
title: How Standard Bank Group automates AI risk assessment for generative AI

summary: OpenAI has significantly strengthened safeguards against extracting internal reasoning from GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol. In adaptive red-teaming tests, the success rate for extracting protected reasoning fell from 54 percent to 0.2 percent.
title: OpenAI makes it much harder for attackers to extract how its latest AI models think

summary: Organizations across financial services, insurance, healthcare, and the public sector depend on document processing. They turn scanned files and paper forms into structured data their systems can act on. As generative AI has matured, these organizations want more than accurate text extraction.
title: Announcing Amazon Textract Insights: Verifiable generative AI for documents

authors: David Chandler | Laboratory for Information and Decision Systems

summary: Modeling of complex, chaotic processes such as weather and climate patterns and turbulent flows in aviation or in ocean currents has advanced enormously in recent years. However, such models are still prone to drift into physically impossible predictions over time.
title: New approach enables physically consistent AI models of chaotic systems

summary: Spotify founder Daniel Ek is backing Europa Fusion, a fusion power startup founded by an AI researcher. Here's what the startup is building.
title: Daniel Ek backs AI researcher’s fusion power startup. Here’s what they’re building

summary: Amid allegations of multiple affairs, including with a direct report and an alleged Chinese intelligence asset, sources tell WIRED the Nvidia board’s main issue was the former CEO’s “lack of candor.”
title: Jensen Huang’s ‘Lying’ Alarmed Nvidia Board Ahead of His Resignation

summary: Mathematicians are having their minds blown by the latest AI-driven result — and there's a competing human solution, too.
title: AI claimed a solution to the 167-year-old Riemann Hypothesis — and a human did, too

summary: We study high-probability linear regression in the infinite variance regime, wherecthe regression noise has only a finite conditional $α$-moment $ν$ for some unknown $α\in(1,2)$, and the covariates may only have finite moments up to a given order (e.g., 4th moment). We give a black-box reduction that converts finite-variance regression procedures into weak-moment procedures.
title: Optimal Linear Regression Without a Variance

summary: This study examines one-day-ahead forecasting of the S&P 500 closing level using a 2006-2025 dataset that includes fundamental price data, macroeconomic indicators, and engineered technical features. We benchmark three model families, namely linear regression, vanilla recurrent neural networks (RNN), and long short-term memory networks (LSTM), within a unified preprocessing and chronological evaluation pipeline.
title: A Methodologically Rigorous Benchmark of Linear Regression,RNN, and LSTM for S&P 500 Forecasting:Identifying Sources of Performance Inflation in Financial DeepLearning

summary: Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder is a neurodevelopmental condition that can affect attention, activity and impulse control. Electroencephalography (EEG) records brain activity as children and adolescents perform cognitive tasks. However, comparing features derived from these recordings requires consistent signal preparation, shared analysis windows and documented quality decisions.
title: On the Complete Feature Set for ADHD Classification in Children and Adolescents Based on EEG Signals

summary: President Donald Trump promised to put a "tremendous tax" on companies that build data centers outside of the US, even as states and cities around the country are placing restrictions on new applications to build them.
title: Trump threatens ‘tremendous tax’ for moving AI data centers outside the US

summary: Dexterous hand design demands repeated expert work across geometry, robot-description code, collision debugging, grasp initialization, and policy training. We present Task2Hand, a Skill: a specification package that turns a functional manipulation brief into a parameterized hand model and routes every candidate through cost-ordered contact, dynamics, and learning gates.
title: Task2Hand: A Contact-Grounded Skill for Parametric Dexterous-Hand Morphology Design

summary: Machine learning has largely kept separate the choice of architecture and the process of training. A classic Transformer, for instance, trains a fixed set of attention and MLP sublayers at every layer, in the same order, and optimizes the weights within.
title: Model Carving: Training Transformers That Optimize Their Own Topology

summary: Hyperparameter optimization (HPO) is essential for high predictive performance, but its computational cost becomes prohibitive when candidate configurations require repeated training on large datasets. This paper proposes a ranking-preserving coreset (RPC) selection framework for accelerating evolutionary HPO.
title: Ranking-Preserving Coreset Selection for Efficient Evolutionary Hyperparameter Optimization

summary: Neuromorphic sensing and computing offer a promising alternative to conventional deep learning pipelines for mobile robots, where perception must run continuously under tight latency and energy constraints. However, most neuromorphic solutions are still evaluated offline or on isolated benchmarks, and their integration into complete robotic systems remains largely unexplored.
title: Real-time neuromorphic audio and vision perception for autonomous robotic applications: Integration and experimental evaluation on a rover platform

summary: Large-scale model training is one of the most expensive workloads you can run on GPUs, and a single unhealthy accelerator can stall an entire distributed job. When training throughput drops, the hard part is rarely noticing that something is wrong. It is figuring out why and where.
title: Introducing enhanced infrastructure observability in Amazon SageMaker HyperPod

summary: Long-context models use sparse or structured attention to avoid quadratic cost, yet retrieving a small set of relevant facts embedded among hundreds of thousands of distractors degrades as normalization mass disperses with length. Hub-and-spoke optimal transport (OT) replaces the dense $L \times L$ matrix with a linear-size graph over local windows and $K$ shared hubs balanced by Sinkhorn scaling.
title: Topology Hub Optimal Transport: Eliminating Long Context Dilution at Flash Speed

summary: Let $\mathcal H\subseteq\{-1,+1,\star\}^{\mathcal X}$ be a partial concept class of finite VC dimension $d$.
title: The Optimal Sample Complexity of Agnostic PAC Learning for Partial Concept Classes

summary: A new report from the AI evaluation nonprofit METR finds that some AI capabilities are continuing to improve along an exponential trajectory—but it also indicates that models aren’t quite as good at tasks that require judgment as they are at coding.
title: The most misunderstood graph in AI just got a major update

summary: When a robot is damaged, it must decide which routes it can still afford, and the amount of risk it may accept can change from one mission to the next. We argue that whether a learned model helps such a robot depends on its decision interface, that is, on what the model hands to the planner.
title: What Must a Model Tell a Planner? Outcome Interfaces for Risk-Aware Planning After Robot Damage

summary: Autonomous racing requires an accurate vehicle dynamics model near the limits of handling, yet a mismatch between the nominal and actual dynamics inevitably remains.
title: Interactive Semi-Parametric On-Track Learning for Vehicle Dynamics in Autonomous Racing

summary: Video corpus moment retrieval asks a system to find, in a large collection of untrimmed videos with subtitles, the video and the time interval that a natural-language query describes. We find that most top-ranked errors of a strong corpus-level scorer come from choosing the wrong video, not from imprecise boundaries, and that re-weighting the evidence the scorer already uses does not fix them.
title: DiTraR: Diverse Scorers and Transcript-Guided Re-ranking for Video Corpus Moment Retrieval

summary: Despite major advances in structure prediction, modelling the motions and interactions that drive biomolecular function at scale remains a central challenge. We introduce BioEmu2, a generative model for atomically resolved biomolecular structures combining static structure prediction, equilibrium sampling and time evolution, that samples orders of magnitude faster than molecular dynamics (MD).
title: BioEmu2: Scalable Emulation of Biomolecular Dynamics

summary: Sparse autoencoders (SAEs) decompose diffusion model activations into interpretable features, but steering a model with them requires identifying which features map to a given semantic concept, if any. Existing methods for this concept to feature task are expensive, relying on grid searches or repeated passes through the frozen UNet. We propose Efficient Semantic Sparse Identification (ESSI).
title: ESSI: Computationally Efficient Semantic Search for Sparse Autoencoder Concepts

summary: Reward-independent representations enable reinforcement learning agents to reuse knowledge across tasks, but limited representation capacity raises three fundamental questions: what statistical dependence should these representations capture, which components of that dependence should be retained for policy improvement, and how does discarding the remaining components affect decision-making?
title: SUAF: Spectral Universal Advantage Features for Zero-Shot Policy Improvement

summary: Cardiovascular imaging offers several ways to measure blood flow, but each provides an incomplete, resolution-limited, or noisy view of the underlying dynamics. Reconstructing the missing information is inherently ambiguous because several flow fields may be compatible with the same observation.
title: Augmentation of cardiovascular flow measurements with generative diffusion models

summary: Vision-language models (VLMs) exhibit strong semantic understanding but remain limited in their ability to reason about metric 3D space in the physical world. Existing VLMs typically infer 3D scene structure from one or more images without known camera calibration or cross-view geometric constraints.
title: StereoVLM: Binocular Vision-Language Models for Metric 3D Spatial Reasoning

summary: Detecting individual instances is crucial for many segmentation problems. However, expert instance annotations are often unavailable, so instances are approximated heuristically (e.g., as connected components of semantic maps), which can merge touching objects or split fragmented ones.
title: Star Panoptic Quality: Selectively Evaluating Split and Merged Instances

summary: Transformer performance scales with depth, but layer count merely counts the opportunities for sequential computation: layers could still behave as nearly independent refinements that barely depend on one another.
title: Functional Depth Is Learned: Isolating the Computation That Layers Produce Only Together

summary: Business data systems must determine whether records refer to the same entity and retrieve records satisfying requests whose decisive properties are implicit. As agents act on these records, both tasks require auditable reasons. Dense embeddings perform well but offer opaque coordinates, cannot be filtered by meaning, and require corpus re-encoding to add new properties.
title: Decision Columns as an Index: Interpretable Embeddings for Explainable Entity Matching and Search

summary: Anthropomorphic non-human characters have long been used to convey hateful messages targeting human groups, from Nazi-era propaganda to recent AI-generated imagery on social media. However, the safety risks posed by such imagery remain largely unexplored. We thus conduct the first systematic study of hateful image generation and detection involving anthropomorphic non-human characters.
title: AnimalFarm: Auditing the Generation and Detection of Hateful Images Featuring Anthropomorphic Characters

summary: This week RadixArk released DaisyRose-27B , its first open-weight model. DaisyRose-27B is an agentic coding model from RadixArk, post-trained from Qwen3.8-27B with reinforcement learning (RL). The model card page states that it used RL only, with no SFT or distillation.
title: RadixArk Ships DaisyRose-27B, a 27B Agentic Coding Model Trained With Reinforcement Learning Only

summary: Lenders don't want SpaceX shooting their collateral into orbit. What does that mean for space data centers writ large?
title: Chips can survive the space environment — can their financing?

summary: Streaming visual geometry transformers retain historical key-value (KV) states as cross-view geometric memory, but growing caches constrain long-sequence inference. We systematically characterize KV quantization in streaming geometry and uncover two linked challenges: Nonuniform Geometric Sensitivity and Cache-Geometry Mismatch.
title: QuantStream3D: Geometry-Aligned Low-Bit KV Cache Quantization for Streaming Visual Geometry Transformers

summary: Electronic health records (EHRs) contain rich health information for uncovering latent patient representations and clinically meaningful subgroups.
title: Communication-Efficient Federated Learning of Latent Patient Representations from Multi-Institutional EHRs

summary: Sustaining user experience (UX) quality in large-scale web search requires scalable evaluation. Traditional surveys are slow and bottleneck rapid A/B testing, while automated metrics often lack the granularity to diagnose visual-spatial UX anomalies. To address this, we introduce the Dual-Tier Sentiment Framework, a novel industrial architecture for automated UX attribution.
title: The Dual-Tier Sentiment Framework: Scalable Multimodal UX Attribution in Web Search

summary: Coding agents increasingly implement rules written by domain experts, and bugs in such code are silent: it runs and returns a plausible answer.
title: TEA-Bench-BR: Can Coding Agents Turn a Branching Clinical Specification into Correct Code?

summary: Individualized treatment rules (ITRs) recommend treatment decisions based on individual characteristics and can improve treatment outcomes beyond traditional one-size-fits-all strategies. However, similar to other commonly used algorithmic decision-making methods, ITRs without considering model fairness may result in unfair decisions across groups defined by sensitive attributes, such as race or gender.
title: FairITR: Fairness-Aware Learning of Multicategory Individualized Treatment Rules

summary: Speculative decoding accelerates language-model inference by preparing candidate continuations before the target model generates them. Its efficiency depends on how well limited drafting computation anticipates the path the target will actually follow. Anticipating this path involves two sources of uncertainty: the target model's predictions and the randomness of sampling.
title: Speculative Decoding Is Less Speculative Than You Think

summary: Neural networks have parameter symmetries: parameter transformations that do not affect the represented function. How do these symmetries affect the functions that neural networks ultimately learn? We study the implicit bias arising from these symmetries by calculating the equilibrium distribution over represented functions under Langevin dynamics with Gaussian regularization.
title: Renormalized Entropy from Symmetries: Simplicity Bias and Neural Heat Death

summary: Tissue architecture provides important information for histopathological assessment, yet its complementary predictive value alongside pathology foundation-model representations remains insufficiently understood. This study investigates whether interpretable measurements of cellular and multicellular tissue organization provide additional predictive information beyond learned representations.
title: Interpretable Tissue Architecture Complements Pathology Foundation Models

summary: Every few months, a cancer patient's CT scans decide whether treatment continues. 3D foundation models can now detect, segment, register and track lesions, yet none of them reads the scans as a radiologist does. A radiologist decides which findings are lesions, which are the same lesion months later and whether a new spot means progression, and checks each decision against the extensive rules of a clinical guideline.
title: LesionAgent: Training-Free Agentic Tumor Tracking and Response Assessment in Longitudinal CT

summary: Modern generative models are typically studied for their ability to generalize, while memorization is treated as a failure mode. We invert this perspective and ask how a generative model can recall a single datum. We frame memorization as a control problem: a learned conditioning signal steers a frozen diffusion model toward a target image, and we follow the formation of this memory throughout training.
title: From Gist to Verbatim: The Controllable Path of One Image Through a Diffusion Prior

summary: Visual world models can now generate compelling interactive worlds, but visual realism does not guarantee faithful dynamics. We systematically compare how categorical and continuous prediction shape learned dynamics under both next-token and iterative whole-frame generation. These choices are often bundled in approaches such as autoregressive token models and whole-frame flow matching.
title: Beyond Visual Fidelity: Comparing Categorical and Continuous World Models

summary: Generative Artificial Intelligence (Generative AI) has emerged as a powerful tool for transforming learning. This review examines how Generative AI can be integrated with established learning style models (VARK, Kolb, Felder-Silverman, and Honey & Mumford) to support student engagement in large online classes.
title: Integrating Generative Artificial Intelligence with Learning Style Models: Opportunities, Challenges, and Future Directions

summary: Specification-guided reinforcement learning (RL) translates formal specifications of desired behavior of agents into shaped rewards. This paper introduces SLICR, a significant paradigm shift that advances the state of the art to specification-guided RL in adversarial settings under partial observability.
title: SLICR: Strategy Logic-Guided Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning

summary: Automatic facial behaviour understanding (AFBU) is fundamental to various human-centred applications, yet existing academically available toolkits offer limited functionality, closed training pipelines, and weak generalisation.
title: OpenAHBU: Open-sourced Automatic Human Behaviour Understanding Toolkit Through Facial Behaviour Analysis
