Failing to distinguish local evolution can lead to similar forecasts for locations that develop differently, increasing prediction error.
title: Interpretable Prototype-Conditioned Adaptation for Weather Forecasting

summary: Representative vision-language navigation (VLN) methods typically couple a vision-language model (VLM) brain with a learnable action head and fine-tune the VLM brain on navigation-domain data to predict geometric goals. However, such adaptation can substantially alter base VLM weights and degrade general visual capabilities.
title: ZeroVLN: Learning to Navigate without Supervised Fine-Tuning of the VLM Brain

summary: Latent world models predict the outcomes of action sequences, but comparing candidate plans through recursive rollout remains expensive at test time. We introduce Fast-JEPA, a latent world model planning framework that advances the success-latency Pareto frontier of predictive search. Fast-JEPA reorganizes predictive computation to support effective action-sequence search at low planning cost.
title: Fast-JEPA: Advancing the Success-Latency Frontier for Latent World Models

summary: Full-duplex interaction models exhibit strong conversational agency, enabling natural, low-latency turn-taking, backchannels, and interruptions. However, completing tasks further requires task agency: timely tool invocation and argument revision following user corrections. Frontend-backend agents separate initiation from execution: the frontend decides whether and what to request, while the backend determines how.
title: Duopra: From Full-Duplex Conversation to Full-Duplex Agency

summary: Peer review relies on several readers finding different problems. We measure critique overlap in conference and journal reviews. At ICLR, measured overlap rose from 12.0% in 2026 to 21.3% in 2027, in reviews from the same stage of the review process, with year-on-year rises at NeurIPS, ICML and the F1000 and PLOS journals.
title: Twice-Told Critiques: Claim-Level Homogenization of Peer Review in the LLM Era

summary: Robotic world models predict future video frames from the current observation and a sequence of robot actions. While recent models follow the given actions closely, manipulated objects often collapse or move inconsistently with the action.
title: Point Dynamics as Proxy for Robotic World Models

summary: Supervised fine-tuning (SFT) is the stage in which Video Large Language Models (VideoLLMs) advance their capability to reason over video. However, the VideoLLM also learns to answer from textual regularities of its training data, a shortcut that bypasses the video. The regularities behind the shortcut are hard to define at the data level, and the shortcut forms regardless of training epoch, data size, or backbone.
title: Suppressing the Shortcut Hidden Behind the Gains of VideoLLM Fine-Tuning

summary: World action models (WAMs) couple generative video modeling with robotic action prediction but typically require large video and action transformers, limiting deployment efficiency. We present LoopedWAM, a compact WAM that recurrently applies a shared six-block core in each expert, executing 30 transformer layers while storing only 12 blocks per expert.
title: LoopedWAM: Looped World Action Models for Elastic Inference

summary: Reasoning domains have shaped the post-training recipes of frontier models even though they are trained and deployed in domains beyond math and code.
title: LLMs Memorize Their Own Hallucinations During Post-Training

summary: As multimodal large language models (MLLMs) become increasingly integrated into everyday life, their ability to provide safe and reliable assistance in realistic daily activities remains insufficiently explored. Existing safety benchmarks primarily focus on isolated harmful requests or adversarial scenarios, overlooking the safety risks that may arise as ordinary tasks unfold.
title: DailySafe: Benchmarking Dynamic Safety Awareness in Everyday Multi-Turn Multimodal Interactions

summary: World models aim to predict environment dynamics under actions, enabling the prediction of action consequences without executing them in the real world. Yet despite producing increasingly realistic videos, current world models often fail to capture how small action changes affect future observations.
title: Learning What Actions Change: Action Effect Matching for Dynamics-Faithful World Models

summary: Release: llm-gemini 0.38 . Today Google introduced Gemini 4 Neon . I wrote recently about how confusing the pricing for the Gemini 4 series was - Neon has somehow made this even worse.
title: llm-gemini 0.38

summary: At Exa , we are building one of the few true web indexes by aggregating and serving knowledge from across the web, along with private and synthetic sources. We optimize the index for semantic search, grounding agents and humans in true, high-quality data.
title: Exa boosts embedding throughput by 50% to index billions of documents on AWS AI chips

summary: The Microsoft CEO downplayed the recent Outlook outage while noting that AI was causing both opportunities and new challenges for securing much of the connected world.
title: Amidst fears of AI cyberattacks, Satya Nadella says lots of critical infrastructure is ‘unpatchable’

summary: Zero-shot large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used as text classifiers, but their labels are only useful when we know to what extent we can trust them. We compare black-box methods (verbalised confidence and sampling) with white-box methods that read token probabilities (P(True), and multiple logit-scoring methods using constrained generation).
title: LLMs Are Already Confidence-Aware Zero-Shot Classifiers

summary: “I don’t think [Huang is] disloyal to the United States," Musk said.
title: Elon Musk says ousting Jensen Huang is like ‘kicking Michael Jordan off your team’

summary: New York, Los Angeles, and Chicago schools are considering Google alternatives after the company said it will disable Search for schools that opt out of its AI features, according to The New York Times.
title: The nation’s largest school districts consider ditching Google Search

summary: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella expressed confidence in Jensen Huang's successor Colette Kress, who is serving as Nvidia's interim CEO.
title: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella remains confident in Nvidia after Huang’s exit

summary: Large training jobs can fail even when every node looks healthy. A GPU with a subtle fault can pass its stress tests and still return wrong values. When a job stalls on an NCCL timeout, it keeps its GPUs, and Slurm still shows it as running.
title: Introducing workload recovery and expanded infrastructure checks on Amazon SageMaker HyperPod

summary: Microsoft's CEO says AI agents could disrupt advertising-driven business models, forcing companies like Amazon to rethink how they compete for customers.
title: Satya Nadella predicts AI agents will reshuffle the economics of the web

summary: Autonomous robots may need to adapt both their task plans and architectural configurations as operating conditions change. These decisions are interdependent: architectural configurations determine which actions a robot can perform, while task plans determine which capabilities are required.
title: Plan your Self-Adaptation! Ontology-Mediated Task and Architecture Co-adaptation Planning for Robots

summary: Reinforcement learning (RL) can improve vision-language-action (VLA) policies beyond imitation, but humanoid exploration is unsafe and simulator RL can exploit residual sim-to-real gaps. We present WEVO, a teleoperation-free framework for post-training a whole-body humanoid VLA in an action-conditioned video world model (WM).
title: WEVO: World Model-Enabled VLA Optimization for Whole-Body Loco-Manipulation

summary: Agentic cyber-physical systems rely on perception and state estimation to support autonomous decisions. Degraded, inconsistent, or manipulated sensor observations can therefore propagate through an autonomous pipeline and create security-relevant failures.
title: A Synthetic Multi-Modal Testbed for Security Stress Testing of Agentic Counter-UAS Systems

summary: Amazon SageMaker JumpStart gives you hundreds of open-weight foundation models you can deploy quickly. That choice is powerful, but it also creates a real question: Which model should you start with?
title: Introducing the Amazon SageMaker JumpStart Model Leaderboard

summary: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) can propose multi-step manipulation plans, but they have no grounded model of how a scene will change, and the pixel-level world models that could check those plans are slow and drift over long horizons. We present Verify2Act, a modular verification framework that separates semantic action proposal from latent physical verification.
title: Verify2Act: Critic-Guided Latent World Models for Verifying Language-Conditioned Manipulation Plans

summary: WIRED is tallying up how many times Nvidia’s interim CEO has assured everyone that the company has everything under control.
title: Does Nvidia Got This? Interim CEO Colette Kress Says It’s Got This

summary: The long-awaited IPO reportedly values the company at $1.5 trillion on a fully diluted basis.
title: Anthropic reportedly prices IPO at $83 a share, above projected range

summary: Ferrofluids are liquids containing magnetic nanoparticles, enabling shape control through external magnetic fields. This deformability supports their use as soft robotic bodies that can navigate confined spaces and manipulate objects. Their nonlinear continuum dynamics, however, make reliable control challenging.
title: Ferrofluid Shape Control with Deep Reinforcement Learning

summary: Fallout from the Nvidia scandal has made any negotiations around AI difficult, officials say.
title: Even His Own Officials Don’t Think Trump’s China Trip Will Lead to Progress on AI

summary: One Wall Street analyst got to the bottom of Nvidia's surprise announcement that it wouldn't be filing its formal quarterly results document, the 10-Q, for weeks.
title: Nvidia created a weird bit of intrigue by not filing a routine SEC report

summary: Amazon Bedrock provides access to foundation models from multiple providers through a common API, with AWS managing the model infrastructure. It integrates with AWS access controls and monitoring, and processes prompts, code, and model responses within AWS.
title: How Airbnb uses cost per task to operate coding agents on Amazon Bedrock

summary: Autonomous navigation in diverse real-world environments remains one of the greatest challenges in robotics. It demands both robust low-level motion control to handle diverse terrain and high-level reasoning to interpret environmental cues. We present ROAM (Robust Open-world Autonomous Mobility), a system that enables legged robots to perform kilometer-scale navigation in complex alpine and urban settings.
title: Bridging vision-language reasoning and learned control for legged navigation in the wild

summary: A customer support chatbot that queries historical tickets and knowledge base articles stored in Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL-Compatible Edition can deliver fast, context-aware answers.
title: Design responsible AI controls for Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL

coverage.title: Google ships Gemini 4 Neon, its fourth new Gemini model in a month

summary: Google introduces Gemini 4 Neon, delivering frontier-level intelligence for complex coding and analysis at a lower cost. See what's new.
title: Introducing Gemini 4 Neon

summary: The Anduril co-founder says outdated technology is leaving systems vulnerable to a new wave of AI-enabled attacks.
title: Palmer Luckey warns AI-powered cyberattacks are outpacing defenses: ‘It’s time to start running’

summary: "It makes America weaker to knock him out," the Anduril CEO said about ousted Nvidia leader Jensen Huang.
title: Palmer Luckey thinks China is ‘thrilled to have Jensen out,’ so he wants the ousted Nvidia CEO reinstated

summary: For high-performance computing (HPC) centers operating under a fixed power budget, every joule spent computing needs to translate into useful scientific work.
title: Connecting Energy Use to Scientific Output with Science per Joule

summary: Crisis and disaster governance increasingly relies on technologies that sense, classify and act faster than humans can. Drone swarms coordinated with human operators, known as human-swarm teaming, provide a productive case to review the field of crisis governance.
title: Crisis Governance at the Joints. Mapping the Ethical and Societal Territory of Crisis Management Technologies: The Case of Human-Swarm Teaming

summary: Adapting robot policies to out-of-distribution (OOD) settings with limited real-world data remains a key bottleneck to generalist robots. The multimodality and scarcity of robotics data lead end-to-end approaches to overfit and break under small distribution shifts.
title: VG-Steer: Visual-Geometric Policy Steering from In-Context Aligned Abstractions

summary: Self-play reinforcement learning (RL) produces strong driving policies, but these policies are hard to verify or interpret. Differentiable model predictive control (DiffMPC) can enforce explicit constraints, but it is usually trained by imitating logged data or with costly RL.
title: From Self-Play RL to Constrained Control: Distilling DiffMPC Students with DAgger

summary: The Trump administration announced plans to clamp down on China’s access to AI chips. Apparently, the cheating scandal of the century was the motivation they were missing.
title: America’s AI Chip War Is Heating Up in the Dumbest Possible Ways

summary: Simulated manipulation benchmarks measure policy performance using hand-written success checkers that label each episode as a success or failure. Passing an expert demonstration shows that a checker accepts one way of completing the task. Learned policies, however, may stop after partial progress or complete the task in a different way.
title: Phantom Success, Silent Failure: Auditing the Success Checkers of Simulated Manipulation Benchmarks

summary: Many teams that build applications self-host their identity provider (IdP), such as Keycloak or PingFederate, inside a private network. These IdPs usually present a TLS server certificate from a private certificate authority (CA).
title: Private certificate authority support in Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Identity

summary: Can the allocation used to train experts also predict which expert will perform best on a prompt? Such a connection would make the intended division of labor inspectable before training and allow the allocation itself to guide inference. We introduce InflEns, a mixture of LoRA experts whose training weights and inference routes come from the same location game in a fixed prompt-trait space.
title: Game-Theoretic Data Allocation for Expert Specialization and Routing

summary: Autonomous energy systems increasingly chain specialized learned agents, such as a forecaster, a state estimator and a dispatcher that may be a language model. These agents can emit confident outputs that contradict physics, and downstream agents may act on them.
title: GridAnchor: Specialized Multi-Agent AI for Safeguarding Autonomous Energy Systems Against Cyber-Physical Hallucinations

summary: End-to-end driving models learn to plan from data, and hand-written planners are widely treated as a thing of the past.
title: Old-School Planners Drive (Sometimes) Better Than Learned Ones

summary: Thanks to Amit Gupta, Senior Director- AI/ML and Mark Wang, Software Engineering PMTS from Salesforce for your contributions in the vision and partnership of cross-Region inference routing on SageMaker AI.
title: How Salesforce is advancing global-scale model serving with cross-Region inference routing in Amazon SageMaker AI

summary: Visual world models enable effective short-horizon goal-conditioned planning, such as reaching nearby targets and pushing objects over short distances, by predicting candidate action outcomes and comparing their representations with a goal representation.
title: GEMS: Generation and Experience Memory for Subgoal-Guided Long-Horizon World Model Planning

summary: "It doesn't feel like it's in like the top 10 weirdest things about my life," Altman said.
title: Sam Altman says his life is so weird that he’s unfazed by Andrew Garfield portraying him in upcoming movie

summary: Lens creators can describe the Lens they want in plain language, and their AI assistant handles the process from start to finish, Snapchat says.
title: Snapchat now lets developers build AR Lenses with AI assistants like Claude Code and Cursor

summary: Today we are releasing DaisyRose-27B, RadixArk’s first model, built on Qwen3.8-27B and trained with reinforcement learning using Miles. We trained it on long-horizon agent tasks with sessions up to 1M tokens, with just 1,200 curated tasks in 18 days on 144 H200 GPUs.
title: DaisyRose-27B: Pushing the Frontier of Post-Training Efficiency

summary: President Donald Trump was greeted by no less than five beauty queens when he landed in the Philippines on Tuesday, according to local news outlet Rappler. As he stepped onto the tarmac, a child handed him small US and Philippine flags. A band played "YMCA," a staple at Trump rallies, as more girls in traditional [. ]
title: Trump’s latest land grab is an AI hub in the Philippines

summary: Every move in a robot team changes the world in which its teammates must act. Coordinated manipulation therefore calls for predicting the team's actions together with the physical future they jointly create. We introduce MAWAM, a multi-agent world-action model that jointly generates each robot's future views and executable action chunks in a single sample.
title: MAWAM: A Multi-Agent World-Action Model for Coordinated Manipulation

summary: If someone handed you $8,300 every second, what would you do? That's how much pure profit Nvidia now makes. By the time you finish reading this paragraph, Nvidia will likely have cleared $45,000 and change. It's easy to look at Nvidia, a company that just lost its visionary founder CEO due to a series of [. ]
title: What’s next for Nvidia? Whatever doesn’t rock the mind-bogglingly profitable boat

summary: This post is co-written by Mariah Miller and Sirajus Salekin from AWS and Nicholas Chase from Social Department. Entertainment marketing teams manage tens of thousands of video assets across studios, networks, and streaming applications.
title: How Social Department built culture-aware video discovery

summary: With Genie 4, Google DeepMind is launching its most realistic world model to date for Google AI Ultra subscribers. It generates interactive 3D worlds that can be modified in real time via text input and, for the first time, includes native sound.
title: Google Deepmind's Project Genie update brings Genie 4, chainable worlds, and a community gallery for remixing

summary: Enabling AI systems to autonomously improve AI models requires agents capable of performing machine learning engineering (MLE). In practice, designing, training, and evaluating complex models demands modifying multi-file repositories to reproduce results, debug training runs, integrate datasets, and port frameworks.
title: BuggyMLE: Scaling Machine Learning Engineering Difficulty with Bug Injection

summary: After some early adopters of Meta’s Muse AI agent complained that it was spying on private messages and behaving unpredictably earlier this fall, Reuters exposed internal chats showing that Meta staff had raised the same alarms.
title: Muse privacy invasions are freaking out Meta staffers, internal chats show

summary: Large language models (LLMs) write fluent financial analyses but miscompute ratios, recall stale prices, and route questions to the wrong tool with high confidence.
title: FinVeriQA: Financial Research Agents for Question Answering: Routing, Retrieval, MCP Tool Use, and Provenance-Aware Evidence Verification

summary: Gas Source Localization (GSL) with mobile robots is challenging because wind and gas measurements are spatially sparse, noisy, and potentially affected by robot motion. Indoor airflow can vary substantially across space, while detailed environmental layouts, boundary conditions, or precomputed airflow fields are often unavailable.
title: Mapping the Wind to Find the Source: Online Physics-Informed Gas Source Localization with Mobile Robots

summary: Humans can understand the 3D structure of scenes even from highly unfamiliar or extreme viewpoints. Cognitive science suggests this generalization stems from a top-down generative inference strategy. In contrast, state-of-the-art 3D reconstruction neural networks typically rely on amortized, feedforward inference.
title: Infer3D: Inverse Generative Modeling Enables Robust 3D Reconstruction

summary: With just a few weeks remaining, lawmakers are trying to pass new protections for victims of online harm before the end of 2026, targeting deepfake creators and online platforms that block users from filing lawsuits.
title: Tech lawsuits defined 2026 — and lawmakers want more

summary: Decentralized multi-agent LLM systems enable independently administered agents, each with its own operator, model, memory, and configuration, to collaborate on complex tasks without centralized coordination. Agents autonomously decompose tasks, execute subtasks and delegate remaining work to peers, enabling scalability and eliminating single points of failure.
title: Attacks and Defenses in Decentralized Multi-Agent Systems with Hop-by-Hop Task Decomposition and Delegation

summary: In many enterprises, a central network team owns every virtual private cloud (VPC) and subnet, and every flow between VPCs must pass a central firewall in both directions.
title: Connect Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway to private APIs in a hub-and-spoke network with centralized inspection

summary: Over the past decade, MIT researchers have developed aerial microrobots with bumblebee-like speed, agility, and durability, for tasks like precision agriculture or search-and-rescue.
title: This featherweight, flying robot carries its own sensors and computers

summary: We introduce $Z$-sight, a unified robot foundation model that couples vision-language-action (VLA) and generative latent world modeling. Video-based world action models (WAMs) show the value of joint future-and-action generation for control, yet inherit the heavy cost of video generators.
title: $Z$-sight: Unifying Vision-Language-Action and Latent World Modeling

summary: World-action models jointly predict future observations and actions, yet reconstruction-oriented visual representations do not explicitly emphasize the spatial relationships and object-state changes needed for manipulation. We introduce Phoenix, which learns representations of scene structure for world-action modeling.
title: Phoenix: Learning Scene Structure Representations for Generalizable World-Action Models

summary: This post is co-written with Danya Gordin from Stretto and Marcelo Wzorek from CI&T. Before Stretto built an AI voice agent, consumers considering bankruptcy on its Bankruptcy.com site filled out a web form with a few fields: debt amount, attorney status, and contact information.
title: How Stretto built an AI voice agent with Amazon Nova 2 Sonic

summary: Jailbreak attempts and harmful prompts remain a challenge for the safe deployment of large language models. We study whether contrastively learned representations can support safety detection without training an additional downstream classifier.
title: Jailbreak Detection on Large Language Models via Contrastive Prototype Structures

summary: When a capable model and a human reviewer cooperate on the same decision, which human still adds value? We argue this is a question about a single cognitive trait, metacognitive calibration: the alignment between a reviewer's behavioral confidence and the actual correctness of their judgments. We develop a trait theory of reviewer value to make it precise.
title: Knowing What You Know: A Trait Theory of Reviewer Value in Human-AI Cognitive Systems

summary: AWS Quick User Group DC inaugural meetup recap . Many organizations are asking how to move beyond static reporting dashboards and begin using generative and agentic AI. But before an AI agent can answer questions or help teams act, it requires a trusted data foundation.
title: From reporting to reasoning: Getting enterprise data ready for AI agents

summary: AI systems are built across many organizations that contribute models, data, compute, capital, talent, and other assets. While the layers of the AI stack are relatively well understood, the relationships between actors and components across layers remains sparsely documented.
title: Mapping the AI Supply Chain: Dependencies, Vulnerabilities, and Market Concentration in the AI Ecosystem

summary: Robot reward modeling faces two challenges: generalizing across tasks and accurately tracking progress in long-horizon manipulation. General-purpose reward models demonstrate broad task transfer, but transfer from short-task pretraining to long-horizon tasks remains underexplored.
title: Grana: Compositional Reward Modeling for Long-Horizon Robot Manipulation

summary: Predicting end-to-end fine-tuning time on shared GPU clusters, from 272 production runs.
title: Why your fine-tuning job takes longer than the FLOPs say

summary: Predicting the consequences of an agent's actions requires modeling both the body's motion and the environment's response. Most video world models attempt to learn both from numerical actions, even though geometry and kinematics already specify the intended motion.
title: Render the Robot, Generate the World: One Video World Model Across Embodiments

summary: Real-world harness engineering is driven by explicit and implicit user requirements, which guide development and validation. However, existing harness evolution methods often overlook implicit requirements and interaction needs, while using a single evolution agent to modify the harness and benchmark scores to select changes. This process often produces narrow patches and leads to benchmark-specific local optima.
title: Agentic Harness Engineering Beta: Requirement-Centered Evolution of Agent Harnesses

summary: In this paper, we propose a Unified Law for Visual Tasks, which could be further divided into Four Laws of Computer Vision, with the goal of enabling a single framework or method to uniformly train on and perform nearly all visual tasks.
title: Unified Law for Visual Tasks (The Four Laws of Computer Vision)

summary: Agentic image restoration composes operations to handle mixed degradations, yet its toolbox often requires storing multiple restoration networks. We propose PrismRestore, which constructs a compact bank of callable restoration actions from a single frozen all-in-one model. Our approach builds on task-dependent yet overlapping channel responses in the shared model.
title: PrismRestore: A Compact Restoration Toolbox for Agentic Image Restoration

summary: Microsoft's AI division MAI unveiled seven new models for code, security, images, language, and routing at Ignite. MAI Code 2 reaches 98 percent of GPT-6.1 Sol's performance at 40 percent of the cost, according to Microsoft. The models are built for running AI agents around the clock in enterprises.
title: Microsoft is replacing outside AI models in its own products with cheaper in-house alternatives

summary: We study two-layer neural networks trained by stochastic gradient descent (SGD) on a multi-index teacher model, focusing on how first-layer parameters orthogonal to the teacher subspace affect generalization. We decompose the first-layer weights into a signal component aligned with the teacher and an orthogonal complement, and analyze their joint SGD dynamics together with the second layer in the proportional limit.
title: Decomposing SGD Dynamics in Neural Networks: Teacher-Induced Spikes and Variance Inflation

summary: Overhead aerial imagery feeds dense-prediction pipelines that are routinely trained in one geographic region and deployed in another, yet no benchmark measures how shadow detection models transfer across regions. Existing overhead shadow datasets either lack a geographic transfer protocol or rely on automatically generated labels.
title: ShadowTransfer: A Geographic Transfer Benchmark for Overhead Shadow Detection

summary: We present a general framework for modeling and learning equivariant functions between finite dimensional semisimple real group representations, unifying constructions developed across many application areas. Our model is a linear combination of equivariant polynomial features whose coefficients are arbitrary learnable functions of invariant polynomial features.
title: Equivariant Modeling with Polynomial Features via Minimal Homogeneous Generators

summary: User simulators offer a scalable way to evaluate interactive agents, but how to assess their quality remains underexplored. In particular, it is unclear whether existing user simulator evaluation frameworks reliably detect meaningful failures in simulated user behavior. This uncertainty makes it difficult to interpret simulator evaluation.
title: On Evaluating User Simulators for Interactive Agents

summary: If the glorious AI revolution rests entirely on the well-being of one man, AI is perhaps not as robust a technology as I had previously been led to believe. Nonetheless, chunks of Silicon Valley are now insisting he is indispensable.
title: What is Nvidia without AI’s sugar daddy in charge?

summary: A fixed dispatch rate for LLM inference becomes stale as serving fleets resize and request sizes change. Generative output length is unknown at admission, and shared provider pools can lose capacity. We present Cap-and-Track, a design for asynchronous inference across provider capacity and internal GPUs. Meta's traffic shaper implements Cap-and-Track for post and live-video understanding.
title: Cap-and-Track: Optimizing LLM Inference Request Dispatch Across Shifting Capacity

summary: Large Language Models (LLMs) now perform strongly on Alan Turing's 1950 Imitation Game, so we propose a harder challenge, the Personal Imitation Game, which asks whether a machine can replicate a specific individual in conversation rather than a generic human.
title: Who are you? The Personal Imitation Game

summary: Large language models have been widely used to generate plausible research ideas, yet it remains unclear what makes automated ideation effective and how generated novel proposals arise from prior scientific work. We introduce the Creative AI Researcher (CAR), an agentic framework combining literature grounding, iterative development and explicit conceptual operators.
title: Ground, Iterate, Trace: Decomposing AI Research Ideation

summary: Robotic haircutting requires accurate motion execution and reliable communication to safely reproduce the operator's commands. Internet-based teleoperation is a key enabling technology to remotely perform precise manipulation tasks such as haircutting.
title: Teleoperated Haircutting with Delay Compensation and Passivity-Based Control for Unilateral Internet Teleoperation under Real Communication Uncertainties

summary: We introduce a notion of monoculture robustness in Probably Approximately Correct (PAC) learning, as a way to mitigate the problem of algorithmic monoculture (Kleinberg and Raghavan, 2021): the tendency of models sharing the same components (e.g., training data) to fail on the same inputs.
title: Monoculture Robust Learning

summary: Agentic artificial intelligence (AI) is emerging in power electronics, where it drives the simulation loop that engineers used to close largely by hand. In this loop, a converter design, or a study of the network it connects to, is built, run, measured and revised until it satisfies its specification. Such an agent can be served from a cloud API or from an inference device on the premises.
title: Local AI Agents in Power Electronics Simulation: Deployment, Measurements and Costs

summary: Large language models (LLMs) are used to explain clinical prediction models, on the promise that they can say what a model computes, find its faults and even reveal new knowledge in it. We tested the three promises where the answers could be checked.
title: Auditing black-box clinical prediction models with a large language model through queries alone: a blinded test with planted flaws

summary: Large-scale, multi-agent self-play trains robust driving policies effectively in simulation, but controlling these models to generate specific, safety-critical edge cases remains a key challenge. Existing goal-conditioned self-play frameworks rely primarily on static map-location goals and fail to reliably produce complex agent interactions such as aggressive tailgating or adversarial cut-offs.
title: Learning to Interact in Multi-Agent Self-Play for Controllable Autonomous Driving Scenario Generation

summary: Neural PDE operators are often optimized through state reconstruction, which largely constrains operator values at observed inputs but does not fully characterize their sensitivity to local perturbations. A more faithful approximation of operator behavior requires not only accurate state predictions, but also correct variations along local perturbation directions.
title: TangentPDE: Learning Local Operator Responses with Sparse Finite-Difference Supervision

summary: Visual agents that read dense documents must ration a finite observation budget across candidate regions, yet answer accuracy conflates where an agent looks, how it adapts to the reads that remain, and how it an?swers once observation stops.
title: Choosing What to Observe: Budget-Paired Counterfactual Audits for Credible Evaluation of Visual Agents

summary: Underwater navigation requires translating visual spatial cues into motion, yet marine vision-language datasets rarely include paired robot trajectories. We present NereidVLA, a vision-language-action model that transfers marine spatial knowledge to language-conditioned 3D navigation.
title: NereidVLA: Learning to Understand and Navigate the Underwater World

summary: Human communication involves highly coordinated multimodal signals such as speech and co-speech gestures. Existing approaches for generating both modalities commonly follow a cascaded pipeline, where speech is generated first and subsequently used to drive gesture generation; speech generation is therefore independent of gestures.
title: Gaspard: Expressive unified speech and gesture synthesis with continuous autoregressive flow-matching and decoupled classifier-free guidance

summary: A team of skilled card players share no information amongst each other, and yet still are able to coordinate their play by watching the same players and reading the same tells. Autonomous systems have failed to exploit this logic, relying instead on explicit communication or complex state estimation schemes that can fail when it matters most.
title: Communications-free Collective Intelligence Via Allocentric Belief

summary: We are rolling out a new Project Genie experience to eligible Google AI Ultra subscribers, opening access to our new Genie 4 world model.
title: Genie 4 is now available

summary: Large language model (LLM) judges have become a common way to create large-scale relevance judgments for retrieval evaluation. However, each judgment requires a potentially expensive call to a frontier model, and the judgments are hard to interpret and may not be reproducible. In this paper, we ask whether an LLM can write a readable program for each topic that replaces its per-document judgments.
title: Can Programs Replace LLM Judges? Executable Program Judges for Scalable and Efficient Relevance Labeling

summary: Most existing approaches enhance mathematical reasoning in large language models (LLMs) as a monolithic capability, despite the fact that different mathematical problems require different reasoning skills. Recent work has explored a more fine-grained perspective by decomposing mathematical reasoning into atomic skills and developing specialized modules for individual capabilities.
title: Atomic MathReasoner: Instance-Level Composition of Atomic Reasoning Skills for Mathematical LLMs

summary: Existing AI agents can retrieve information, call tools, run experiments, and produce multi-step outputs. Yet most are built around relatively static workflows and struggle to preserve reliable state as the environment changes. Financial trading makes this limitation especially consequential: prices, news, market conditions, portfolio positions, and available capital evolve continuously.
title: Vibe-Trading: Towards Agent-Native Trading

summary: Language models acquire their capabilities from training data, and developers withhold data during training to keep models from learning capabilities that could be misused. How long this delays a capability, and how much data is needed to acquire it later, is unknown. Here we show that the general progress a model makes on the rest of its training data substitutes for the data that was withheld.
title: General progress substitutes for specific training data in language models

summary: Neural surrogates for external vehicle aerodynamics are fast alternatives to physics-based computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations. Their foundational limitation is a lack of zero-shot generalization across vehicle classes, which results in an expensive, custom training campaign for each new vehicle design.
title: Measuring and Improving Transfer of Neural Surrogates for Vehicle Aerodynamics

summary: World models are increasingly used in autonomous driving to predict how a scene evolves under the ego vehicle's actions, supporting counterfactual reasoning and model-based planning. However, existing evaluations focus on prediction fidelity and planning performance, and rarely verify that the predictions depend on the conditioning action.
title: Does the Action Matter? Probing Action-Conditioned Semantic Forecasting as a World Model for Autonomous Driving

summary: One popular architecture for multi-agent systems (MAS) relies on an orchestrator that generates an initial plan, coordinates its execution, and dynamically revises the plan based on agent feedback when tasks cannot be fully specified in advance. This dynamic replanning introduces a critical vulnerability: malicious agents can embed instructions within their feedback to hijack the replanning process.
title: Kaer: Security-Aware Replanning for Multi-Agent Systems

summary: Google's new temporary threads let users have conversations in AI Mode without adding them to their search history or influencing future recommendations.
title: Google’s AI feature in Search gets its own incognito mode

summary: Despite the proliferation of survival analysis methods, current benchmarks often operate under narrow conditions: they heavily rely on the concordance index (C-index) for evaluation and model selection, and frequently either exclude deep learning (DL) methods or underrepresent challenging dataset regimes.
title: What Survival Benchmarks Don't Tell You: Impact of Model Selection and Dataset Regimes

summary: Learning robot manipulation is constrained by the availability of action-labeled robot data, for both imitation and world models. Humans can demonstrate skills in seconds, but their demonstrations lack the required robot actions. We introduce DiWALI, a framework that learns and improves diffusion policies within a world model trained on human and robot play.
title: DiWALI: Diffusion Policy Learning in World Models via Latent Action Inference from Human and Robot Play

summary: Explainable AI (XAI) is frequently applied to high-stakes tabular data, yet the field relies heavily on feature attribution methods. While these approaches offer technical transparency, evaluating dozens of isolated features demands excessive cognitive effort from non-expert users.
title: Overlooked and Underutilized: Prototypes are the Missing Piece in Tabular XAI

summary: Working with AMD, OpenAI achieved up to 14 percent PPA improvement on AMD's flagship GPU IP in less than five months. According to OpenAI, that's roughly a year's worth of progress, and AMD has already folded the changes into a design sent to production.
title: OpenAI says its models delivered a year's worth of chip optimization on top of AMD's own engineering

summary: The spectral range of the Field Imaging Nanosatellite for Crop residue Hyperspectral Mapping (FINCH), developed by the University of Toronto Aerospace Team's Space System Division, poses significant challenges for hyperspectral unmixing to determine crop residue cover fractional abundances. The severe lack of standard indices necessitates the use of complex, data-driven unmixing models.
title: Synthesizing hyperspectral Data using generative Models to train spectral Unmixing Methods for low-cost Crop Residue Cover Mapping

summary: As advanced and lifelike as the animatronic characters at Disney parks have become, they typically either stick to predefined movements and routines, or there's an out of sight puppeteer helping make their behavior appear more spontaneous.
title: Disney’s new Star Wars animatronics interact with guests using AI

summary: Learning shared action representations is central to cross-embodiment manipulation. However, identical joint values can produce different spatial configurations across robots, limiting representations learned from joint values alone. We introduce RoboMorpher, a morphology-conditioned action tokenizer that jointly reconstructs joint angles and link poses to associate control coordinates with their kinematic effects.
title: RoboMorpher: Scaling Robot Morphology Representations for Cross-Embodiment Action Prediction

summary: Rooftop photovoltaics raise three questions: should a household invest, which incentive costs the state least, and does the feeder stay within limits? Those who ask are rarely modellers. We present LAaDT-DSS, decision-support software that answers all three under Turkish tariff rules from one simulation core.
title: LAaDT-DSS: decision support for non-experts on rooftop PV, incentive and grid simulations under Turkish tariff rules

summary: Hybrid attention models combine full and linear attention to achieve a better quality--efficiency trade-off. Converting pretrained Transformers into such models requires identifying which layers should retain full attention under a prescribed budget.
title: On-Policy Morphing into Hybrid Attention Models

summary: Self-supervised learning has produced powerful visual representations, yet learning strong dense features remains challenging. While consistency between augmented views provides strong image-level supervision, extending this principle to local visual content is less straightforward.
title: ReCoCo: From Patches to Compositions for Visual Representation Learning

summary: Smart wearable devices, such as augmented reality glasses, increasingly rely on cameras to understand and interact with their surroundings. However, their compact sensors often capture noisy RAW images, while limited compute and power make high-quality on-device restoration difficult. This creates an emerging need to reduce both local computation and transmission cost without sacrificing image quality.
title: Edge-Efficient Joint RAW Image Compression and Restoration for Smart Wearable Devices

summary: Global planners and path-tracking controllers are often evaluated independently, although their interaction determines how a vehicle follows a planned path. Whether simulation accurately predicts the performance of specific planner-controller combinations on Ackermann-steered hardware remains uncertain.
title: Planner-Controller Interaction for Ackermann Navigation: A Matched Simulation and Hardware Benchmark

summary: Modeling systemic failure in high-dimensional environments is fundamentally limited by supervised algorithms that attempt to predict sparse, noisy or censored endpoints.
title: Prognosis Without Prediction: The Intrinsic Geometry of Survival

summary: Quantum Machine Learning (QML) has attracted increasing interest as a possible route to construct feature representations that are difficult to reproduce with classical models. However, near-term QML architectures based on trainable parametrized quantum circuits remain affected by limited hardware resources, noise, and severe optimization difficulties such as barren plateaus.
title: Soft Mixture of Quantum Experts for Hybrid Quantum-Classical Learning

summary: Neural networks with randomly initialized, fixed weights and trainable biases are universal approximators, yet the dynamics of bias-only training remain largely unexplored. We study these dynamics in one-hidden-layer ReLU networks through activation codes, the binary patterns of active neurons that partition the input space into convex polyhedral regions.
title: Bias-Only Training Dynamics in ReLU Networks

summary: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) struggle with accurately capturing camera-object relations, especially for object orientation, camera viewpoint, and camera shots. This stems from the fact that existing MLLMs are trained on images with limited diverse camera-object relations and corresponding textual descriptions.
title: Ultimate3D: Teaching Multimodal LLMs 3D Camera-Object Relations by Large-Scale Visual Instruction Data

summary: Visualizing intermediate representations could help us inspect the reasoning steps underlying a model output. Unified multimodal models offer this opportunity by combining understanding and generation in one architecture. Their image generators can access representations formed while processing text.
title: The Elephant in the Question: Unified Models Picture the Concepts Behind Their Answers

summary: Self-supervised encoders for animal behavior are often trained on, or fed, hand-built movement features. We ask whether they beat those ingredients when compared fairly.
title: Training-free motion statistics match self-supervised behavior encoders

summary: Isabelle Pool Server (IPS), a verification service with a pool of warm headless Isabelle sessions behind an HTTP API, with session leasing and reclamation, memory-aware admission control, and a time budget on every call.
title: Isabelle Pool Server: a pooled verification service for prover training and multi-agent proving

summary: Interim CEO Collette Kress sought to ease employee concerns following Jensen Huang’s ouster, in part by promising to increase compensation.
title: Inside Nvidia’s First Post-Jensen All-Hands: Pay Raises and More Equity

coverage.title: Banks Have Had It Up to Here With Your AI Agent

summary: Citi is the latest major financial institution to put the breaks on personal finance AI agents.
title: More banks say customers using AI agents are on their own — even if they get hacked

summary: Vision-language models (VLMs) are often asked several questions about the same image in a single prompt (co-asking), yet existing evaluations report conflicting accuracy gains and hallucinations at the prompt level without tracking how individual answers change.
title: Read Together, Answer Apart: How Earlier Questions Help Vision-Language Models Look

summary: Neural networks trained on the same task develop related weight-space structures, yet remain distinguishable after learning. Do these differences merely reflect alternative solutions, or do they preserve information about individual learning histories? We tested whether final weights reveal initialization, task order, and earlier trajectory states.
title: Learning Trajectories Leave Decodable Traces in Neural Network Weight Space and Internal Representations

summary: Self-supervised video encoders are commonly trained to either reconstruct pixels or predict latent features, yet it remains unclear how these objectives shape representations for downstream dynamics. We present a capacity-matched study isolating this choice: two identical video encoders with a shared FSQ bottleneck are trained under autoencoding and V-JEPA objectives on a continuous control environment.
title: Reconstruction vs. Prediction Pre-Training of Discrete Video Representations for Continuous Control

summary: World models operate in a world they cannot fully observe. When a hidden disturbance, such as a current pushing a boat, changes the outcome of an action, a counterfactual question follows: what would have happened under a different action, subject to the same disturbance? Its answer separates bad decisions from bad luck.
title: Counterfactual World Models: JEPAs That Reason About "What If"

summary: Electron ptychography recovers atomic structure from 4D-STEM data: diffraction patterns at multiple positions of a scanned probe. Current codes reconstruct an image and read atoms off it, or fit atoms under an $L_1$ loss; neither gives per-atom uncertainty.
title: 4D-TEMPO: Differentiable 4D-STEM ptychography via fast Physics Optimizers

summary: This paper presents a hierarchical admittance-impedance controller that combines an inner Cartesian impedance controller, an outer 6D admittance supervisor, and workspace-aware mobile-base assistance for guided load transfer. The method is motivated by assistive tasks such as airport baggage handling, where a robot should support a payload while a human worker guides its motion through small physical forces.
title: Hierarchical Admittance-Impedance Control for Mobile Manipulator Load Transfer

summary: Identifying high-impact attack paths in cyber-physical power systems is critical for improving grid resilience. Existing methods typically rely on either structural topology analysis or simulation-based cascading-failure models.
title: LLM-Guided Cyber-Physical Attack Path Identification in Smart Grids

summary: Learning the spatiotemporal dynamics of cells from spatial transcriptomics requires connecting snapshots of different cells acquired in different coordinate frames. A rotation or translation of a section can appear as cell movement and distort the inferred correspondence. We introduce horizontal flow matching, which learns changes in tissue organization, molecular state, and cell abundance up to shared rigid motion.
title: Horizontal Flow Matching for Single-Cell Spatiotemporal Dynamics

summary: Reconstructing cellular dynamics from snapshots is challenging because the destructive nature of single-cell measurements makes tracking the same cells over time impossible. Cellular dynamics are inherently stochastic and involve changes in population size through proliferation and apoptosis.
title: Elysium: Simulation-Free Unbalanced Schrödinger Bridges

summary: Recent Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) have achieved strong performance on general video understanding benchmarks, yet their ability to reason about participant roles in aggressive interactions remains largely unexplored.
title: A$^3$Bench: Compositional Reasoning over Aggressive Interactions in Videos

summary: Online A/B testing is the standard approach for evaluating changes to user-facing systems, such as a new recommendation or ranking policy, before deployment. While the difference-in-means estimator of a standard A/B test is unbiased, it often suffers from high variance.
title: Variance-Optimal Counterfactual Policy Design for Sample-Efficient Online A/B Testing

summary: We extend our previous search for the modular data of topological quantum field theories in 2+1 dimensions from 22 to 42 anyons, identifying 150,679 new modular data. We do so by adding to our algorithm three rejection gates, two of them based on logistic regression, that discard representations of $SL(2,\mathbb{Z})$ unlikely to yield modular data.
title: Learning the Anyon Atlas

summary: Lateral velocity is safety-critical for vehicle-dynamics control but cannot be measured with production sensors. Model-based estimators such as Kalman filters are established, whereas data-driven estimators are more accurate within the training regime but suspected to lose accuracy beyond it. Their transfer to a structurally different vehicle has rarely been tested.
title: Cross-Vehicle Transferability of Lateral Velocity Estimation on Production Vehicles through Input Selection and Data Augmentation

summary: World model accuracy starts with high-quality, diverse training datasets. Yet capturing rare defects, nighttime incidents, and other challenging scenarios is.
title: Build Training-Ready Physical AI Datasets with Two Prompts in NVIDIA Cosmos

summary: The Google Gemini app now supports lower-memory Android devices. Access Gemini Live and custom image creation on your phone. Download the app today.
title: The Gemini app is now available on lower-memory Android devices

summary: Our previous post in this series introduced the Ranking Engineer Agent (REA), an autonomous system that generates hypotheses, designs experiments, and proves new machine learning (ML) techniques on ads ranking models.
title: How Meta Uses AI Agents to Scale ML Innovations Across Ads Ranking Models

summary: Sam Altman and Greg Brockman pushed back against Silicon Valley's growing debate over an AI takeover, while acknowledging the challenges of keeping advanced models under human control.
title: Sam Altman warns against a future where AI, not humans, calls the shots

summary: Parkinson's disease (PD) is the second most common neurodegenerative disease in the world, and 70\% to 75\% of PD patients suffer from speech disorders at some stage. Since PD affects men more frequently than women, previous publications tend to rely on unbalanced datasets that potentially introduce sex biases into trained models.
title: Sex Differences in the Detection of Parkinson's Disease from Speech

summary: Accurate matched affinities determine mutation effects, but gains in aggregate affinity prediction may transfer unevenly to average effects, ordering and local accuracy. We evaluated eleven method families using method-specific matched populations. Controlled CoPRA reduced absolute-affinity mean absolute error from 1.2898 to 1.1431 pKd.
title: Uneven gains in protein-RNA affinity and mutation-effect prediction

summary: Recent advances in world models are opening new possibilities for fine-grained embodied tasks, with hand-object interaction offering a particularly demanding setting. Modeling these interactions involves capturing how hand actions change objects and how the resulting states persist over time. Yet systematic evaluation tailored to these hand-centric capabilities remains underdeveloped.
title: HandWorldBench: A Unified Benchmark for Hand-Centric World Models

summary: The rapidly expanding generative AI landscape brings together methods that differ in architecture, learning objective, mathematical representation and sampling procedure. A concise, selectively organised technical guide can provide an accessible starting point for developing a coherent understanding of this increasingly complex landscape.
title: How Generative Models Generate: A Concise Guide to the Generative AI Landscape

summary: In this paper we investigate the generalization capability of state-of-the-art object detection models (Hi-SAM, YOLO, and RT-DETR) for the automatic segmentation of text lines in historical documents. Generalization is needed because it is not practical for museums and archives to produce large amounts of labeled samples for each new collection.
title: Generalization of Text Line Segmentation for HTR in Historical Documents

summary: We propose a novel view synthesis tool for galaxies based on Gaussian Splatting (GS). Unlike RGB data, where GS has achieved success, galaxy observations consist of multi-band signals from a massive number of bodies, contain complex patterns of cross-band interactions, and capture light propagation in highly heterogeneous media.
title: Multi-Band Galaxy Novel-View Synthesis with Radiative Gaussian Fields

summary: What makes a small trained map from encoder states to the embedding space of a frozen language model sufficient for competitive speech recognition? The premise of the SLAM-ASR architecture is that a frozen language model possesses linguistic knowledge rich enough to perform the recognition task. This assumption, while reasonable, provides little insight into the mechanisms underlying these models.
title: Induction Head Origins of SLAM-ASR Speech Recognition Models

summary: The integration of vision-language models (VLMs) into end-to-end (E2E) autonomous driving has demonstrated strong potential by providing scene description and reasoning capabilities. However, VLMs are computationally expensive, and switching language reasoning on and off at runtime without hurting closed-loop performance has not been demonstrated, which hinders practical adoption.
title: DRIFT: Detachable Reasoning for Runtime-Flexible and Efficient End-to-End Driving

summary: Agents that do science must choose informative experiments and reason from their results, but most discovery benchmarks cannot separate that skill from recall, unstated scoring rules or shortcut policies.
title: Openhagen Worlds: Calibrated Environments for Measuring and Training Scientific Discovery Agents

summary: Artex and similar penetration testing tools allow newbie hackers to scan targeted systems for vulnerabilities and successfully wage attacks using prompts fed to chatbots.
title: Artex Is Criminals’ New Favorite ‘Point-and-Shoot’ AI Hacking Tool

summary: Deployed world-action models (WAMs) can keep improving only if they make good use of their own experience. Existing methods supply retrieved rollouts or demonstrations to the policy as context, yet such experience often turns previously solved tasks into failures. What, then, makes good experience for a WAM?
title: F$^3$: What Makes Good Experience in World-Action Models?

summary: Omni-modal large language models (omni-modal LLMs) can respond to spoken requests directly through voice and video calls. Such requests rely on the scene shared by the user and the assistant, so the same utterance may call for different help or for no response. Most audio-visual benchmarks provide questions as separate text input, and interactive benchmarks mostly score a response as a whole.
title: Can Omni-modal LLMs Understand Spoken Intentions?

summary: Continual pre-training (CPT) is widely used to adapt pretrained language models to dialectal and non-standard language varieties, yet it remains unclear when this additional training is necessary, what drives its benefits, and whether aggregate evaluation scores adequately capture its effects.
title: When Does Continual Pre-Training Help? A Controlled Study of Dialectal Adaptation for Québec French

summary: Reinforcement learning (RL) has become a common approach for training large language model (LLM) agents on long-horizon tasks. However, learning from sparse terminal rewards makes credit assignment and exploration difficult. We approach these challenges through a policy-induced capability region, the set of states from which the current policy can reliably complete a task.
title: Depth Before Breadth: Reverse-to-Forward Curriculum with Advantage Decomposition for LLM Agent

summary: Semantic 3D mapping is a powerful representation that enables platform agnostic mobile robot navigation in challenging offroad conditions. Current vision foundation models can accurately predict semantics zero-shot on structured scenes but performance is compromised in natural environments.
title: Improving Zero-shot 3D Semantic Mapping in Offroad with Geometric Priors

summary: Nvidia founder and former CEO Jensen Huang stepped down last week amid several scandals, including an affair with an alleged Chinese spy.
title: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman says it’s ‘hard to imagine the AI industry without Jensen’

summary: Widely used category discovery benchmarks have become increasingly saturated and often fail to reflect real-world discovery settings, making long-term evaluation of new methods difficult.
title: Predicting Species Splits: A Challenging Fine-Grained Benchmark for Category Discovery

summary: The AI detection tool Pangram flags 99 percent of a prize-winning Peruvian novel as AI-generated, but Mexican publisher Almadía is standing by the award after its own review. Pangram also classified over 80 percent of the author's personal texts as machine-written.
title: Pangram flags 99 percent of an award-winning Peruvian novel as AI-generated, but the publisher stands by its author

summary: Hugging Face’s harness-hub team has released Qwen3.8-27B-pi-adapted , a LoRA adapter for Qwen3.8-27B . It was trained with reinforcement learning to work inside the pi coding agent . The Qwen3.8-27B-pi-adapted LoRA adapter targets one harness instead of general chat.
title: New LoRA Adapter Lifts Qwen3.8 Coding Success From 39% to 65%

summary: During the time these agents converted 185,000 lines of C code into 340,000 lines of Rust code (I counted), we merged over 300 commits in the actual curl project. We actually improved curl during these a little more than three weeks. A little over 200 bugfixes actually.
title: Quoting Daniel Stenberg

summary: Small language models (SLMs) can run on commodity hardware and support privacy-preserving, on-premises clinical deployment, but their medical explanations are often short and poorly structured compared with large language models.
title: Self-Rewarded Reinforcement Learning for Better-Structured Medical Explanations in Small Language Models

summary: This paper presents the development of an initial full-vehicle simulation model of the PixKit modular electric test platform in IPG CarMaker. The objective is to create a physics-based and extendable model structure that can serve as a low-level foundation for future digital twin applications.
title: Conceptual full-vehicle modeling of a modular all-wheel-drive robotic ADS test platform as a foundation for a digital twin architecture

summary: Zero-Shot Multimodal Anomaly Detection (ZSMAD) aims to identify both appearance and geometric defects in novel categories without relying on target-specific training data, making it especially valuable in real-world scenarios constrained by data scarcity, privacy concerns, or high annotation costs.
title: AggCLIP: Aggregating CLIP for Zero-Shot Multimodal Anomaly Detection

summary: Multimodal language models for materials science rely on effective mechanisms for incorporating three-dimensional structural representations. MatterChat addresses this challenge using a large bridge module between a pretrained structural encoder and the LLM, together with a separate contrastive alignment stage.
title: Choosing the Right Representations: Task-Aware Fusion for Multimodal Materials Language Models

summary: A Vals AI investigation shows that leading AI models from Anthropic, OpenAI and Google have almost no safeguards against use in autonomous weapons systems. In tests, the models readily flagged civilians as military targets, and a simple video game framing in the prompt was enough to override even belated refusals.
title: Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google models readily marked medics, journalists, and surrendering soldiers as kamikaze drone targets

summary: Continual learning (CL) enables neural networks to adapt to non-stationary data streams by mitigating catastrophic forgetting, offering a path to robust, private, and adaptable edge devices.
title: Hypnos: A Dual-Phase End-to-End Platform for Scalable Continual Learning at the Edge

summary: We introduce Clover-35B-A3B-Preview (Clover), a mixture-of-experts diffusion language model with 35 billion total parameters and 3 billion activated parameters, supporting thinking-mode generation. Clover adapts Gated Delta Networks to block diffusion by combining recurrent memory of previously generated context with bidirectional softmax attention inside the current block.
title: Clover-35B-A3B-Preview Technical Report

summary: Inspired by seminal work by E.M. Purcell, we discuss the problem of predicting and optimizing the performance of autonomous robots swimming in confinement. Our approach is based on the explicit numerical resolution of the fluid flow induced by the swimmer, and it is validated experimentally on a cm-size prototype composed of a cargo head and a rotating propulsive tail.
title: Hydrodynamics of robotic micro-swimmers in confinement

summary: This summer, OpenAI paused its largest planned frontier training run after its AI agents accidentally hacked Hugging Face and early evidence suggested that its next model could independently find and exploit security flaws.
title: Remember the frontier AI pause? Chip companies don’t either

summary: During human cortical development, functional systems become increasingly differentiated. We asked whether improved reasoning in language models involves a comparable regional reorganization.
title: Transferring an analysis of human brain organization to language models

summary: Chain-of-Thought (CoT) prompting improves the performance of Large Language Models by eliciting intermediate reasoning steps. However, CoT is far from perfect: on some tasks, models perform worse than with direct-answer prompting, and on others they generate a few hundred tokens to reach the correct answer.
title: Chain-of-Thought Hidden States Reveal Task-Solving Directions for Direct Answers

summary: This research investigates whether a large language model or an autonomous AI Agent performs better at translating from English to Arabic, which is considered a low-resource language.
title: Large Language Models or AI Agents for English to Arabic Translation? An assessment on WikiEn-Ar190

summary: Egocentric human recordings are far cheaper than dexterous robot demonstrations, promising stronger pretraining and direct skill learning without task-specific robot data. Yet humans and robots differ in morphology and kinematics, so human recordings lack the joint positions and actuator commands that supervise robot policies, providing only retargeted end-effector (EEF) actions.
title: SHAPE: Discrete Supervision and Parallel Continuous Streams for Learning Dexterous Manipulation from Egocentric Human Data

summary: Visual foundation models provide powerful representations for diverse tasks, but their features become stale as visual content changes between image observations. Refreshing them requires new frames and repeated runs of a computationally expensive image encoder. We introduce ALIVE, an event-based method that incrementally updates native foundation model features between image observations.
title: ALIVE: Bring Foundation Features to Life with Events

summary: Manifold-constrained Hyper-Connections (mHC) extend a Transformer's residual stream into multiple parallel streams with learned cross-stream connections. Prior work trains all streams toward a shared objective. We instead study whether assigning distinct learning objectives to different streams can improve task performance and induce objective-specific specialization.
title: Objective-Specialized Residual Streams in Manifold-Constrained Hyper-Connections

summary: Thomas Nagel has done landmark work on consciousness in nonhumans; this week, he won the million-dollar Berggruen Prize for his contributions to the field. And he has a lot of thoughts on AI.
title: ‘Just Ridiculous’: A Famed Philosopher Takes on AI Consciousness

summary: Real-time forecasting, anomaly detection, and optimization, powered by IBM time-series models with more than 50 million downloads. Now available natively on Confluent, in the cloud and on premises, running on CPUs.
title: Time-Series Models in the Streamhouse: A New Frontier and Use Cases

summary: Training a next-generation machine learning interatomic potential (MLIP) requires ground truth: tens to hundreds of millions of density functional theory (DFT).
title: Tackling GPU Bottlenecks in Plane-Wave DFT with K-Point Batching and Mixed Precision

summary: Visuomotor policies have demonstrated that imprecise low-cost robots can autonomously complete complex manipulation tasks. However, most inexpensive manipulators rely on compact and rigidly position-controlled servos for actuation, which complicate simulation, operation, and safety.
title: TinyARM-X: A Series of Open-Source, Configurable, and Transparent Torque-Controlled Desktop-Scale Robotic Manipulators

summary: Building a small language model requires choosing which published improvements to combine. We compare five changes in the same model, using the same data and training budget. We test selected combinations and repeat each one with a second random seed. Mixture-of-experts layers, Muon optimisation and a Gated DeltaNet hybrid give the largest gains.
title: Do Frontier Model Ingredients Add Up? A Replicated Factorial Study of Small Language Models

summary: Patient history taking is a strategic, multi-turn process that refines diagnostic hypotheses through iterative questioning, mirroring clinical reasoning where each inquiry updates beliefs over candidate diagnoses. Deploying AI in this setting is constrained by privacy, cost, and latency, making Small Language Models (SLMs) a more desirable backbone compared to larger LLMs.
title: ProbMedTOD: A Bayesian Network Guided Task-Oriented Dialogue System for Patient History Taking

summary: Like a nasty rash, AI seems to spread everywhere. Google crams AI Overviews down your throat even though it costs the company billions of dollars in lost ad revenue. Leave your apartment, and you might pass two people heaving an AI-powered humanoid robot up the stairs to clean someone’s rooms.
title: The AI Hype Index: AI is everywhere

summary: Mistral's AI agent Vibe now has its own desktop app. The article Mistral plays catch-up with Vibe Desktop as rivals already command full operating systems appeared first on The Decoder .
title: Mistral plays catch-up with Vibe Desktop as rivals already command full operating systems

summary: Multimodal Entity Linking (MEL) aims to disambiguate mentions in multimodal contexts by grounding them to specific entities in a knowledge base. A pivotal challenge in MEL is capturing multi-level correspondences: the semantic consistency between mention-entity pairs and the complementary correlations across modalities.
title: MECI: Multi-Element Collaborative Interaction for Multimodal Entity Linking

summary: OpenAI is giving four independent audit organizations, including Apollo Research and METR, direct access to unreleased models, source code, and training data for the first time. The embedded reviews are designed to uncover hidden misbehavior and safety gaps.
title: OpenAI opens its AI systems to four independent on-site auditors for the first time

summary: In this work, we introduce OmniFish, a bioinspired modular soft robotic fish designed to emulate the full spectrum of body and/or caudal fin (BCF) locomotion modes within a single robotic platform. The design combines morphology averaging across representative fish species with a tendon-driven compliant segmented spine whose effective stiffness can be reconfigured through progressive mechanical jamming.
title: OmniFish: A Bioinspired, Modular, Reconfigurable Soft Robotic Fish Enabling Multi-Modal Swimming

summary: Hugging Face now routes language model requests through OpenRouter, which automatically selects the cheapest or fastest provider. Bring-your-own API keys for language models are going away. According to OpenRouter, the new routing cut capacity errors by 46 percent. Both partners face multibillion-dollar acquisitions.
title: Hugging Face now routes model requests through OpenRouter for the best price or speed

summary: Robot learning systems require synchronized, high-quality demonstrations that combine visual, proprioceptive, and action data. However, collecting such datasets with mobile manipulators is often slowed down by fragmented teleoperation interfaces and manual post-processing workflows.
title: Single-Controller Teleoperation and Multimodal Dataset Generation for a Mobile Manipulator

summary: A Harvard study published in Nature Sustainability found that 403 US hyperscale data centers produced roughly 25.7 million metric tons of CO2 between May 2024 and April 2025, more than all of Denmark. Over half of their electricity came from fossil fuels.
title: More than half the electricity feeding America's largest data centers comes from gas and coal

summary: Vision-language-action policies control embodied agents through a perception-action loop grounded in physical interaction, where adversarial patches can corrupt action predictions and thereby alter subsequent observations. To mitigate these threats, many existing defenses rely on policy adaptation or auxiliary models, but require additional training or inference.
title: RECLAIM: Robot-Vision-Informed Adversarial Patch Defense via Embodied Attention Feedback

summary: Recent research suggests that individual neurons can have interpretable roles in AI behaviour. In Qwen3.5-4B, steering along one neuron's output direction increased decisions to conceal information more in teams than alone across five scenarios, even when teammates provided no messages.
title: Nothing to Declare: Steering a single neuron increases concealment in AI teams

summary: Planning with a visual world model requires deciding both which actions to execute and how long to search for them. We introduce Selective CEM Refinement (SCR), a learned rule for deciding whether to continue cross-entropy method (CEM) search with a frozen LeWorldModel.
title: When to Refine: Selective Search for Frozen Visual World Models

summary: Vision-language-action (VLA) policies implicitly assume that third-person cameras remain fixed at their data-collection poses; once a camera is bumped, remounted, or swapped at deployment, task success degrades precipitously even though the underlying task and robot remain unchanged.
title: Homeward: No Place Like the Training View

summary: New NVIDIA RTX Spark compact desktops from ASUS, Dell and MSI are available today, bringing local AI agents, image and video generation, and model fine-tuning to a dedicated Windows PC.
title: NVIDIA RTX Spark Compact Desktops Out Now

coverage.title: Will Wright's next simulation will use AI to mine content from your memories

summary: Will Wright, the creator of legendary franchises like SimCity and The Sims, is working on a new game - and it's built around AI. The new title, focused on your memories, is called MyMems. Like Wright's other titles, it sounds extremely ambitious, giving players a new way to explore worlds they create on their own. [. ]
title: Will Wright’s next game uses AI to map your memories

summary: KPMG deployed more than 100 AI agents alongside the regular audit of a UK-listed company. The agents asked "better questions" than the audit team in some cases, according to UK head of audit Cath Burnet.
title: KPMG's "Project Exponential" put AI agents alongside a real audit team and found the bots dug deeper on individual questions

summary: Guidance vector fields (GVFs) are a popular framework for tasks such as robotic path-following and multi-robot motion coordination, but existing approaches may be non-differentiable or have large derivatives, limiting their use in controllers that require derivatives of the guidance signal, which is common when the GVF is used as an input in a cascaded controller.
title: Constructive Infinitely Differentiable Guidance Vector Fields for Robotic Control

summary: High-quality causal reasoning datasets are essential for developing models with reliable causal understanding, particularly in specialized domains. However, existing datasets frequently suffer from incorrect annotations and structural imbalances, which can lead to biased predictions and limited generalization.
title: CaDO: Formal Verification-Guided Multi-Agent Framework for Causal Dataset Repair and Generation

summary: Judgements of sexism are subjective and may vary across communities, yet sexism detection datasets usually reduce annotator judgements to a single majority label, obscuring disagreement and how models behave on contested cases. We introduce MuDAS, a dataset of YouTube comments in Saudi, Egyptian and Moroccan Arabic, each labelled by three native speakers of its dialect, with the individual annotations preserved.
title: What Majority Labels Hide: Annotator Disagreement and Model Errors in Multi-Dialect Arabic Sexism Detection

summary: AI agents read their whole history at every step. People do not work like that: we keep what the moment needs and hold the rest as a rough note we can recall. MoE-Context applies this to language models. The context is split into blocks. Before each step a fast yes or no pass decides which blocks the step needs; the rest stay as one-line notes that can be brought back, and nothing is deleted.
title: MoE-Context: Show the Model Only What It Needs

summary: End-to-end autonomous driving systems have been shown to suffer from shortcut learning and causal confusion, limiting their ability to generalize robustly under distribution shift. To mitigate these limitations, recent works based on Vision-Language Models (VLMs) have explored incorporating linguistic reasoning capabilities into driving decision-making, reporting improvements in driving performance.
title: Teaching VLMs What to Say, Not How to Reason: Rethinking Counterfactual Reasoning in Autonomous Driving

summary: Object search in unknown environments requires robots to gather useful observations while avoiding obstacles and accounting for limited sensor visibility. We present SearchDiffusion, a diffusion-based planner that generates position and heading trajectories using a learned dense utility map. The map represents geometric accessibility, useful visibility, and semantic progress.
title: SearchDiffusion: Information-Guided Diffusion Planning for Object Search

summary: Nvidia has stopped sending its advanced AI chips to China despite the approval it received from the White House to do so in December last year.
title: Nvidia isn’t selling any more AI chips to China

summary: As Axiom Math ’s AI swarm was putting the final touches on the automatic verification of 15,000-page proof of the Classification of Finite Simple Groups (CFSG) , colloquially referred to as the ‘enormous theorem’, on Sunday 25 October, the company’s Founding Mathematician Ken Ono had nothing to do but watch and…
title: Startup Makes Headway Towards Formalizing All of Math With AI

summary: If Nvidia is backstopping a data center loan, it won't be on the hook unless the neocould has independent financing and gets the facility built, with Nvidia gear installed, interim CEO Colette Kress explained.
title: Nvidia clarifies when it will — and won’t — keep financing neoclouds

summary: Fine-tuning a vision-language-action (VLA) model on a few dozen demonstrations is the standard way to put a manipulation policy on a robot, yet the resulting policy silently assumes that the camera and the robot base stay exactly where they were during data collection: a bumped tripod or a base re-docked a few centimetres away makes it reach for the wrong place.
title: Towards Pose-Robust Few-Shot Vision-Language-Action Models

summary: Building autonomous agents that continually explore open worlds and acquire new capabilities through experience is a long-standing aspiration in artificial intelligence.
