Behavioral evaluations show that language-model predictions largely conform to the proposed hypothesis.
title: Polarity Composition Hypothesis: Causal Evidence from Negation in NLI

summary: Preference optimization (PO) is the standard way to reduce object hallucination in large vision-language models. We find that four public PO checkpoints of LLaVA-1.5-7B also lower object coverage. They name fewer object categories, and their lower hallucination rates bring no significant gain in set-level object F1 on CHAIR. We therefore ask how much of the PO gain the base model can reproduce by stopping earlier.
title: Say Less, Hallucinate Less? Diagnosing and Restoring Object Coverage in Preference-Optimized Vision-Language Models

summary: A working-memory model must remember stimuli and use its memory flexibly to perform different tasks. Here we introduce a model of working memory for images that combines dynamic activity with temporary associations between image features.
title: Déjà View: A Shared Working-Memory Model for Visual Tasks

summary: Empirical research is changing rapidly as AI coding agents are becoming increasingly proficient in every step of it, from writing code to manipulating data. We argue that while the potential of coding agents for science is vast, their use in hypothesis testing poses a substantial threat to classical inference, as these agents enable a supercharged form of selective inference.
title: Inference after coding agents

summary: Networks that predict angles, gaze directions, and rotations do not output these quantities directly: they emit raw coordinates that a fixed decoder, such as normalization, maps to the final prediction. Attribution methods are usually applied to the raw coordinates, so they can credit inputs for changes the decoder discards, such as rescaling a vector when only its direction matters.
title: Attribution Through the Decoder: Prediction-Space Explanations for Structured Outputs

summary: Routed low-rank adapters offer a parameter-efficient means to improve the performance of large language models (LLMs) across tasks. Hence, it is assumed that they can also be used to improve the support of low-resource languages in LLMs, which currently serve English far better than the thousands of other languages spoken worldwide.
title: MoE--LoRA Methods for Multilingual Adaptation: A Systematic Empirical Study

summary: November 17, 2026 Category: AI . Microsoft and Salesforce Announce Copilotforce, Bringing Trusted Customer Context and Action into Microsoft AI Experiences .
title: Microsoft and Salesforce Announce Copilotforce, Bringing Trusted Customer Context and Action into Microsoft AI Experiences

summary: Sqwish Labs has a new wrinkle on the decision model: Train it with your own data to max its capabilities.
title: As decision model use skyrockets, is customization the next frontier?

summary: Recent advances in text-to-image generation have substantially improved image quality, particularly through diffusion-based methods that require multiple inference steps. In contrast, Sphere Encoder offers an efficient generative framework capable of producing images with fewer forward steps. However, extending it to free-form text is nontrivial, because its class-conditioned design lacks cross-modal alignment.
title: TextSphere: Efficient Text-to-Image Generation via Shared Hyperspherical Alignment and Uniformity

summary: Across industries, decision-making starts with understanding what is changing and why. Industrial organizations collect data that informs decisions across their operations.
title: Reason over time-series data with OpenTSLM on Amazon SageMaker JumpStart

summary: Inference-time scaling improves the performance of large language models by sampling multiple responses and evaluating their collective utility. However, many existing approaches obtain these samples by repeatedly sampling from a single policy. In this work, we study if the sample budget at inference time can instead be allocated across a population of policies.
title: Learning Stratified Policies for Inference-Time Objectives

summary: Video question answering under tight frame budgets requires preserving localized motion and event order, yet current video multimodal large language models (MLLMs) reduce comprehension to static multi-image reasoning by discarding unselected frames and encoding keyframes independently: (1) Spatially, whole-frame pooling dilutes small moving targets into static backgrounds; (2) Temporally, dropping intermediate…
title: VIVID: Beyond Static Multi-Image Reasoning with Localized Visual Differences and Textual Entity Dynamics in Video MLLMs

summary: The company uses agentic AI to make supply chains faster and more reliable.
title: Pedestal AI raises $4.7 million to agentify the supply chain

summary: The agents in a heterogeneous team can cooperate to accomplish tasks that exceed their individual capabilities. The team trajectories for a cooperative task can be generated by a generative model, provided that the model has been trained on demonstrations of the agents cooperating. Yet, demonstrations of cooperation are costly and may not exist for tasks that the team has never performed.
title: Capability Composition in Heterogeneous Teams via Barrier-Guided Diffusion Sampling

summary: The "AI revolution" has enabled teams across the technology industry to deliver software features at unprecedented velocity. While code evolves faster than ever, customer-facing documentation often struggles to stay up to speed.
title: Mind the Gap: A Deployed Multi-Agent System for Documentation Maintenance

summary: Visual foundation models are central to physical intelligence, yet their development remains constrained by fragmented training datasets, inconsistent annotation quality, and limited multimodal supervision. To address these challenges, we introduce GameRealm, a large-scale, richly annotated dataset that grounds visual observations in synchronized, game-native supervision.
title: GameRealm: Grounding Visual Learning in Interactive Games

summary: Enabling large language models (LLMs) to autonomously conduct training and improve target models is an important foundation for recursive self-improvement (RSI). As LLMs expand their role from being trained to conducting training, their model-training capability warrants dedicated study and systematic development.
title: RSI-Prime: Training Models to Train Models

summary: Flow matching models, ODE-based generative models, generate samples by gradually morphing a simple source distribution into a target distribution. However, these models still face challenges in optimally balancing computational efficiency with generation fidelity.
title: Correcting Flows with Marginal Matching

summary: Urban air mobility arises to mitigate ground traffic congestion. Multidisciplinary analysis and optimization (MDAO) has been introduced to reduce the energy consumption, thereby expanding aircraft performance. Surrogate-based MDAO lowers the cost of optimization, but multimodality disrupts global optimum search for both simulation-based and surrogate-based optimizations.
title: A Neural Envelope Method for Rapid Gradient-based Optimum Takeoff Trajectory Design

summary: Advection-diffusion priors are a common way to make neural sea surface temperature (SST) forecasts physics-informed.
title: Where Should Physics Enter? Information, Identifiability and Calibration in Probabilistic Sea Surface Temperature Forecasting

summary: Retrieval-augmented vision-language models (VLMs) answer from two sources of evidence that can each fail: the retrieved text can be wrong or noisy, and the image can be degraded or contradicted.
title: The Illusion of Grounding: Do Vision-Language Models Weigh Retrieved Text and Images Like an Ideal Observer?

coverage.title: OpenAI launches GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol with lower API prices and some benchmark gains
OpenAI Releases GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol With a 20% Cheaper Astra API
GPT‐6.2 Astra and GPT‐6.2 Sol

summary: Introducing GPT‐6.2 Astra and Sol, with better professional outputs, coding, computer use, and efficiency at lower cost across ChatGPT Work, Codex, and the API.
title: Introducing GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol

summary: More historical data can improve estimation while introducing relationships that transfer poorly to current market conditions. We therefore examine how training quantity and historical selection interact with forecast horizon in intraday equity prediction.
title: Which Past Matters? Training History and Multi-Forecast Horizon in Equity Transformers

summary: GRPO has become the dominant reinforcement learning method for eliciting reasoning capability in LLMs using verifiable rewards. However, it suffers from a fundamental failure mode: when a training question exceeds the base model's current capability, all generated responses fail and receive zero reward, yielding no gradient signal and stalling further capability expansion.
title: Get Hint-Augmented GRPO Done Right Through Activation Steering

summary: While gravity is often used in mobile robotics as a global constraint for Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM) algorithms, most estimation methods rely on indirect observation of the gravity vector. In this paper, we propose the use of altimeter measurements to directly observe the direction of the gravity vector.
title: Pressure Drop: Gravity Vector Estimation from a Distributed Barometric Pressure Sensor Array

summary: Effective multi-agent collaboration requires agents to adapt task allocation as goals and responsibilities evolve. Prior task-allocation frameworks often assume static goals, full observability, or rely on large language models (LLMs) without explicit, verifiable beliefs about task allocation or intent.
title: Dynamic Task Allocation with Dialogue

summary: A legged robot can learn to walk inside a learned simulator: a neural network that predicts the robot's next state and is run forward on its own predictions. They are usually trained and checked one step ahead, although a policy uses them for a hundred steps or more.
title: Auditing a Learned Simulator for Legged Robots: The Robotic World Model on ANYmal D

summary: Identifying whom a person looks at is central to understanding multi-party conversations, yet gaze geometry alone becomes ambiguous as more people appear. Conversations offer cues that geometry lacks, such as who is speaking and what is said, but no gaze dataset provides them for many multi-party scenes.
title: Nunchi: Ears Help Eyes in Multi-Party Conversations

summary: Photographic color grading shapes the tone and color of a photograph to achieve a desired look. Text-driven photographic look transfer lets users specify these adjustments in natural language, with the goal of reproducing the requested look across photographs while preserving their content.
title: LUTBench: Benchmarking Text-Driven Photographic Look Transfer

summary: What reusable units of computation can we discover within a language model's neurons? Prior work has shown that individual forward passes can often be sparsified post-hoc to small groups of neurons, but it has been unclear whether these groups form coherent computational entities reused across inputs.
title: Large-scale Neuron Community Discovery Reveals Neuron-Sparse Behaviors in Language Models

summary: Proton's new Lumo Desktop app for Windows, Mac, and Linux lets users automate tasks across files and connected apps, with granular controls over what its AI can access.
title: Proton’s Lumo, a privacy-focused alternative to ChatGPT and Claude, arrives on desktop

summary: Event cameras offer high temporal resolution and low power consumption, making them promising for speech-related applications. These include automatic lip reading, audiovisual speech analysis, and human-robot interaction, particularly in challenging environments characterized by low illumination or high dynamic range.
title: Event-Based Dynamic Lip Region Estimation During Speech

summary: Agentic workloads, long documents, and large codebases are pushing context lengths from tens of thousands of tokens to hundreds of thousands. At those lengths,.
title: Co-Designing Sparse Attention for Efficient Long-Context Inference

summary: Generative Artificial Intelligence is transforming the role of natural language in computational systems. In classical Natural Language Processing (NLP), language was treated as an object of computation: something to analyse, classify, translate, or generate.
title: Natural Language Programming: Rethinking Language, Memory, and Cognition in the Era of Generative AI

summary: Model-based quadruped controllers usually step on a cyclic gait, which lifts the legs in a fixed order on a fixed period, wherever the safe footholds are. We present CADENCE, a learned step planner with a small action space. Every 40 ms, it picks one of at most 65 discrete choices: no step, or one leg's step to a safe foothold. It also predicts a swing time.
title: CADENCE: Learning Acyclic Gaits for Model-Based Quadruped Locomotion

summary: Vals, a San Francisco-based AI evaluation startup, tested whether leading AI models could be manipulated into participating in autonomous warfare. They usually compiled.
title: AI models can be tricked into identifying civilians as military targets by telling them it’s a game

summary: Fine-tuning on narrow harmful tasks can cause emergent misalignment, where models generalize harmful behavior beyond the training distribution. Inoculation prompting can reduce this effect by explicitly eliciting the undesired behavior during training, but recent work shows that the behavior can reappear when evaluation prompts contain cues from the training context.
title: Hidden-State Similarity Predicts Re-Elicitation After Inoculation Prompting

summary: Hierarchical models have been proposed as synthetic settings for studying language. However, their relevance to realistic language corpora remains underexplored.
title: What's in a Tree ? Hierarchical $n$-gram models as controlled approximators of language

summary: AI-assisted RTL localization and debugging need ground-truth bug datasets with known locations and observable failures, while testbench grading uses injected bugs to measure detection capability. Creating such datasets at scale remains a major EDA challenge. BugGen 1.0 shows that Large Language Models (LLMs) can generate context-aware RTL mutations.
title: BugGen 2.0: Rethinking the Roles of LLMs for Scalable RTL Bug Synthesis

summary: Maritime search and rescue requires locating people in the water quickly, motivating the use of UAVs to survey the search area. During flight, camera motion and the longer exposures used in low light can blur small targets and hinder person detection. Event cameras record brightness changes as they occur, reducing the motion blur associated with longer exposure times.
title: Event-Based Person Detection for Maritime UAV Search

summary: Audio-visual question answering on lightweight user devices requires balancing speed, memory usage, privacy, and communication. One approach is to run audio-visual encoders on a server and a lightweight language decoder on the user device, keeping questions local while offloading media encoding. However, transferring and processing the full multimodal representation remains costly.
title: Transfer Once, Ask Locally: Compact Audio-Visual Memory for On-Device Question Answering

summary: AWS Quick is the AI workspace built only for work, where the dashboards, agents, and automations one person creates are available to everyone on the team. Built on AWS with enterprise security and governance from the start, Quick connects to the data and applications you use every day.
title: Your complete guide to AWS Quick at AWS re:Invent 2026

summary: Transfer learning in reinforcement learning (RL) has shown strong empirical success. In this work, we take a more principled perspective by studying when and how transferring knowledge between MDPs (a source and a target) can be provably beneficial. Specifically, we consider the case where there exists an undo map such that applying this map to the target's state space recovers the source exactly.
title: Learning to Undo: Transfer Reinforcement Learning under State Space Transformations

summary: Science advances from frontier to frontier as discoveries reshape what is known and create the basis for further discovery. We present Colombo, a self-organizing AI researcher that drives this renewal, first instantiated in oracle-based optimization. Here, the central question is how efficiently a problem class can be solved through a prescribed information interface and what costs no admissible algorithm can avoid.
title: Colombo: A Frontier-to-Frontier Autoresearch System for Oracle-Based Optimization

summary: Event-based cameras provide high temporal resolution, low power consumption, and a high dynamic range, but progress in event-based object detection remains constrained by the scarcity of annotated training data. To solve this issue, this paper introduces the tool UnrealEvent, a synthetic dataset-generation pipeline implemented in Unreal Engine 5.5.
title: UnrealEvent: Synthetic Dataset Generation and Annotation for Event-Based Vision

summary: Many real-world planning applications, from logistics, routing to resource allocation, give rise to optimization problems that need to balance multiple, conflicting objectives. While machine learning is often used to predict the unknown parameters or costs of these problems, standard models trained on prediction accuracy can lead to suboptimal plans.
title: Pareto-Informed Smart "Predict, then Optimize" for Multi-Objective Combinatorial Problems

summary: This post is co-written with Mariah Miller from AWS and Colin Terry from LoanPro . Have you ever wondered what the experience is like for the person on the other end of the phone when you call your bank for support?
title: How LoanPro built an agentic AI loan servicing assistant with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore

summary: AI agents are governed by hundreds of natural language criteria, yet existing verifiers cannot efficiently evaluate an agent's output against a large set of such criteria and report which are satisfied, violated, or inapplicable.
title: Runtime Verification of Multiple Natural Language Criteria for Agent Governance

summary: Quantum processors are being integrated into supercomputing centers worldwide. National programs in North America, Europe, and Asia are driving the installation.
title: Integrating QPUs into Supercomputing Centers Using Slurm HRES Plugins

summary: Tasks in Gemini is now free of charge in six countries, with new features starting in the U.S. and deeper Google Workspace integration to get things done on your behalf.
title: Put Gemini to work for you

summary: Learning a neural sampler can reduce the cost of repeated sampling from an un-normalized distribution, but obtaining good training data remains difficult. We develop a corrected self-training scheme across a sequence of tempered targets, making use of importance sampling and Markov chain Monte Carlo to correct the samples and replay buffers to store them.
title: Amortizing Tempered Sampling with Corrected Self-Training

summary: Household robots often need to operate appliances, and smart appliances offer both control panels and device APIs. Existing embodied AI simulation environments, however, model appliances solely as physical objects. We introduce PAIR, a smart-home simulation environment grounded in the Matter protocol~\footnote{https://csa-iot.org/all-solutions/matter/}, the industry standard for smart-home devices.
title: PAIR: Bringing Household Robots into the Smart Home

summary: Agent evolution follows a simple loop: a proposer writes candidate artifacts (prompts, skills, memories) and selection accepts those that score higher. This loop has shown promise, yet practitioners face a puzzle: methods trade wins across papers, and evolution often fails to bootstrap on certain tasks.
title: The Resolution Hypothesis: Agent Evolution's Key Is Identifying Improvements

summary: Self-improving agents are typically optimized for the results they produce, with less attention to how they produce them. Their instructions give designers limited ways to shape how they work, especially when the task is open-ended. This paper studies whether a short value statement in an agent's persistent instruction file changes not only how well the agent performs but also what it builds.
title: Values Shape What Self-Improving Coding Agents Build

summary: Companies build agentic AI platforms to govern the applications, tools, skills, models, and storage that agents use. The nondeterministic nature of generative AI models introduces a complexity that previous software development practices didn’t anticipate.
title: Responsible AI for agentic AI: A phased roadmap for platform and application teams

summary: OpenAI wants GPT-6 Astra and GPT-6 Luna to automate administrative tasks in US healthcare through computer-use agents that operate existing clinic software and insurance portals the way a human would. Luna handles tasks like prior authorizations for about 8.5 cents each.
title: AI agents are starting to fill out medical forms and file insurance requests in place of human staff

summary: Efficient control of underfloor heating (UFH) systems coupled with heat pumps (HPs) is challenging due to the high thermal inertia of buildings and the slow dynamic response of UFH systems. Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) offers a data-driven control approach capable of simultaneously optimizing energy consumption and thermal comfort.
title: Deep Reinforcement Learning for Heat Pump and Underfloor Heating Control: An End-to-End Case Study

authors: Doug Burger, Ava Amini, Eric Horvitz, Dr. Eric Topol

summary: Technical advancement is moving at such a rapid pace that it can be challenging to define the tomorrow we’re working toward.
title: Can AI help build a healthier future?

summary: It can be hard to use Google products—or even the Internet itself—without coming into contact with Gemini AI. That is, of course, by design . The more you use Gemini, the more data Google collects to train and improve its generative AI chatbot.
title: Google makes it easier to use Gemini without training AI on your data

summary: Large-scale robotic simulation requires diverse deformable objects with executable physical properties and realistic interaction behaviors. However, existing 3D asset collections primarily emphasize visual diversity, while scalable physical construction and verification remain challenging.
title: RFW-S: Everyday Deformable Objects with Independent Simulation Verification

summary: LLM-based multi-agent systems (MAS) rely on not only individual agent behaviors but also the interactions that connect agents, including message exchanges and task dependencies. Existing MAS safeguards mainly perform agent-level anomaly detection, which becomes insufficient when failures originate from agent interactions and detected anomalies do not necessarily reveal their true sources.
title: TRACE-MAS: Diagnosing and Repairing Collaboration Failures in Multi-Agent Systems

summary: Long-video question answering benchmarks like Video-MME-v2 typically evaluate systems under a uniform frame budget for every question, despite stark variation in the evidence each query actually demands. We analyze this mismatch on Video-MME-v2 and find that different question subsets prefer different frozen frame-budget policies, while uniformly increasing the frame count does not reliably improve all metrics.
title: FrameRouter: Frame Budget Routing for Long-Video Understanding on Video-MME-v2 and Beyond

summary: Datasette Lite is my port of the Datasette Python application to run directly in the browser using WebAssembly and Pyodide . I've released a complete rewrite of Datasette Lite using service workers, and it's now almost indistinguishable from the real server-side application.
title: Running the full server-side Datasette Python app in the browser with service workers and Pyodide

summary: 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) enables photorealistic scene reconstruction. Existing 3DGS color transfer and interactive editing methods are guided by reference images and user-specified color adjustments. However, in many applications, users simply want aesthetically guided color enhancement that automatically makes the scene more visually appealing while maintaining consistent colors and tones across viewpoints.
title: ReTouchGS: Ultralight Render-free Aesthetic Color Enhancement and Transfer for 3D Gaussian Splatting

summary: The US is tightening its chip export controls. Data centers in third countries like Singapore and Malaysia will soon need a US license to buy Nvidia chips, closing the loophole that let Chinese firms rent cloud compute abroad.
title: The US wants to block China from renting AI power abroad but China already built a parallel supply chain from US AI output

summary: Feed-forward 3D reconstruction models predict dense point maps from multiple images in a single pass. Without explicit geometric constraints, however, their predictions are often inconsistent across views and lack fine-grained precision.
title: Refin3R: Geometry-Guided Refinement for Feed-Forward 3D Reconstruction

summary: Magnetic levitation with six-degrees-of-freedom enables frictionless transport and micrometer-scale positioning in principle, but low-level control is inherently challenging due to its complex and unstable dynamics.
title: Magflow: Differentiable Simulation of Industrial-Grade 6D Magnetic Levitation

summary: Global canopy height maps are increasingly used to estimate forest carbon, yet their regional accuracy is rarely tested. We present wall-to-wall maps of canopy height (10~m) and aboveground carbon density (30~m) for the Brazilian Atlantic Forest in 2024.
title: Wall-to-wall maps of canopy height and aboveground carbon across the Atlantic Forest

summary: Agents built on large language models (LLMs) increasingly forecast real-world events by searching the Web and reasoning over what they find. How well such an agent forecasts depends on both the retrieved evidence and the model, making control over that evidence essential for evaluation.
title: ForecastGym: A Live, Controlled, and Replayable Benchmark for Forecasting Agents

summary: In the global attention layers of Gemma 4 31B, the value is the normalized key projection, and the key is the value scaled by a fixed weight, with rotary position encoding on one quarter of its dimensions. The Gemma 4 report states that this design reduces the global KV cache by up to 37.5%, but the open serving engines that we checked still store a full key and a full value: 1,024 values per KV head and token.
title: Storing the Gemma 4 K=V Cache Once: Exact Global-KV Memory Savings in a Paged Serving Engine with Unchanged Attention Kernels

summary: Not every perception error changes the planner's action. Yet adaptive-resolution perception chooses where to spend high-resolution computation from image cues, which can neither reliably point to an object that low resolution missed nor tell which objects matter to the planner.
title: Check Your Blind Spots: Decision-Guided Perception by Probing the Planner with Hypothetical Objects

summary: Daydream's new AI shopping agent can remember your style, virtually try on clothes, plan outfits around your wardrobe, track sales, and complete purchases.
title: Daydream’s new AI agent acts as your personal stylist — and can shop for you, too

summary: Signal Temporal Logic is a popular framework for describing a robotic system's goals. Once described using a temporal logic framework, synthesis turns the goals into actual steps for the robots to follow.
title: Satisfiability Modulo Theories for Robust Synthesis of Signal Temporal Logic Specifications

summary: The Justice and Commerce Departments said that they are investigating Megaspeed, the Singapore-based data center company intertwined with the resignation of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, after reporting suggested an investigation had been halted last year.
title: The DOJ says it’s investigating Megaspeed

summary: In automated driving, world models provide future scene predictions for evaluating candidate trajectories, but fixed selection rules may not capture scene-dependent trade-offs. We propose a residual-guided reinforcement learning (RL) framework for lightweight trajectory selection with a frozen world model and a fixed candidate bank.
title: Residual-Guided Lightweight Reinforcement Learning for Risk-Aware Trajectory Selection with a Frozen World Model

summary: Recent world action models (WAMs) drop future prediction at inference, assuming that representations learned through auxiliary future supervision still benefit action generation.
title: Making Future-Predictive Representations Actionable

summary: Agentic systems using retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) must repair their own answers by gathering more evidence, testing alternative policies and deciding if, when, and what repairs are needed. Yet how do we know if a system's repairs are working when metrics like accuracy can be misleading?
title: RagHarnessDebugger: Jev-Guided Agentic RAG in Contract Inference Repair Auditing

summary: Accurate shape estimation of Deformable Linear Objects (DLOs) is a fundamental challenge in robotic manipulation, often hindered by visual occlusions and the high-dimensional configuration space of flexible materials. While Force/Torque (F/T) and vision-centric methods have been proposed, they frequently struggle with grasp-site ambiguities and environmental interference.
title: Physics-Informed Tactile-based Shape Estimation of Deformable Linear Objects

summary: The emergence of large language models (LLMs) in late 2022 has raised questions about the future of science, but assessing their impact requires understanding how scientific practices were already evolving. We analyze 2.5 million full-text papers across five disciplines from 2015 to 2025, tracing trends over a broad spectrum of lexical, structural, epistemological, and social dimensions.
title: Large Language Models Have Not Yet Transformed Science

summary: ArisGlobal, a provider of life sciences technology spanning pharmacovigilance, regulatory, medical affairs, clinical, and quality functions, developed NavaX, an AI engine purpose-built for life sciences on Amazon Bedrock , to automate adverse-event case processing.
title: How ArisGlobal scaled generative AI inference on Amazon Bedrock

summary: Failure avoidance in complex robot-environment interactions is challenging because the underlying dynamics are difficult to model accurately, and available predictive models may not provide reliable derivatives.
title: Sim2CBF: From Forward Simulations to Implicit Control Barrier Function Safety Filtering without Model Derivatives

summary: Contact center systems often need to make bounded decisions, such as identifying a caller's intent, retrieving the knowledge-base article that answers a query, assessing agent compliance, or judging the output of AI models used in production.
title: Can Decision Models Replace LLMs in Real-World Contact Center Classification and Judging Tasks?

summary: Many LLM benchmarks for languages other than English are translated, multiple-choice, or difficult to score automatically. We introduce The Shared Word (TSW-NL), a Dutch benchmark built around four core principles: it is language-specific, open-vocabulary, human-curated, and deterministically scored. Each puzzle gives three clues that describe different senses or uses of the same Dutch word.
title: The Shared Word: Evaluating Language Models on Dutch Word Puzzles

summary: Drifting, the deliberate control of a vehicle at large sideslip angles, is relevant to both motorsport and recovery from unexpected oversteer. Existing autonomous drifting methods typically determine drift intensity through predefined reference trajectories, optimization objectives, or learned policy rewards, rather than accepting a desired sideslip angle as an explicit input.
title: Sideslip-Conditioned Drift Trajectory Planning with Flow Matching and Control Barrier Functions

summary: Typed decision models combine natural-language understanding with a structured interface that returns a selected action and an option-level probability distribution without generating lengthy textual responses. Their low inference cost and response latency make them attractive for transportation problems with predefined alternatives.
title: When Do Typed Decision Models Work in Transportation? Evidence from Travel Choice and Traffic Signal Control

summary: This work presents Arboreus, a realistic Boreal forest simulator, developed to support statistical validation of robotic autonomy algorithms in Boreal forest environments. Arboreus presents an automated methodology for synthesizing large-scale, data-informed, plausible forest worlds from parametric trees, height-variant terrain, and satellite-informed tree density distributions.
title: Arboreus: A Realistic Boreal Forest Simulator with Topographic Terrain and Satellite-Informed Parametric Tree Distributions

summary: OpenAI is opening its cybersecurity tool Daybreak to NATO and several European governments, including Germany, France, and Poland. The EU's cybersecurity agency ENISA has already used it to find real vulnerabilities in EU software.
title: OpenAI opens its cybersecurity tool Daybreak to NATO and European governments

summary: Planning a trip is a favorite demo for personal AI assistants: you can try it with Muse, or with Gemini or half a dozen other choices. But while most pitches use travel-planning as part of a general-purpose agent pitch, a new startup from a Google Maps alum is betting that a specialized travel-planning agent can [. ]
title: Voyage Labs raises $12 million for a specialized AI travel assistant

summary: Edinburgh's Childlight Institute reports a more than 8,400 percent increase in AI-generated child sexual abuse material over two years, from about 4,700 reports in 2023 to over 400,000 in 2025. Abusers are using tools like nudify apps for blackmail.
title: Reports of AI-generated child sexual abuse material have surged more than 8,400 percent in two years

summary: Natural language-guided UAV navigation enables intuitive human-robot interaction and flexible autonomous flight in complex environments. However, reliable navigation requires accurate instruction following, continuous task progress tracking, and safe obstacle avoidance, which remain challenging for existing world-action models that primarily focus on action prediction.
title: Fly as Instructed: Refining World-Action Policies for UAV Vision-Language Navigation

coverage.title: Isomorphic Labs raises $5 billion in its second mega-round within six months

summary: Isomorphic Labs, the AI drug-discovery platform that was spun out of Google’s DeepMind in 2021, has raised $5 Billion in a Series C funding round.
title: Isomorphic Labs raises $5B as it looks to take drug candidates to clinical trials

summary: As a subscriber, you now have access to 4 in-depth research reports on AI, energy, and climate tech.
title: Research Reports

summary: A rare label seldom occurs alone, and a classifier can recover it from the frequent labels it co-occurs with, its companions, without having learned the label itself. Existing diagnostics of this need a trained model: none says before training whether a corpus admits the failure, or what the standard aggregate hides.
title: When the tail is earned by its companions: measuring label dependence in long-tailed multi-label classification

summary: Language-conditioned traffic simulation enables scalable test scenarios steered by natural language. The goal is to control selected agents while surrounding traffic reacts to their observed behaviour. For example, a vehicle instructed to cut in late should cause the following vehicle to brake only when the manoeuvre becomes observable.
title: CaFe: Causally Faithful Conditional Traffic Scenario Generation

summary: This paper presents the design and implementation of Auriga Robotics' mobile manipulator robot, developed at the Robotics and Intelligent Automation Laboratory, Department of Electrical Engineering, Shahid Beheshti University. Hereafter, this platform is referred to as the @Work Robot. The robot targets industrial tasks, with an emphasis on improving efficiency in repetitive or hazardous work environments.
title: Technical Report of Mobile Manipulator Robot for Industrial Environments

summary: Lidar-inertial odometry (LIO) has an efficiency problem. High-resolution lidars produce millions of points per second that must be processed online on the resource-constrained hardware of robots, cars, or drones, yet most LIO methods neither bound their memory nor report their compute footprint.
title: Pelorus: Resource-Aware Lidar-Inertial Odometry

summary: Science Corp raised a $400 million Series D to scale up its anti-blindness business.
title: Science Corporation’s brain tech is worth $3.5 billion after new funding

summary: Verification procedures in coding agents must preserve execution facts, interpret their scope and discharge checking obligations. We study these responsibilities through qualified repository checks, controlled evidence consumers and executable workflows. A prospective thirteen-task factorial study finds that correct reported facts need not yield the requested finite verdict.
title: When Passing Checks Do Not Establish Completion: Evidence Interpretation in Coding Agents

summary: Conventional balance formulations often assume a rigid, stationary support, decoupling body stabilization from support motion. This assumption becomes inadequate on mechanically responsive supports, creating a coupled control challenge: corrective body motions intended to restore equilibrium can also excite support motion.
title: Lyapunov-Inspired Sustained Balance on Dynamically Responsive Supports

summary: When a twelve-lead electrocardiogram is written as text for a large language model, the number of tokens has to be balanced against the information lost through compression. This paper presents a deterministic encoding that writes eight independent leads as amplitude letters and exact time gaps and recovers the remaining four limb leads algebraically.
title: Compact and Decodable Electrocardiogram Text for Large Language Models

summary: The new standing committee will give board-level oversight of national security policies, export control compliance, and global trade risks, the company said.
title: Nvidia’s first big move after Jensen Huang’s exit targets national security

summary: Researchers recently discovered unexpected behavior from Grok Bot, the AI agent platform from Elon Musk’s SpaceXSI. Over five days, Grok bots installed on two separate employee laptops made 31 requests to access data stored in employee calendar, email, Slack, and GitHub accounts.
title: Grok Bot took unapproved actions, ignored orders to stop, and then denied it

summary: Double Oracle (DO) and PSRO approximate Nash equilibria in two-player zero-sum games by iteratively expanding a strategy population with best responses supplied by an oracle.
title: Virtual Double Oracle: Faster Convergence by Leveraging Strategies That Were Watching All Along

summary: NVIDIA’s Ian Buck kicked off the company’s week at SC26 in Chicago on Monday with new tools for AI agents, software that can plan experiments, run code and check results on researchers’ own systems.
title: Ian Buck Kicks Off NVIDIA’s Week at SC26 as Science Enters the Age of Agents

summary: The idea of computing with light has been around for over 70 years, but until recently it’s remained largely in the realm of research.
title: AI Is Giving Optical Computing Another Shot

summary: The update comes as Billboard reported last month that Sony Music had requested the removal of more than 260,000 deepfake songs from digital platforms, nearly double the number the label disclosed in March.
title: Spotify’s new tool aims to stop deepfakes from being attributed to real artists

summary: Robot demonstrations are collected on different embodiments, leaving many robot-skill combinations unobserved. Pooling these data shares visual knowledge, while joint labels remain tied to the demonstrating kinematic chain. We propose a geometry-supervised training framework for zero-shot composition of familiar robots and skills.
title: Zero-Shot Compositional Generalization for Embodied Manipulation

summary: Adaptive reasoning must decide whether to answer now or spend more compute. Predicting that the current answer is wrong does not establish whether further reasoning will improve it.
title: A Full-Ledger Counterfactual Audit of Adaptive Reasoning

summary: Executable synthetic environments provide scalable training tasks and verifiable feedback for long-horizon agents. Existing environment synthesis methods primarily generate tasks within individual environments. However, these tasks do not adequately capture real-world interactions across services, where actions in one service depend on information obtained from another.
title: CrossEnv: Synthesizing Verifiable Cross-Environment Tasks for Long-Horizon Agent Training

summary: Swarms of unmanned aerial and ground vehicles (UAV/UGV) operating in contested environments cannot rely on software alone for physical safety, since the software stack and its networks are part of the attack surface.
title: Guarded Swarms in the Loop: A ROS 2/PX4 Digital Twin for Hybrid Digital-Analog Coordination of UAV/UGV Swarms

summary: Passive back exoskeletons show promising benefits for reducing occupational musculoskeletal disorders. However, their assistance cannot be modulated towards the task requirements. Active exoskeletons offer opportunities for pose-specific assistance, but, developing these systems from scratch for research can be time consuming.
title: Levio: Smart Actuated Back-Exoskeleton via Retrofit of a Commercial Passive Device

summary: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) improves factuality by grounding large language models (LLMs) in external evidence. However, long retrieved contexts incur computational overhead and can even hurt performance due to noisy or irrelevant content.
title: StitchRAG: Constructing Compact and Evidence-Preserving Contexts for RAG with Diffusion-Based Stitching

summary: Large language models (LLMs) in embodied robots create security dependencies beyond inference. We investigate a network-exposed configuration attack on the Pollen Robotics Reachy Mini Lite, allowing an unauthenticated attacker to replace personality settings and the cloud LLM's system prompt through a management interface, without adversarial conversational input.
title: Network-Exposed Configuration Attacks on LLM-Controlled Social Robots

summary: Diffusion models are increasingly adopted in robotics and control due to their capability to express multiple feasible solutions to a given task. However, the role of stochasticity in the diffusion model-sampler across denoising remains poorly understood. We introduce a per-timestep counterfactual diagnostic that tests how changing the sampled noise affects the final output.
title: Stochastic Diversity Windows: Diagnosing Noise Influence in Robotic Diffusion Sampling

summary: Currently, robots can learn whole-body loco-manipulation through scale: the strongest policies have billions of parameters and still need task-specific fine-tuning. Humans have limited processing capacity, yet learn and act efficiently through a body schema that organizes what they see and how they move.
title: Body Schema Policy: Body as the Vision-Action Interface for Efficient Robot Loco-Manipulation

summary: Recent multilingual large language models (LLMs) have improved machine translation, yet culturally adaptive translation for low-resource languages (LRLs) remains underexplored. This is particularly challenging for recipes, where ingredients, cooking tools, measurements, and procedures may require adaptation to the target cultural context.
title: Cross-cultural Adaptation of Recipes for Low-Resource Languages: A Benchmark and Multilingual Culinary Lexicon for Hausa, Yorùbá, and Igbo

summary: Maritime shipping simultaneously faces the dual challenges of escalating port congestion and increasingly stringent decarbonization mandates. Large-scale vessel anchorage at hub ports inflates unit transport costs while generating significant additional \(CO_2\) emissions from idling auxiliary engines.
title: Route Optimization under Port Congestion and Carbon Reduction: An NSGA-II Approach

summary: Accurate end-effector trajectory tracking on quadruped manipulators is challenging because uncertainties in actuators, foot-ground contact, and geometric errors are propagated through the leg-arm kinematic chain.
title: Learning Accurate End-Effector Trajectory Tracking with Inertial Feedback for a Quadruped Manipulator

summary: When AI agents share limited resources, such as computing services or public infrastructure, their individual choices affect how much work they complete as a group. Can sharing evidence of what is available let a group make full use of its resources after capacity changes? We tested this with language-model agents choosing between two simulated servers.
title: Groups of AI agents underuse resources despite shared evidence of increased capacity

summary: How 3GPP Releases 15, 16, and 17 brought satellite access into 5G NR, NB-IoT, and eMTC. Why satellite links suit IoT devices that send small, infrequent, and delay-tolerant messages. Where non-terrestrial networks (NTN) add value, including asset tracking, agriculture, public safety, and offshore operations.
title: Understand How Satellite Links Shape IoT Device Design and Testing

summary: Live Rewind and Siri Recap can transcribe missed moments and summarize your day—if you don’t mind a little social clumsiness.
title: The Apple Watch’s Live Rewind Can Record and Rewind Spoken Conversations. It’s Pretty Awkward

summary: The French CEO of Hugging Face, a mega-hub of open-source AI software, says the attack by OpenAI models earlier this year proved one thing: Humanity can’t let AI be controlled by the few.
title: Rogue Agents Hacked His Company. Why Is Clément Delangue So Optimistic About AI?

summary: Google and Apple alumni Chad Steelberg and Andy Baynes are applying what they learned running software companies and designing iPhones to manufacturing lethal munitions.
title: AI Told These Ex-Google Guys How to Build a Billion-Dollar Weapons Business

summary: NVIDIA has released 2 open-source projects for running managed Kubernetes on GPU infrastructure: NVIDIA Kubernetes Engine (NVKE) and NVIDIA Kubernetes Recipes (NVKR) . Both were recently announced as components of the NVIDIA DSX AI Factory Platform . NVKE is the control plane for a managed Kubernetes service.
title: NVIDIA Open-Sources NVKE and NVKR for Managed Kubernetes on GPU Infrastructure

summary: Sarvam has opened Sarvam Token Factory to everyone. Sarvam Token Factory is an inference platform from Sarvam that serves its own models and open-weight models from GPU clusters in India. Developers reach every model through one OpenAI-compatible API .
title: Sarvam Launches Sarvam Token Factory: Bringing India-Hosted Inference to 8 Open Models

summary: Shared memory for multi-agent debate is usually built to resolve inconsistency: retrieval returns one winning fact and the disagreement disappears before any agent sees it. We ask whether that is correct. In DebateGraph, four backends share one contract (read/write/snapshot), so five mechanisms from the agent-memory literature can be removed independently under a fixed budget, each gated on a pre-declared threshold.
title: Surfacing Disagreement Beats Resolving It: A Gated Ablation Study of Provenance-Weighted Memory for Multi-Agent Debate

summary: Liquid AI just released d1.2 and d1.2-ultra . A decision model does not write text. It returns calibrated probabilities over a fixed set of answers. The Liquid AI d1.2 decision model family now accepts text, images and audio.
title: Liquid AI Releases d1.2 and d1.2-ultra: Omnimodal Decision Models That Top the AA Decision Index

summary: Explore the new Sales plugin and 30+ new and expanded partner plugins in ChatGPT to research prospects, prepare pitches, update your CRM, and move deals forward.
title: Introducing ChatGPT for Sales

summary: What protects an LLM team when one teammate quietly goes wrong? Most multi-agent LLM work assumes cooperative partners and inspects chat between turns before acting. Real-time embodied cooperation does not allow this pause: chat runs alongside action, so a teammate whose words stay cooperative while behavior diverges can cause damage faster than the team can name what is happening.
title: Bad Apples in the Kitchen: How LLM Teams Detect, Correct, and Calibrate Against Their Misaligned Members

summary: Wearable and smartphone sensors capture behavioral signals associated with mental health, yet inferring mental health outcomes from these signals has traditionally relied on supervised models requiring labeled data and offering limited insight into their predictions.
title: OAK-Mind: Zero-Training Mental Health Change Inference from Passive Sensing via Knowledge-Grounded Multi-Agent LLMs

summary: Multi-agent delegation lets LLM systems distribute evidence collection across workers with separate contexts. This creates a consistency challenge: facts retrieved by workers may be missing from the evidence available to the lead for a joint conclusion.
title: Multi-Agent Memory Inconsistency: Where Factual Conflicts Disappear in LLM Agents

summary: John Urschel PhD ’21, the Class of 1956 Career Development Assistant Professor in the MIT Department of Mathematics, is no stranger to building muscle: Before earning his PhD at MIT, Urschel strengthened his offensive muscles as a lineman for the Baltimore Ravens.
title: Q&A: Why building math muscles remains important in the AI era

summary: When deploying deep learning models in high-stakes scenarios, researchers would like to understand how they work. Today, this requires unraveling an enormously complex network of internal processing nodes to understand what the model knows and how it will likely behave in practice.
title: Learning the language of machine learning

summary: In Bayesian and inverse Bayesian (BIB) inference, a large prediction error can trigger surprise nullification, which expands belief and likelihood variances by a common factor, leaving the updated variance ratio the same as in standard Bayesian updating. This can increase belief uncertainty while keeping the learning rate low.
title: Emergence and Collapse of Leader-Follower Flocks through Phantom Targets: Surprise Nullification in Bayesian and Inverse Bayesian Inference

summary: Large language model (LLM) trading agents are tested on news, but news reaches stock prices within minutes, and a benchmark that replays headlines at their publication time finds no alpha in trading on them. Money can then remain in two places, before news whose date is known, such as earnings announcements, and after bad news, if the market's fall went too far.
title: The Only Edge Was Memorized in Training: LLM Trading Agents Around Earnings and Bad News

summary: Cooperative multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) often fails under exogenous variability such as shifts in opponents or environment regimes that cannot be controlled by the team but alter the transition dynamics.
title: Addressing Exogenous Variability in Cooperative Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning

summary: Training coding agents for long-horizon tasks requires environments with verifiable feedback. Existing pipelines often follow a linear process that ends with validation, establishing usability but providing little guidance on improving training value.
title: From Repositories to Training Environments: Scaling Long-Horizon Coding Agents with Environment Evolution Loop

summary: CAD practitioners often work with proprietary parts that they are unwilling to share with external services. For individuals and small companies, bringing this work in-house also requires computational resources they can afford. We introduce CADMAGEDDON, an open-source agent that reconstructs editable CAD from meshes and can run locally on single-GPU systems and current-generation laptops.
title: CADMAGEDDON: High-Fidelity CAD Reconstruction with Local Inference

summary: Turning a CAD model into a machining program requires both process knowledge and geometric precision. Language models can generate such workflows by writing geometry and toolpath code for each part, but this makes numerical execution part of the model's task. We introduce MillBill, an agent that separates machining decisions from their geometric execution and verification.
title: MillBill: A Machining Agent with Geometric Feedback

summary: Identity matching asks whether two records denote the same identity, yet the answer depends on the target granularity. Two records may match at the base level but not at the variant level: they share an underlying design while differing in attributes such as color or size. Final matching accuracy does not separately characterize the capabilities involved.
title: PURE: A Diagnostic Benchmark for Multi-Granularity Multimodal Identity Matching

summary: We present the Autoregressive View Model (AVM), which generates a scene as a stream of views without constructing an explicit 3D representation. Through a unified in-context interface, AVM conditions on images or videos to generate short clips along a requested camera path. Visual context grounds reconstruction and interpolation, while a learned prior enables extrapolation into unseen regions.
title: Autoregressive View Model

summary: Standard neural architectures such as the Transformer were chosen because they train well with gradient descent and run fast on GPUs. In weight-space programming, a large language model (LLM) writes target weights by hand without gradient-based training, so those reasons no longer apply. Should we keep the Transformer?
title: Weight-Space Programming Doesn't Need Transformers

summary: Autoregressive video diffusion models generate frames based on new observations and inputs, making them a promising medium for interactive visual experiences. However, existing models are orders of magnitude too slow for fluid interaction. This paper introduces FastFrames, a family of fast autoregressive video diffusion models that achieves interactive latency without compromising quality.
title: FastFrames: Video Generation at Interactive Latency

summary: LLM agents increasingly drive their own learning. Self-improvement methods delegate various components of model optimization to the models themselves. As models become more capable, this motivates a basic question: do these increasingly capable models still need us to specify how they should self-improve?
title: Do LLM Agents Still Need to Be Told How to Self-Improve?

summary: Robot manipulation videos provide a rich visual experience, yet recovering robot action and gripper-state annotations from RGB observations still remains challenging. Using the embodiment-agnostic tool-center-point (TCP) pose as the action space, we present TCP4D, a unified model in which a shared 4D scene representation both tracks observed TCP motion and generates future TCP trajectories.
title: TCP4D: A Unified Tool-Center-Point Tracking and Generation Model for Robot Manipulation

summary: Attention scores candidate supports of an answer, which we call witnesses, and reads the scores at a temperature. We build a higher-order attention layer whose state lives on pairs of items: for a pair (a, b), each third item k is a witness judged through its legs (a, k) and (k, b).
title: Attention at Absolute Zero

summary: Claude Fable 5.2 has solved two open problems in theoretical physics. Both concern black holes and the search for a theory of quantum gravity.
title: Claude Fable 5.2 solves two open problems in the physics of black holes

summary: Deep models often rely on spurious correlations that fail on underrepresented groups. Existing methods either correct human-specified bias attributes or infer unknown biases from the learned representation space. However, annotated attributes may differ from the shortcuts actually used by a model, while a single representation provides incomplete and potentially noisy evidence.
title: Let Samples Sing in Chorus: Mitigating Spurious Correlations via Cross-view Consensus

summary: Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation (MOPD) enables a single student to absorb the skills of several domain teachers by learning from its own generated responses. We present Multimodal Model Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation Reasoner (M3OPD-Reasoner), a fully open recipe for post-training vision-language models (VLMs) over three reasoning domains: image STEM, image perception, and video.
title: M3OPD-Reasoner: An Open Recipe for Post-Training Multimodal Reasoning with Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation

summary: π^4 is a unified foundation model for 4D scene perception. From diverse, uncalibrated RGB observations in the wild---a single image, an unordered collection, or a video sequence---it recovers dense geometry, camera poses, and metric scale, together with 2D/3D point tracks and moving-object masks for multi-image inputs.
title: π^4: A Foundation Model for 4D Scene Geometry and Motion

summary: Large language models (LLMs) have renewed interest in Page Stream Segmentation (PSS), splitting a multi-page file into its constituent documents. Yet published LLM methods still frame the task as boundary classification over one or a few neighboring pages, and commercial document-splitting APIs do not disclose their methods.
title: RICoT: Recurrent Interleaved Chain-of-Thought for Page Stream Segmentation

summary: -05-X-03), Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalogs, and exploitation sightings. We introduce an evidence model implemented in Vulnerability-Lookup that selects the earliest evidence for each lifecycle event, distinguishes vulnerability-specific records, preserves date precision, and ensures traceability to original sources.
title: Exploited Before It Was Fixed? Vulnerability Timelines from Open, Machine-Readable Evidence

summary: Fine-grained questions about long videos ask how many times an action occurs, in what order events unfold, or exactly when a state changes. Answering them can require finding brief moments scattered across hours of footage. Agentic models that decide when and where to look promise to find these moments, yet this ability is hard both to measure and to learn.
title: NexSight: Verifiable Tasks for Fine-Grained Agentic Long-Video Understanding

summary: Autoregressive vision-language-action (VLA) models predict discrete action tokens with the next-token objective of their vision-language backbone, so the action tokenizer defines the interface between the policy and the robot. In bimanual manipulation, the two arms share a repertoire of movements yet coordinate through complementary roles, and an action representation should capture both.
title: BiCAT: Bimanual Coordination Action Tokenization

summary: How OpenAI is working with NATO and allied cyber agencies to help trusted defenders find vulnerabilities, test fixes and protect essential systems.
title: Strengthening NATO and allied cyber defenses with AI

summary: OpenAI and the Government of Chile are partnering to support responsible AI adoption, build public-sector skills and help local startups develop AI applications.
title: Introducing OpenAI for Chile

summary: Reward models for instruction-guided video editing can favor temporal consistency at the expense of motion. We study this failure, termed motion collapse, using controlled motion-suppression variants of real edits. On VE-Bench, the evaluated composite reward prefers a motion-suppressed candidate in 97% of cases.
title: Motion-Aware Reward Modeling for Instruction-Guided Video Editing

summary: We introduce Faithfulness Video Score (FVSCORE), a neuro-symbolic framework for specification-driven video generation evaluation. Existing evaluators rely on holistic MLLM judgments or vision-language metrics, yet aligning their scores with human judgments and tracing them to specific temporal violations remain open challenges.
title: FVScore: Specification-Driven Neuro-Symbolic Video Evaluation

summary: Latent diffusion models rely on a decoder to map denoised latents to pixels, adding complexity and inference cost. We introduce Decoding Without a Decoder (DWD), which lets a finetuned diffusion transformer produce final pixels directly through a linear head.
title: Decoding Without a Decoder: Direct Pixel Prediction from Diffusion Transformers

summary: We present Xing 4, a series of large language models that extends the TeleChat lineage through coordinated advances in model architecture and training infrastructure on Ascend. This report describes the design principles and systems engineering behind the series, spanning architecture selection, large-scale pretraining, and reasoning and agentic post-training.
title: TeleChat to Xing4: Advancing Frontier Agentic Models on Domestic Chips and Frameworks

summary: Collaboration promises to extend humanoid capabilities beyond what individual robots can achieve. However, realizing this potential requires coordinated whole-body interactions, coherent long-horizon planning, and precise synchronization across robots. We introduce Heave-Ho, a decentralized framework for long-horizon collaborative multi-humanoid loco-manipulation.
title: Heave-Ho: Decentralized Long-Horizon Multi-Humanoid Collaboration

summary: The goal of this paper is to reduce the input token cost of Omni-modal large language models (Omni-LLMs) at inference time. Omni-LLMs reason jointly over audio, video and text, but the cost of the three streams is highly unbalanced: visual tokens account for the vast majority of the input, and are highly redundant.
title: Out of Sight, Still in Mind: Token Compression for Omni-LLMs

summary: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed as autonomous shopping agents that process multimodal product listings (consisting of visual and text data) and recommend purchases on behalf of consumers. Naturally, one might assume that models with more thinking power would make higher-quality purchasing decisions.
title: Thinking Harder Doesn't Lead to Better Choices: Reasoning Effort Increases the Confidence but Not the Correctness of LLM Shopping Agents

summary: Hyper-Connections (HC) expand the residual stream of a Transformer into N parallel streams, and manifold-constrained HC (mHC) stabilizes them at scale. However, mHC benefits little from more than four streams, partly because each sublayer writes a single output to all streams, limiting how differently they can be updated.
title: TPHC: Improving Hyper-Connections with Tensor-Parallel Grouped Updates

summary: Visual proxies decouple explicit world-state simulation from photorealistic video synthesis, offering a controllable interface for both offline clip creation and real-time interactive streaming. Yet a practical renderer must address two challenges.
title: Code World Model 2.0: Towards Infinite Controllable Video Generation

summary: Our aim is to accelerate autoregressive vision-language-action models (VLAs), which generate robot actions one token at a time. Speculative decoding makes this possible: a lightweight draft model proposes several tokens at once, and the VLA verifies them in a single pass, accepting only those that match its own predictions, so decoding remains lossless.
title: VSpark: Speculative Decoding for Autoregressive Vision-Language-Action Models

summary: Learned lossless codecs make smaller files than common classical codecs, yet the images we archive and train on still use classical codecs. A main reason is time: a learned codec takes seconds to decode a photo that a classical codec opens in milliseconds, and their faster variants give up most of their gain in size.
title: FMT: Lossless Image Compression in a Fixed Number of Parallel Steps

summary: Astra for Law ranked first in a launch evaluation spanning 24 areas of law. Every ChatGPT Enterprise customer can now request access.
title: Astra for Law leads in legal intelligence

summary: Release: llm 0.37.3 . A bug fix release for LLM , mainly to cover a problem with the most recent Homebrew package of the software. Homebrew now ships the latest SQLite, 3.54.1 , which includes a fix that broke LLM's logging code .
title: llm 0.37.3

summary: Three months since introducing its product, AI cybersecurity startup Corba has raised a $125 million Series A at a $1 billion valuation led by NEA.
title: Cybersecurity AI startup Corma reaches $1B valuation in about 3 months

summary: Jensen Huang's stunning resignation from Nvidia after more than 33 years has sent shockwaves throughout the tech industry.
title: Tech leaders are convinced that Jensen Huang’s exit was a plot against him

summary: A humanoid robotics company backed and advised by President Donald Trump’s son, Eric Trump, has reportedly missed payroll and may be on the brink of collapse after a funding shortfall.
title: Robo-soldier startup backed by Eric Trump misses payroll, may collapse

summary: Amazon Bedrock Managed Knowledge Base and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore memory now store conversations, extract facts, and bring long-term memory into a single AgenticRetrieveStream call.
title: Build memory-aware AI agents with Agentic Retrieve on Amazon Bedrock Managed Knowledge Base

summary: Turning public data into prediction datasets requires connecting source discovery, task definition, construction, and distribution. We deployed Dataset Factory to perform these steps continuously under a standing release policy. Bounded language-model tasks interpret sources, write construction code, and review task meaning; deterministic software manages state, workers, retries, and publication.
title: Operating an Agent-Driven Dataset Factory: Discovery, Construction, and Public Release

summary: Molecular dynamics (MD) is an indispensable tool across physics, chemistry, biology, and materials science. Owing to its arithmetic structure, particularly the.
title: Accelerate Molecular Dynamics Simulations with Accurate, Flexible Primitives Using NVIDIA cuPotential

summary: With $k\geq 1$ repairpersons starting initially from a depot, we present a 3.877-competitive deterministic algorithm for the fundamental online traveling repairperson problem on an arbitrary metric. For the special class of zero-residual instances, we improve the ratio to $3+ε$ for every $ε>0$. We also extend these results to some variants of the related so-called online dial-a-ride problem.
title: Beyond 4: Improved Competitive Traveling Repairperson

summary: Financial institutions face a critical challenge: processing massive volumes of data with speed, accuracy, and compliance while operating under some of the world’s strictest regulatory frameworks. Duco is the agentic Operations platform for financial services, serving tier-one banks and other financial institutions.
title: How Duco transforms financial data automation with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore

summary: Nvidia interim CEO and longtime CFO Colette Kress is about to have one of the biggest days of her career on Tuesday when the company reports its third-quarter results. Given the turmoil Nvidia is in, there are a number of questions that Nvidia should answer.
title: All the questions Nvidia should answer on Tuesday — but probably won’t

summary: Enterprise teams are building multi-agent systems, and when early implementations fall short, the cause is rarely the model. Multi-agent coordination is a distributed systems problem, and many teams taking it on haven’t yet built distributed systems instincts.
title: Taxonomy of multi-agent design patterns, anti-patterns, and lessons from manufacturing

summary: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman is once again addressing his controversial comments on PC RAM purchases. "I want to be clear, I want people to have a lot of RAM, I think everybody should be able to buy a lot of RAM for their own computer," Altman said today. "I think the home tinkering is great." [. ]
title: Sam Altman says he wants everyone ‘to have a lot of RAM’

summary: Constellation Energy - America's largest operator of nuclear power plants - does not share Wall Street's concerns that the Democrats will slow down data center development. On the company's third-quarter earnings call last week, CEO Joe Dominguez was, for lack of a better word, unbothered as he addressed the blue wave.
title: Big Nuclear isn’t worried about the Democrats stopping data centers

summary: Fossil fuels are still the biggest source of electricity for hyperscale data centers in the US, a new paper published in the journal Nature Sustainability shows. They likely burn through more electricity collectively than many countries do, resulting in a serious amount of greenhouse gas emissions.
title: US data centers now burn more electricity than a midsized country

summary: The PyTorch Foundation is proud to celebrate the winners and nominees of the fourth annual PyTorch Foundation Contributor Awards! Presented on the keynote stage at PyTorch Conference 2026 in San.
title: Celebrating the 2026 PyTorch Foundation Contributor Award Winners and Nominees

title: California state AG sues OpenAI over rogue agent incidents

summary: Deb Shoquist leads operations at NVIDIA, overseeing the supply chain and manufacturing behind its AI platforms. That description sums up the job, but it doesn’t begin to encompass what Shoquist has made possible over decades.
title: How the World’s Most Advanced AI Infrastructure Supply Chain Invents the Future

summary: Coordinating a team of heterogeneous agents to complete tasks with unknown requirements is a challenging multi-agent planning problem. Agents differ in their ability to discover task requirements and in their ability to engage tasks, so the planner must coordinate task discovery, execution, and staging.
title: Coordination of Heterogeneous Teams with Uncertain Task Requirements

summary: Google's Threat Intelligence Group has for the first time caught attackers finding and exploiting security vulnerabilities with no human involvement at all. An AI framework called "exploit_agent," found on an exposed server, automatically compared code before and after patches, built exploits, and ran them on its own.
title: Google warns that fully automated cyberattacks have arrived and will get worse fast

summary: Apple released betas of iOS 27.3, iPadOS 27.3, and macOS 27.3 today, and the company is using the update to test new per device daily usage limits for some Siri AI and Apple Intelligence features, according to MacRumors.
title: Apple is testing daily usage limits for more complex Siri AI interactions

summary: OpenAI is announcing a tool that it says will help child sexual abuse investigators cut through the noise to find harmful material they can act on quickly. At a Monday press briefing in Washington, DC, OpenAI announced a classifier it says can better detect abusive imagery of kids, including whether it's AI-generated.
title: OpenAI wants to stop deepfakes from overwhelming child abuse tiplines

summary: AI systems are increasingly deployed in high-stakes decision-making contexts, where interactions among components can introduce fairness risks that remain undetected when auditing components or collective outcomes in isolation. As LLM-based multi-agent systems become more prevalent, understanding how biased information propagates through agent interactions is essential for assessing their fairness.
title: Corrupting Ties: Investigating Robustness to Bias Injection Across Multi-Agent Network Topologies

summary: OpenAI physicist Nathaniel Craig used GPT-6 Astra to tackle a problem that had stumped particle physicists for over 25 years. The AI model took Craig's strategy for defining the full Standard Model on a computational lattice and turned it into a working proof.
title: OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra tackles the Standard Model's toughest math problem on a lattice

summary: Trump contradicted his own government's intelligence officials, who reportedly concluded that Alice Huang is a Chinese spy.
title: Trump says ex-Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s affair with an alleged Chinese spy did not threaten national security

summary: On the heels of the Nvidia scandal , the Trump administration is preparing to crack down on foreign data centers that are fueling China’s advancements in artificial intelligence by allowing remote access to otherwise restricted high-end chips necessary for AI training.
title: US moves to cut China’s remote access to AI chips

summary: Monitoring oil spills with fleets of Autonomous Surface Vehicles (ASVs) requires mapping a heterogeneous pollutant field from sparse, noisy measurements under tight time and energy budgets. Informative Path Planning (IPP) addresses this problem by coupling a reconstruction model, which infers the field and its uncertainty, with a planner that decides where to sample next.
title: Better Calibrated, Better Planned: Uncertainty-Aware Multi-ASV Informative Path Planning for Oil Spill Monitoring

summary: Language models typically increase per-token computation through deeper or looped layers and latent reasoning steps, while richer residual connections improve information flow across layers. We instead increase computational capacity: the number of active computational states a model maintains.
title: Latent Lattice Language Models

summary: Face forgery detection methods often perform well on seen manipulations but generalize poorly to unseen ones. Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) can recognize facial parts and assess their visual plausibility. Existing MLLM-based methods typically express these judgments through textual explanations, but seldom treat individual part decisions as explicit learning targets.
title: FaceJev: Direct Visual Decisions for Face Forgery Detection

summary: Visual agents answer questions about ultra-high-resolution photos by zooming into the relevant regions. However, existing agents often answer from common sense instead of reading the evidence. Reinforcement learning (RL) on the final answer cannot correct this, because a guess earns the same reward as reading. We propose Cross-Input Relative Policy Optimization (CrossRPO), which trains agents on contrast sets.
title: ViRA: Toward Ultra-High-Resolution Visual Agents via Cross-Input Relative Policy Optimization

summary: The National Hurricane Center routinely releases Tropical Cyclone Discussions that offer insights into its tropical cyclone forecasts. This study examines the added value of these discussions for intensity forecasting beyond a set of numerical predictors.
title: Quantifying the added value of human forecaster discussions for tropical cyclone intensity prediction

summary: When a vision-language model describes an image, it names one object at a time and it rarely repeats itself, yet how the model plans this order is far from obvious. We characterize the mechanism a VLM uses to decide where to look before it looks. The mechanism has four main parts. First, binding heads match the relevant text tokens against the image and resolve them into pointers to the matched image region.
title: How VLMs Plan What's Next

summary: We introduce Hyperlyve (Hyperplane Partitioned Lyapunov Verification and Enumeration), a framework for proving the asymptotic stability of nonlinear dynamical systems, including those with neural network controllers. Hyperlyve learns and formally certifies continuous piecewise-affine (CPA) neural Lyapunov functions within a counterexample-guided inductive synthesis (CEGIS) loop.
title: Hyperlyve: Parallelized Enumeration and Exact Lyapunov Stability Certification for Deep ReLU Networks

summary: Continual reinforcement learning requires adaptation to changing conditions while preserving performance under previously encountered dynamics. It was investigated whether specialists generated by evolutionary search can provide a reusable memory when combined with environment detection and failure-driven search.
title: Mitigating Catastrophic Forgetting with Physics-Indexed Specialist Memory: the Evolutionary Neuroplastic Agent

summary: We study how to learn an autoregressive next-token generator $f\colonΣ^\star\toΣ$ from a class $\mathcal{F}$, given chain-of-thought (CoT) demonstrations of length $T$ generated by $f$. We present a simple algorithm based on bagging, which outputs a majority vote of generators that are trained to be CoT-consistent on bootstrap samples of the training data.
title: Optimal Autoregressive Chain-of-Thought Learning via Bagging

summary: In Joint-Embedding Predictive Architectures (JEPAs), a well-constrained projector output does not by itself prevent representation collapse. We find that, from initialization, the encoder representation is dominated by a component shared by different inputs.
title: SADL: On the Demand-Supply Geometry of Representation Collapse

summary: Cryogenic circuit design requires compact transistor models that reproduce measured low-temperature behavior and run in standard circuit simulators. We fit BSIM4 parameters to measured I-V curves of SkyWater 130 nm (SKY130) transistors at 77 K using a neural surrogate of NGSpice. The surrogate maps compact-model parameters and device geometry to the complete set of output and transfer characteristics.
title: Surrogate-Assisted Compact-Model Extraction for SKY130 CMOS at 77 K

summary: Job titles and job descriptions alone provide limited insight into how technical roles differ in a changing job market. To assess how such roles differ in their work and industry applications, we design and compare two methods based on deep learning and transformer representations using 36,081 early-career job postings collected from LinkedIn in the United States between December 2025 and October 2026.
title: Beyond Job Titles: Interpreting Early-Career Job Advertisements with Sparse Autoencoders and Semantic Clustering

summary: Training with MXFP4, a 4-bit microscaling format, is non-deterministic: identical inputs can produce different results across parallelism layouts and GPU vendors. These differences complicate debugging and training audits and can cause training and inference engines to disagree. We present CertiSum to make MXFP4 training bitwise invariant across runs, parallelism layouts, and GPU vendors.
title: CertiSum: Bitwise-Identical MXFP4 Training Across Platforms and Parallelism Layouts

summary: Moonshot AI is done chasing coding benchmarks, it says. The Beijing startup is pivoting its Kimi language models toward biology, chemistry, and pharma research, arguing that science demands smarter AI than law, finance, or code.
title: Moonshot AI pivots Kimi models from coding to science as benchmark gains flatten

summary: Cyber-range and capture-the-flag scenario construction remains labor-intensive because authors must coordinate infrastructure, vulnerable services, attack paths, artifacts, and success conditions. LLMs can propose detailed exercises, but plausible descriptions do not guarantee deployable software or verifiable objectives.
title: ScenarioForge: Resource-Grounded Generation and Execution Validation of Cyber Exercises
