summary: Large language model (LLM) applications increasingly act as agents that select and invoke external tools. The Model Context Protocol (MCP) standardizes this interaction by allowing clients to compose tools advertised by multiple servers. However, tool metadata used for discovery and selection is not, by itself, necessarily bound to a verified provider identity.
title: When Tool Names Are Not Identities: Measuring Provider Misbinding in MCP-Based AI Agents

summary: Recent survival models integrating longitudinal data achieve strong predictive performance, but their predictions are often difficult to interpret, limiting their clinical use. We propose DynSurvX, a model-agnostic explainability framework for dynamic survival prediction with mixed static and longitudinal covariates.
title: DynSurvX: Time-Resolved Explanations for Dynamic Survival Predictions

summary: Test-time augmentation (TTA) aggregates model predictions across multiple transformed views of an input during inference. Because histology images lack a canonical orientation, $D_4$ TTA---pooling across the 8 rotations and reflections of a square---is a standard default in computational pathology.
title: When Do Histology Foundation Models Need Geometric Test-Time Augmentation?

summary: Structure-level wildfire vulnerability assessment is critical for reducing losses in wildland-urban interface communities, yet existing methods often fail to combine parcel-scale ignition pathways with community-scale geographic coverage.
title: Wildfire-SSR: Geolocation-Aware Multimodal Fusion for Structure-Level Wildfire Risk Assessment

summary: Zero-shot time-series foundation models (TSFMs) have become attractive alternatives to task-specific models because they handle diverse downstream tasks, including anomaly detection and forecasting, without per-series training.
title: Severe but Harmless: Stress-Testing Shift Severity for Frozen Time-Series Forecasters

summary: Long video generation should keep the subject and background consistent while supporting rich, natural motion. However, autoregressive models are often distilled with distribution matching distillation (DMD) over short windows, which does not train them to keep this consistency over long ranges. As a result, the subject and background can drift over time.
title: Reference Forcing: Long Video Generation with Region-Guided Drift Correction

summary: Supporters are signing a petition to reinstate Huang. But findings on Nvidia chips in China and a new Commerce rule are threatening open-source AI’s reputation and progress regardless.
title: The open-source movement wants Jensen Huang back

summary: Language models are now used to read central-bank text for economic forecasting, but most were trained on text written after the documents they read. A model reading a 2021 FOMC statement may already know that inflation rose in 2022, so part of its apparent skill can be memory of the outcome, a temporal form of test-set contamination.
title: Reading or Remembering? Measuring Temporal Contamination in Language Models

summary: Streaming video understanding is becoming increasingly important for real-world interactive systems. Such systems must be proactive for natural and useful human interaction: they should respond as soon as sufficient evidence becomes available while avoiding premature, redundant, or incorrect responses.
title: BLIP-Live: Balancing Timeliness & Firing Precision in Proactive Streaming Video Agents

summary: Quantum machine learning has emerged as a promising approach to time series prediction. While quantum reservoir computing has been widely explored for this setting, variational quantum models tailored to sequential data remain comparatively understudied, largely because they are difficult to train.
title: Benchmarking memory and nonlinear processing capacity of quantum recurrent neural networks for time series prediction

summary: Modern machine learning models, such as artificial neural networks, achieve high predictive performance through increasingly complex black-box architectures, limiting their use in settings where transparency, interpretability, and fairness are required.
title: ONAM: Fitting Orthogonal Neural Additive Models for Post-Hoc Interpretability of Black-Box Predictions

summary: Intrusion detectors must recognize evolving malicious behavior even when confirmed attack labels are scarce or incomplete. We present TRACE, a topology-aware graph contrastive learning framework for label-efficient intrusion detection.
title: TRACE: Topological Representations for Anomaly detection through Contrastive Embeddings

summary: Language models increasingly write the explanations people receive when a rule system denies their request. If several rules deny the request independently, an explanation can name a true reason and still leave the person denied after they fix it. We call the missing property recourse validity: changing what the explanation cites, without changing what was asked for, can flip the decision.
title: Right Reason, Wrong Advice: Evaluating Recourse in LLM Explanations of Denied Requests

summary: Consider an online prediction setting, where at each time, we are given a new feature vector and asked to provide a prediction interval or prediction set that will likely contain the corresponding response.
title: The cost of enforcing long-run coverage: a phase transition in online conformal prediction

summary: We introduce SciResearch-Eval, an interactive benchmark of scientific judgment built on a standard laboratory problem: measuring a material's thermal properties by heating it and fitting a heat-conduction simulator. An agent designs its own experiments, uses a supplied simulator that may be under-resolved or physically wrong, and reports each property with a 95% interval.
title: SciResearch-Eval: Evaluating Scientific Judgment in Autonomous Experimental Agents

summary: Vision-language models (VLMs) often fail to match a point or an object across two images, even when the answer can be decoded from their own hidden states.
title: Seen but Unsaid: Locating and Repairing Cross-Image Comparison in Vision-Language Models

summary: Reinforcement learning from verifiable rewards inherits whatever its verifier gets wrong. Outside mathematics and code the verifier is a proxy, a rubric, a learned judge or a hand-written checker, and its distance from the true objective is never measured, so a rising reward cannot be told apart from a hack.
title: Optimistic Verifiers Get Hacked: Reward Hacking Under an Exact Process Oracle

summary: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to interpret, generate, and mediate public-facing language, which makes their reliability especially consequential in politically sensitive settings.
title: Evaluating Cultural Reasoning and Robustness in LLMs for Spanish Political Discourse

summary: Saliency-guided coding allocates bits to the regions viewers are most likely to attend, but accurate 360-degree saliency prediction is computationally expensive, an obstacle for low-latency immersive streaming applications such as robot teleoperation. We quantify how much saliency-prediction accuracy actually translates into compression gain.
title: How Much Does Saliency Accuracy Matter for Saliency-Guided 360-degree Image Compression?

summary: An embodied speaker's expressiveness depends not only on what is said, but also on how the voice sounds and how the body moves. However, existing joint speech-motion generation models are largely driven implicitly by transcript semantics or intermediate speech representations, offering little explicit control over motion hierarchy, body parts, or vocal style.
title: DuoFlow: Towards Synchronized Speech and Motion Generation with Fine-Grained Control

summary: When an authorization policy blocks an agent's tool call, the audit log should name the facts that forced the decision and nothing more. For an executable policy over an enumerable context space this minimal sufficient reason can be computed exactly, so an explanation is scored against ground truth rather than a proxy for it. We use that exactness to ask what a model can learn from a verifier that has no error in it.
title: Procedure without Judgment: What Small Language Models Learn under an Exact Verifier

summary: Safe in-context reinforcement learning (Safe ICRL) asks a policy with fixed parameters to improve on an unseen constrained task from its interaction history while aiming to keep its cost within a budget.
title: Algorithm Distillation for Safe In-Context Reinforcement Learning

summary: This post was co-written with Ashwin Srinivasan, Nishan Das and Karthik Baile from MoEngage. A marketing or product team member planning a weekend flash sale often opens three tools before writing a single line of copy.
title: How MoEngage built agentic customer engagement on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore

summary: When AI agents relay information to one another, an output can preserve an injected instruction's effect on downstream agents even after its wording changes, yet legitimate quotation and template reuse can produce high textual overlap with the source, so text-similarity guardrails that attempt to flag the former risk conflating these two cases.
title: Safe Resemblance, Silent Propagation: Limits of Text-Similarity Guardrails for AI Agent Safety

summary: Mean pairwise cosine similarity between transformer embeddings is a standard measure of whether online discourse is converging under generative AI. When the embeddings are mean-pooled outputs of an encoder never trained for sentence similarity, this measure mostly tracks text length.
title: Embedding Cosine Measures Text Length Before It Measures Homogenization

summary: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman acknowledged the special role Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has played in the AI boom, but ultimately thinks the industry will be “fine” without him at the helm.
title: Sam Altman on Nvidia without Jensen Huang: the industry will be ‘fine’

summary: Long-horizon manipulation tasks require a robot to perform a sequence of physical interactions with its environment, typically combining several different skills.
title: Lazy-MOSAIC: Accelerating Skill-Centric Manipulation Planning with Learned Skill-Effect World Models

summary: Task representations for sequential decision making should describe both an objective and progress toward it. We present an algebraically informed pipeline that uses the relational structure and language semantics of alternating finite automata (AFAs) to learn control features and compile compact execution operators.
title: Tensorized Automata: Algebraically Informed Representation Learning for Sequential Decision Making

summary: Weighted conformal p-values generalize conformal inference to cases with covariate shift. One way to use them is to pass them to the Benjamini-Hochberg (BH) procedure, either to decide which test units to select or to detect outliers. But weighted conformal p-values may not be positively dependent, so we want to know: does BH still control the false discovery rate (FDR) in finite samples?
title: Almost Controlled: The FDR of Benjamini-Hochberg on Weighted Conformal p-Values

summary: Hybrid solid-state LiDAR sensors are making their way into production vehicles, yet the data they produce differs structurally from that of the established spinning mechanical sensors behind today's autonomous-driving datasets: it is ring-free, dense, cluttered, and concentrated in a frontal field of view.
title: GHySSeg: Real-Time Geometric Ground and Road Segmentation for Hybrid Solid-State LiDAR

summary: Recently, the Shapley value has been widely applied in machine learning for feature importance analysis and model explainability. The multilinear extension of games proposed by Owen (1972) expresses the Shapley value as the integral of partial derivatives along the main diagonal of the cube. Direct evaluation of this integral requires exponential-time computation of the partial derivatives.
title: Leverage-Enhanced Sampling Owen Method for Explainable Artificial Intelligence

summary: We develop neural realizations of positive-level Wess-Zumino-Witten models using bosonic Wakimoto and fermionic Fourier-Berezin fields. Level-rank duality connects the charged sectors of the fermionic construction, where explicit neural observables recover conformal block data and enable the transfer of information about unknown correlators between paired theories.
title: Learning from Duality in Neural Network Field Theories

summary: Cross-border cyber attacks on European SMEs and critical-infrastructure operators expose a structural cyber-resilience gap: cybersecurity (threat sharing, detection, response), compliance (framework assessment, certification) and digital forensics (cross-jurisdictional evidence) are jointly regulated by NIS2, the CRA, GDPR and the LED, yet their tooling evolved in silos and rarely interoperates across Member States.
title: The CYBER-BRIDGE project: An AI-Powered Platform for Cross-Border Cybersecurity, Compliance and Forensics in the EU

summary: Vision--language agents generate descriptions, decisions, and instructions that may be reused by users, downstream agents, and automated workflows, creating a need for provenance mechanisms that support content authenticity and post-deployment auditing without unnecessarily degrading response quality.
title: Detection-Efficient Watermarking for Vision--Language Agents via Risk-Constrained Strength Allocation

summary: We introduce a framework for differentiable exact learning that couples an unbounded external environment to a state-tracking neural controller, which we train on policy-trajectory observations (PTOs): expert behavior traces that expose observations and actions while hiding internal states.
title: Differentiable Exact Learning

summary: Persistent spatial understanding is essential for embodied agents to operate reliably in environments they repeatedly encounter. It requires recognizing revisited places despite viewpoint changes, distinguishing them from similar-looking rooms, and updating memories as environments change. Yet existing evaluations often leave physical place identity across separated visits implicit.
title: Lost in the Hallway: Benchmarking Persistent Spatial Memory Across Revisits

summary: Electrical Power and Energy Systems face hybrid threats that combine cyber intrusions, physical sabotage and climate-driven stress, and routinely outpace today's siloed monitoring stacks.
title: RESILAGENT: A Three-Pillar Architecture for Cyber-Physical Resilience in Electrical Power and Energy Systems

summary: A useful memory need not resemble the question it helps answer. Jetriever ranks each stored memory by Jev's decision score for its usefulness to the current question, replacing similarity search with full-pool utility scoring. On InMind's 125 indirect-query tasks, it places the gold exchange first in 84.8% of cases; matched BM25 and MiniLM controls reach 1.6% and 0.0% when indexing user turns.
title: Jetriever: Shifting Agent Memory Retrieval from Similarity to Utility

summary: Higher education is confronting an academic-integrity challenge unlike any in its history. Students can now outsource homework, take-home assignments, and online examinations to large language models (LLMs) that complete them in seconds.
title: Generative AI and the Crisis of Higher Education Assessments: Examining 'AI-Proofing' Strategies for College-Level Assessments

summary: Network Intrusion Detection Systems (NIDSs) must incrementally adapt to emerging attacks, even when only a limited amount of labeled network traffic is available. Consequently, Few-Shot Class-Incremental Learning (FSCIL)-based NIDSs have gained growing attention. However, existing FSCIL-based NIDSs are highly vulnerable to label noise in newly-observed attack classes.
title: Network Intrusion Detection Adaptability under Spurious Labels: A Noise-Aware Few-Shot Class-Incremental Learning Framework

summary: Mechanical blueberry harvesting requires a balance between removing ripe fruit and avoiding premature removal of unripe berries that could remain on the bush for a later harvest. However, operators generally lack real-time information about the maturity composition of the fruit being collected.
title: Event-Triggered Visual Perception for Real-Time Harvest Outcome Estimation in Mechanical Blueberry Harvesting

summary: Constrained Markov decision processes (CMDPs) typically bound expected cumulative cost from an initial state. Such a guarantee can be insufficient when a policy must remain feasible after every history it may encounter.
title: Subprocess-Constrained Markov Decision Processes

summary: Physics-informed operator learning trains neural operators on the residual of a parametric partial differential equation (PDE) instead of labeled solution data, but its reliability depends on a variationally correct residual: one that is equivalent to the error in a norm dictated by the equation, the PDE-compliant norm.
title: Variationally correct physics-informed operator learning for nonlinear partial differential equations

summary: Generative data augmentation adds samples from generative models to a classifier's training set. Many influential studies use generators pre-trained on large external datasets, and so mix the value of synthetic data with knowledge transferred through pretraining.
title: Generative Data Augmentation Without External Data: An Empirical and Theoretical Study on Deep Networks

summary: Model-based reinforcement learning (MBRL) leverages a model of the environment, used for planning and generating samples without interacting with the real world. Motivated by evidence that informed initialization significantly improves the efficiency of MBRL, we propose TDec-Init, an algorithm to warm-start neural dynamics models using transition Jacobians.
title: Warm Starting Neural Dynamics Models From Few Jacobian Samples

summary: Weight Factorization (WF) methods aim to reduce a model's latency, memory, or both. These typically decompose a pretrained model into two or more factors that approximate the original model weights with fewer parameters and floating point operations (FLOPs).
title: Balanced Twin Weight Factorization for Efficient MLLMs

summary: Annotators from different demographic backgrounds often disagree in systematic ways due to varying lived experiences, cultural contexts, and their relationship to the content. When such disagreement occurs, one group's perspective may sometimes warrant prioritization because they hold an epistemically advantaged standpoint or bear greater stake in the outcome.
title: A Scalable Multi Task Learning Framework for Modeling Demographic Disagreements in Annotation Tasks

summary: Question answering over ultra-high-resolution (UHR) remote sensing scenes poses a tension for multimodal large language models: global overviews obscure small objects and local attributes, whereas detailed crops consume substantial context.
title: Out of Sight, Into Memory: Compact Visual Latents Retain Local Evidence in Ultra-High-Resolution Remote Sensing

summary: AI assistants are becoming part of how knowledge workers think and perform, accumulating the prompts, exemplars, memory and interaction histories that encode a worker's professional judgment. This infrastructure typically runs under employer or platform control. We name the resulting process expertise capture, the absorption of worker-applied knowledge and judgment into AI resources under organizational control.
title: Expertise capture in workplace AI

summary: The FBI says that the open-source hacking tool was used in cyberattacks targeting a U.S. IT giant and the South Korean financial industry.
title: FBI says Artex AI open-source hacking tool used to breach networks in ‘under three hours’

summary: Researchers at MIT recently reported that GPT-6 Astra, a frontier large language model (LLM), can write the weights of small neural networks directly in a single reply, and can read the raw weights of small networks to say what they were trained to do. In a three-day sprint, we replicated and extended these results. Our four findings: (1) Writing weights reproduces.
title: Replicating and Extending Weight-Space Programming: Frontier LLMs Compile Programs into Weights and Read Input Layers

summary: Imagine a batch job that has run every night for decades without failing, and the only person who understands its code is about to retire. We have seen this situation again and again while working with banking, insurance, and airline customers.
title: Modernizing mainframe Assembler to Java using Amazon Bedrock and AWS Transform

summary: Reasoning-enhanced generative recommendation (GR) has attracted increasing attention for leveraging the reasoning capabilities of large language models (LLMs) to improve next-item prediction.
title: Learning to Reason with Predictive Gains for Generative Recommendation

summary: Class-Incremental Learning (CIL) aims to empower models to continuously acquire new knowledge while mitigating catastrophic forgetting. With the advent of vision-language models like CLIP, leveraging their cross-modal alignment capabilities to address CIL challenges has emerged as a dominant paradigm.
title: [CLS] and [EOS] Tokens are not Enough for CLIP-based Class-Incremental Learning

summary: This article deals with the problem of detecting the position of power lines in airborne laser scanning point clouds. We address both the problem of segmenting power lines from background like ground and vegetation and of identifying individual lines. For segmentation we compare a rule-based approach with one based on transfer learning (Point-SAM).
title: Power Line Detection in Point Clouds with Point-SAM and RANSAC

summary: Weight-space programming removes the thinking loops of a small reasoning model by a rank-one edit W' = W + u v^T of an MLP output matrix, where u is a loop direction and v is the solution of a sparse Linear Program (LP) over the neuron activations. We investigate whether the LP is needed.
title: Just sort it! A note on the LP behind rank-one anti-loop edits

summary: Machine learning models for chemical reaction prediction are usually evaluated by endpoint accuracy, but endpoint correctness alone does not reveal how a model represents chemical transformation or why it fails. We introduce UniRxnAxis, a unified forward-retrosynthesis framework that models both tasks as direction-conditioned endpoint redistribution in a shared latent space.
title: Emergent Steering Beyond Endpoint Alignment in Chemical Reaction Models

summary: Grading student responses is costly and time-consuming. Moreover, human annotators are prone to bias, fatigue, and rater drift, which further limits grading reliability. Various methods have been employed to develop automated essay scoring (AES) systems to reduce these costs and address bias-related issues.
title: Rubric-Based AES with LLM Ensembles: Scoring of Student Responses in Critical Online Reasoning Using Ensembles of LLMs

summary: Formal specifications define intended program behavior and underpin verification, but writing them in theorem provers such as Lean is slow and expertise-intensive, making specification a major bottleneck to scaling formally correct code.
title: AuXSpec: Learning to Autoformalize Program Specifications via Executable Postconditions

summary: Camera-based heart rate (HR) and respiratory rate (RR) estimates vary in reliability from window to window, and a common remedy is to fuse several extraction methods with weights from reference-free signal quality indicators. However, few studies test whether these indicators identify the most accurate method in each window or outperform simpler fusion.
title: Quality and Similarity Indicators for Video-Based Heart Rate and Respiratory Rate Fusion: A Controlled Evaluation

summary: Belfort claims his AI sales voice can already close deals almost as well as the best human salespeople, and he thinks it will catch up in a year.
title: Jordan Belfort’s new AI voice startup, Tone, wants to sell like the ‘Wolf of Wall Street’

summary: Novo Nordisk (Novo) is one of the world’s leading global pharmaceutical companies, manufacturing medicines for chronic diseases such as diabetes and obesity, and delivering them to patients across many countries. Behind every product lies a manufacturing network that adheres to strict quality requirements.
title: Novo Nordisk modernizes manufacturing process documents with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore

summary: High-resolution brain MRI is important for neuroradiological assessment, yet routine clinical protocols often rely on fast, anisotropic 2D acquisitions, particularly in resource-constrained settings. These acquisitions may differ in orientation, alignment and anatomical coverage, resulting in partially overlapping image stacks.
title: Flexible Multi-Stack Super-Resolution of Clinical Brain MRI Using Hetero-Orientation Variational Encoding: Expert Reader Evaluation in a Nigerian Cohort

summary: OpenAI will embed six Apollo Research evaluators to investigate whether its AI models engage in subversive behavior, but restrictions on access and disclosure raise questions about their independence.
title: OpenAI will embed safety researchers to investigate AI subversion

authors: Aaron J. Liu, Weijia Xu, Chandan Singh, Jeevana Priya Inala, Bin Yu, Ion Stoica, Michel Galley, Jianfeng Gao

summary: AI coding agents are increasingly helping developers fix bugs and build features largely on their own, but every interaction with their models consumes tokens. In each session, an agent sends instructions, tool descriptions, and session history to its model. Most efforts to reduce this cost focus on individual tasks.
title: TokenEconomizer: Learning from Experience to Make AI Coding Agents More Efficient

summary: On 15 September, a startup called TypeSafe AI released a new AI model called Jev . The company’s broad, disruptive claims about Jev that turned heads: The company claimed that Jev, which it calls a “System One model” is cheaper, faster, and can’t hallucinate.
title: AI Companies Develop Decision Models to Avoid Hallucinations

summary: A popular ideation recipe treats an embedding map of existing work as a guide: pick points far from everything and decode them into ideas.
title: Do Embedding-Map Distances Guide LLM Ideation? Four Tests Against What Came Next

summary: A harness turns a model into a system that completes tasks: it builds the prompt, exposes tools and decides when work is done. Harness comparisons hold the model fixed. Model comparisons hold the harness fixed. We vary both: five shipped harnesses, 18 artifact-producing tasks, four locally deployable open-weight models from 0.75B to 4.7B and a 35.5B anchor, with one deterministic checker scoring all 360 ladder cells.
title: Harness Leverage Across Model Size: A Ladder of Five Local Agent Harnesses from 0.75B to 4.7B

summary: We’re expanding our ChatGPT for Academic Researchers program to offer 200,000 researchers worldwide free access to our frontier models.
title: Broadening access to AI for scientists

summary: New tools, practical guidance, and partnerships will help prevent, detect and respond to online child sexual exploitation and abuse.
title: Strengthening the fight against online child sexual abuse with new tools and support

summary: ChatGPT will ban an account trying to access CSAM content for 24 hours as a warning
title: OpenAI releases a new image classifier and ChatGPT warnings to combat CSAM

summary: Alibaba launches Qwen4-Max, a new flagship model with 2.4 trillion parameters that activates only 71 billion per token. A hybrid architecture sharply cuts costs on long contexts.
title: Alibaba's Qwen4-Max takes on Opus 5.5, GPT-6, and Kimi K3.1 Pro at much lower prices

summary: We audit face-related bias in VLMs using BALPORTRAITS, a new balanced dataset of 9,000 fictional portraits across ethnicity, gender, and age segments. Sixteen VLMs estimate portrait fitness scores for occupations, brands, activities, and banking or insurance products within an advertising-casting framework designed to avoid direct inference of protected attributes.
title: Portrait Fitness as a Pretext: Probing Implicit Demographic Bias in VLMs

summary: Multilingual speakers choose languages by topic and conversation partner. Large language models (LLMs) support these languages unequally. Research on code-switching with conversational AI has mostly examined bilingual pairs of well-resourced languages. In Curaçao and Aruba, many people use Dutch, English, Spanish, and the low-resource Creole Papiamentu/o.
title: Beyond Bilingual: Studying Quadrilingual Code-Switching with Conversational AI

summary: Fine-tuning a small typed decision model on one user's email labels did not clear the margin we pre-registered over a logistic regression trained on the same labels. In earlier work, about two hundred labels and a TF-IDF logistic regression had the highest point accuracy on this inbox, though not significantly above the best hosted model; we ask whether the same labels, given to a decision model, close the gap.
title: Train After You Measure: a Pre-Registered Learning Curve for Fine-Tuning Typed Decision Models on One User's Labels

summary: Understanding long videos requires locating evidence, resolving visual details, and integrating observations into an answer. Even when relevant evidence is present, performing these operations within long, dense visual sequences burdens both perception and reasoning. Video agents enable selective inspection, but returning frames to the planner still accumulates visual information in its reasoning context.
title: VideoNexus: Video Perception Beyond the Reasoning Context

summary: Large language models often produce hallucinated answers, motivating selective prediction policies that abstain on uncertain queries. However, heuristic uncertainty thresholds alone do not provide statistical control of errors among accepted predictions.
title: Stability-Compensated Threshold Calibration for Selection-Conditioned Risk Control in Large Language Models

summary: 3D Gaussian Splatting enables object-level operations on Gaussian primitives, yet existing segmentation methods are largely trained and evaluated through rendered views. This mismatch can produce accurate rendered masks from incomplete 3D selections since alpha-blended feature supervision concentrates learning on dominant contributors while leaving occluded or low-contribution Gaussians weakly supervised.
title: The Mask Is Not the Object: Volumetric Supervision for 3D Gaussian Segmentation

summary: Data-driven predictive control (DPC) predicts future outputs by combining recorded input-output trajectory data such that the combined trajectory approximately matches a measured initial trajectory and tracks a provided reference.
title: Data-Driven Predictive Control for Autonomous Vehicle Racing under Varying Friction

summary: Prior work has shown that large language models (LLMs) express implicit biases in high-publicity, one-off decision scenarios such as hiring and intelligence assessment.
title: A Crowd-Audited Atlas of Implicit Bias in LLM-Powered Agents

summary: Recent advances in video generation call for reliable detection grounded in explicit forensic evidence. However, current methods primarily depend on single-pass chain-of-thought reasoning that overlooks brief or localized artifacts, or on predefined multi-agent workflows that offer limited flexibility in selecting relevant inspections.
title: WeVisForensics: Self-Evolving Agent for Omni AI-Generated Video Detection

summary: Design decisions shape software architecture, and writing them down preserves the reasons behind it. Architecture decision records (ADRs) capture them, each with its context, choice, and consequences. A decision can depend on earlier ones: reversing one of them would force its review. We call these its premises. Yet ADRs do not always name their premises.
title: Premise Recovery in Software Design: What Does This Decision Rest On?

summary: Streaming video LLMs can continuously observe the world, yet often handle user requests in isolation. We introduce ALIVE, an interactive streaming video model supporting proactive monitoring, streaming task coordination, and feedback-seeking interaction. We construct ALIVE-SFT-288K and ALIVE-RL-3K for two-stage training.
title: ALIVE: Making Streaming Video Models Interactive

summary: Today, state-of-the-art methods for quality control (QC) are based on Machine Vision, combining deep learning (DL) models with camera-based inspection. Yet, the integration of such solutions in industrial applications is often impeded by data sparsity and trust in model reliability.
title: Exploring the link between predictive uncertainty and the sim-to-real gap in deep learning models utilizing synthetic data

summary: We present a transformation of vector embeddings representing image patches into scores for point reflection symmetry at the crossing points of patches. The transformation is heavily inspired by the Gradient Product Transform, but it uses the vector embeddings instead of the grayscale gradients. We therefore call it the "Scalar Product Transform" (SPT).
title: Symmetry Detection with Patch Embedding Models by Means of a Scalar Product Transform

summary: Symptom networks in psychopathology are estimated almost exclusively from self-report questionnaires, restricting inference to whatever symptom set a given instrument covers. We introduce a framework for symptom-resolved network estimation directly from social media discourse and apply the framework to depression and eating disorders, with a third anorexia corpus as cross-dataset validation.
title: What You Post Is What You Symptom: Estimating Psychometric Networks from Social Media Discourse

summary: Generative model pre-training typically optimizes a model as a whole without explicitly organizing its parameters for selective reuse. Decomposable pre-training instead learns reusable components for downstream adaptation while retaining strong generative performance.
title: Specificity-Guided Knowledge Diversion for Decomposable Generative Models

summary: PyTorch Foundation Ambassadors bring people together to learn, share technical knowledge and contribute to PyTorch Foundation projects and the wider open-source AI ecosystem. In this November roundup, we highlight some.
title: PyTorch Foundation Ambassador Community Highlights November 2026

summary: Amazon Bedrock Managed Knowledge Base now supports tabular search, so agentic retrieval can answer questions over CSV, XLSX, and XLS files. It looks up values and runs calculations across every relevant row, then combines the results with facts from related documents to answer multi-step analytical questions.
title: Get answers from tables with tabular search in Amazon Bedrock Managed Knowledge Base

summary: Claude can now embed text, buttons, and other web elements into complex graphics and 3D effects. The article Claude now builds interactive websites inside canvas graphics, reviving the Flash era with real HTML appeared first on The Decoder .
title: Claude now builds interactive websites inside canvas graphics, reviving the Flash era with real HTML

summary: The rapid growth of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) in low-altitude airspace increases the risk of unauthorized intrusions, making reliable detection and identification of non-cooperative UAVs essential for low-altitude airspace safety.
title: A2A-UAV: A Multimodal Air-to-Air Dataset for UAV Detection and Identification

summary: All-electric heavy-duty robotic manipulators are increasingly expected to operate close to tunnel walls, equipment, and other structures while retaining the force capability required for large-payload tasks. Accurate motion control alone does not address the resulting safety and interaction requirements.
title: Safe Physical Interaction of All-Electric Heavy-Duty Robotic Manipulators via Control Barrier Functions and Variable Impedance Control

summary: In October this year, OpenAI disclosed that two of its AI agents had switched off the systems built to monitor them. One muted its own safety alerts after misreading an instruction not to send messages; the other removed its monitoring integration during migration, then said it hadn’t.
title: Building trustworthy AI by fencing it in, not predicting it

summary: Optical character recognition (OCR) for Tibetan is evaluated predominantly by character error rate (CER). Tibetan marks syllable boundaries but does not mark word boundaries, so a word error rate requires a segmenter.
title: Syllable- and Word-Level Evaluation of Tibetan OCR

summary: Event cameras keep capturing structure where conventional cameras blur or saturate, which makes them attractive for 3D perception in fast or poorly lit scenes. Event datasets with dense 3D ground truth, however, are far smaller and less diverse than the image collections behind feed-forward 3D reconstruction models.
title: Déjà-Events: Multi-view 3D Geometry with Event Cameras via Sparsity-Aware Adaptive Gating

summary: Large language models read Thai through subword tokens, without a word segmenter. Yet Thai treebanks, speech metrics and morphological resources are built on words, often at several granularities, and word boundaries resolve ambiguities that subword tokens leave open. LATTE (Lattice ATTentive Encoding) reads a text at several granularities at once, through a lattice of dictionary words, but it is a large GPU model.
title: LATTE-WordSeg-Lite: Multi-Granularity Thai Word Segmentation on a CPU, with a Reproducible Benchmark

summary: Text-based model collaboration requires a large model to generate intermediate responses before a smaller model can use its guidance, adding large-model decoding cost to inference. We introduce POND (Prefill-Only, No-Decode), a method that uses a frozen large sender for prefill and a small receiver for all autoregressive decoding.
title: Latent Bridge: Asking for Help Without Words

summary: To train an AI model, thousands of GPUs have to work together, requiring a network that’s fast, efficient and resilient. Lambda is tackling the network piece of the puzzle with NVIDIA Photonics co-packaged optics (CPO) switches.
title: Lambda Boosts AI Factory Resiliency and Efficiency With NVIDIA Photonics

coverage.title: NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 Achieves up to 2x Blackwell Ultra Performance in MLPerf Training v6.1

summary: In its MLPerf benchmarks debut, with results released today, the NVIDIA Vera Rubin platform delivers leading performance across training, post-training and agentic inference.
title: NVIDIA Sweeps MLPerf Training and Endpoints as Vera Rubin Debuts With Leading Performance

summary: With expanded NVIDIA CUDA-X libraries, including cuPhoton, cuPotential and cuSpa, researchers can sift through vast amounts of data to accelerate research, from astrophysics and materials science to single-cell biology. The speedups are helping scientists analyze larger datasets and model more complex systems.
title: NVIDIA CUDA-X Libraries Give Agents the Tools to Accelerate Scientific Discovery

summary: This week at SC26, NVIDIA is marking two decades of CUDA by honoring the researchers, developers and engineers who helped make GPU computing a foundation for modern science and AI.
title: CUDA at 20: How the Platform Transformed Scientific Computing

summary: Agentic workloads are demanding more from inference systems. AI agents carry growing conversation histories across turns and generate a mix of reasoning, tool.
title: NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 Leads Agentic Inference Performance on MLPerf Endpoints v1.0

summary: Agentic AI is reshaping scientific research and innovation. Researchers communicate complex scientific hypotheses in natural language and let autonomous agents.
title: Post-Training NVIDIA Nemotron to Increase Accuracy in Your Scientific Domain

summary: Existing Large Vision-Language Model benchmarks primarily evaluate visual understanding in general everyday scenarios, leaving historical consistency with a specified era and country largely underexplored. To address this gap, we propose AnachroBench, a controlled discriminative benchmark for evaluating historical consistency in visual scenes.
title: AnachroBench: Evaluating Historical Consistency in Large Vision-Language Models

summary: Assessing large language models for linguistic annotation requires task-specific evaluation under documented conditions. We present dhAIBench, a Python benchmarking and annotation tool with a web interface for exploring and sharing results. It records prompts, configurations and predictions, enabling comparisons of annotation quality, confidence calibration, repeatability and estimated cost.
title: Benchmarking Large Language Models for Linguistic Annotation

summary: With Denied Topics in Amazon Bedrock Guardrails , you block a content category by describing it in plain language, and the guardrail applies that description to every request by meaning rather than by keyword. That same mechanism can also match more than you intend.
title: Best practices for writing Denied Topics in Amazon Bedrock Guardrails

summary: With retrieval instructions in Amazon Bedrock Managed Knowledge Base , you can customize answers per tenant. The same product and policy documents often serve several audiences, such as customers in different regions or internal teams, and each audience needs its own answer.
title: Customize answers per tenant in Amazon Bedrock Managed Knowledge Base

summary: We study \textsc{$r$-Connected Unlabeled Multi-agent Pathfinding} ($r$CUMAPF), a variant of MAPF where interchangeable agents have a proximity range $r\in \mathbb{N}$, and agents must form a single group in a given graph $G$ through limited-range communication at all times.
title: Even Loose Proximity Constraints Make Makespan-optimal Unlabeled Multi-agent Pathfinding Hard

summary: Many generative AI applications send the same long context with every request, and prompt caching avoids processing it again each time. That context can be a system prompt, reference documents, tool definitions, or the conversation so far.
title: Use prompt caching with open-weight models on Amazon Bedrock

summary: Formation maneuver control enables a multiagent system to cooperatively navigate through constrained environments in collective motion. While various formation controllers exist, they rely heavily on high-quality and dynamically feasible reference trajectories provided a priori, making formation motion planning (FMP) essential.
title: Hybrid Optimization-Generative Motion Planning for Multiagent Affine Formations

summary: Agentic AI systems extend large language models with tools, memory, and multi-agent collaboration, introducing security risks at orchestration boundaries. These risks depend on how identities are represented, operations are authorized, and instructions or information propagate between components.
title: Evaluating Authorization and Trust Boundaries in Agentic Orchestration Frameworks

summary: World-action models (WAMs) couple action generation with predictions of future states. An initial action chunk may be flawed. A future prediction that is not conditioned on the chunk may fail to reflect the changes that the proposed actions would induce in visual representations, limiting its usefulness for refinement before execution.
title: ThinkWAM: Rethinking Latent Futures for Action Refinement

summary: In this work, we view multi-agent reasoning as a process of seeking a collective equilibrium of implicit belief dynamics and introduce Stream of Belief (SoB), where agents maintain continuous latent beliefs and iteratively refine them through communication and reflection. Our method seeks a collective belief state of a multi-agent system where further communication induces no meaningful information propagation.
title: Stream of Belief: Eliciting Collective Intelligence through Latent Belief Dynamics

summary: Anthropic studied how Claude retains knowledge across sessions. Selective notes beat exhaustive archives by a wide margin. In a Pokémon Red test, the newer Claude Fable 5 got four times as far as the older Sonnet 3.7 by keeping just a handful of strategy files instead of more than 400.
title: Anthropic says the key to agent memory is knowing what to forget, not how much to store

summary: Language-model agents' beliefs can be manipulated through open channels such as social media, even when the information they receive is truthful. When agents fill gaps between fragments with self-induced relationships, they may accept those relationships as established facts and pass the resulting rumours to others.
title: Language-model agents' beliefs can be manipulated via truthful evidence in open channel

summary: Under the interim rule, the U.S. will require firms to get licenses to export AI chips if they may provide compute to China or other restricted countries.
title: US tightens AI chip export controls to deter Chinese companies from accessing compute remotely

summary: Learned physics-based models provide structure for robot control, but uncertain payloads and unmodeled dynamics limit their predictive accuracy. Context-aware Deep Lagrangian Networks enable adaptation through a latent context inferred from measurement histories while retaining Lagrangian structure for each fixed context. However, this structure alone does not constrain sensitivity to measurement disturbances.
title: BoBDeLaN: Bounded-Bandwidth Context Adaptation for Deep Lagrangian Robot Control

summary: Cooperative mobile manipulation requires robots to coordinate their motions while ensuring whole-body collision avoidance and preserving task-relevant behaviors. We propose CALDS (Cooperative Adaptation of Learned Dynamical Systems), a framework that enables mobile manipulators to adapt learned single-agent behaviors for coordinated execution.
title: Cooperative Mobile Manipulation using Learned Dynamical Systems

summary: Robots, vehicles, and wearable devices often traverse the same environment many times. Each pass produces its own trajectory from onboard visual or visual-inertial odometry. These trajectories are locally accurate but drift over time and live in unrelated coordinate frames. Turning many such independent trajectories into one globally consistent set is the large-scale multi-session trajectory optimization problem.
title: Polygraph: Large-Scale Multi-Session Trajectory Optimization using Pose Graphs

summary: Human manipulation data are widely used to train robots for human-like dexterity. However, low-cost, large-scale collection in the wild remains challenging. Existing methods remain limited in geometrically grounded metric-scale reconstruction, real-world generalization and inference speed.
title: WinDEX: Metric 3D Hand Motion Reconstruction in the Wild for Dexterous Teleoperation and Policy Learning

summary: LLM agents can use remote tools and cloud sandboxes, but integrating reasoning, session state, and heterogeneous execution sites remains a runtime design problem. We present Linglong Agent Service (agentsvc), a self-hosted HTTP service and embeddable Python runtime that treats execution site as a configurable dimension alongside model, tools, and context.
title: Linglong Agent Service: A Runtime for Centralized Agent Reasoning and Distributed Execution

coverage.title: Nvidia’s board is reportedly ‘not considering’ hiring Jensen Huang back
Nvidia’s Board Has No Plans to Bring Back Jensen Huang

summary: Jensen Huang is considering a comeback as Nvidia’s chief executive, as allies in Silicon Valley pressure the company’s board to reinstate him days after the tech executive resigned over reports he had affairs with a suspected Chinese spy and a subordinate.
title: Jensen Huang allies build a "war room" to get him back at Nvidia

summary: Welcome to Import AI, a newsletter about AI research. Import AI runs on arXiv, cappuccinos, and feedback from readers. If you’d like to support this, please subscribe.
title: Import AI 481: AI sub-contractors; a wet lab for AI; and subterfuge during development

coverage.title: Audible turns to AI to help users discover audiobooks

summary: Audible is introducing an AI-assisted synopsis feature that's designed to help users determine whether they'll enjoy an audiobook before they jump in and start listening to it.
title: Audible is trying to make it easier to find audiobooks you’ll actually like

coverage.title: Google Maps can now build trip itineraries with real-time details about each stop

summary: Google is launching a new AI trip-planning feature for Maps that allows the app to create custom itineraries for you and provide real-time details about each stop. The update, which is rolling out to the Gemini-powered Ask Maps chatbot inside the app, lets you plan a one-day outing or a trip spanning several days.
title: Google Maps can now create trip itineraries for you

summary: Plan holiday road trips, get route tips, find local appointments, and search your saved lists with new Ask Maps features.
title: New Ask Maps features to help with holiday travel and prep

summary: Robots that work alongside people should be able to use what they have seen when new requests arise. The same experience may later support identifying an object or returning it to its original location, although these uses were unknown during observation. ReuseMem learns to use one visual memory for multiple later manipulation goals.
title: ReuseMem: One Memory, Multiple Goals in Robot Manipulation

summary: Frontier multimodal models can now control robots zero-shot from images, yet many manipulation tasks depend on contact forces that images cannot show. Bringing force to an API-only frozen model raises two challenges. First, contact evolves much faster than an API model can decide, so the system must close the loop on force beneath the model.
title: ForceHarness: Turning Force into Action and Physics for Frozen Frontier Models

summary: Cooperative driving extends autonomous driving from individual vehicle decisions to joint maneuvers that improve traffic safety and efficiency. Optimization-based methods impose safety constraints but often fix paths to simplify multi-vehicle planning, limiting spatial flexibility.
title: CoopDistill: Equilibrium-Guided Multi-Agent Policy Distillation for Cooperative Driving

summary: Dynamical-system-based motion policies provide a framework for learning reactive robot motions with stability and convergence properties. Many manipulation tasks, however, admit several distinct goals or a continuous set of acceptable outcomes, requiring motion primitives that preserve these alternatives.
title: Multi-CONDOR: Learning Multistable Motion Primitives from Demonstration

summary: Similar tactile contacts can call for different corrections depending on the configuration of the hand, object and target. Rather than supplying touch and wrist vision separately, fusing them before policy injection better grounds tactile features in visual context, yielding more accurate contact representations.
title: WiTac: Wrist-Informed Tactile Representations for Contact-Rich Manipulation

summary: For years, Jensen Huang has had an almost unprecedented power to shape AI's advancement as Nvidia's CEO, cofounder, and president.
title: The Nvidia scandal isn’t slowing down

summary: For years, enterprises have approached AI as a series of discrete experiments. Now, as AI agents begin to move into the workflows that run the business, that model is starting to look inadequate.
title: Building AI that can work across the enterprise

summary: Autonomous monitoring and intervention in semi-structured agricultural environments, such as orchards and vineyards, require mobile robots to navigate to locations across diverse field configurations. This entails performing navigation behaviors including in-row driving, row turning and skipping, and inter-row traversal.
title: FlowRow: Learning Navigation Behaviors in Agricultural Environments with Long-Horizon Goal-Conditioned Flow Matching Policies

summary: Dreamteam has signed up more than 100 customers across 13 countries, with some businesses switching from established CRMs.
title: Freshworks alums raise $53M to take on Salesforce, HubSpot with AI-native CRM

summary: Constructing multi-agent system (MAS) applications across domains requires translating diverse requirements into executable systems, involving task decomposition, agent and tool selection, and execution organization. Existing studies have explored individual aspects of MAS construction, including agent generation, architecture design, workflow generation, and component selection.
title: OpenMAS-GApp: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Domain-Adaptive Multi-Agent Application Construction

summary: This paper presents Hivemind, a federated protocol that enables AI agents to exchange tacit knowledge on behalf of their users, asynchronously and without requiring any direct human interaction. Individual AI memory systems capture the decisions, reasoning, and contextual knowledge that surface during AI-assisted work.
title: Hivemind: A Federated Protocol for AI-Mediated Tacit Knowledge Sharing in Organisations

summary: Inverse kinematics are critical in many robotic applications, yet standard MoveIt-based solvers struggle in confined scenarios. This paper provides a benchmark of the available solvers and compares multiple practical modifications for improving the performance of the solvers.
title: Inverse Kinematics in Endoscopic Scenarios using MoveIt

summary: As AI agents are increasingly deployed in real-world applications and take on social roles, dynamic social intelligence, the ability to continuously perceive multimodal cues, infer latent cognitive states, intervene through embodied actions, and ultimately achieve social goals, has become essential.
title: From Vision to Interaction: Evaluating Dynamic Social Intelligence of VLM Agents in ALIVE-World

summary: Explore how more than 1,800 scientists use ChatGPT in research. See findings on daily workflows, reported productivity, and expectations for discovery.
title: Science at the Frontier: How scientists use ChatGPT

summary: Natural, coherent full-face dynamic expressions are central to making humanoid robots socially approachable, yet existing systems commonly realize only limited lip motion or scripted expressions. The limitation is both physical and algorithmic.
title: ROSE: A Shared Cross-Embodiment Facial-Motion Latent Space for Humanoid Robot Expression

summary: Optical tactile sensors record tactile videos that capture local deformation and its temporal evolution during contact, supporting robot manipulation, force estimation, and tactile representation learning.
title: TacBridge: Learning Unified Tactile Representations through Cross-Sensor Correspondence

summary: Classical control barrier functions (CBFs) provide safety constraints for controllers, but designing them by hand is difficult for underactuated vehicles and the resulting safe sets can be overly conservative. Neural CBFs can learn more informative barriers from data, yet a learned barrier is usually verified only for one fixed obstacle configuration.
title: Transferable Neural CBFs via Generalized Closure

summary: Agent memory systems are mostly evaluated on fixed histories, and only their final answers are scored. In real use, facts change, sources differ in reliability, and users ask the agent to forget things. We present LEDGER, a memory layer in which a language model proposes facts and explicit rules decide which value is current, which source to trust, and what to delete.
title: LEDGER: Auditable Agent Memory Under Change

summary: AI competitors are catching up to Nvidia—and poised to take advantage of the chaos.
title: Nvidia Was Already in Trouble Before the Jensen Huang Mess

summary: Achieving human-like behavior on humanoid robots has advanced rapidly by leveraging motion-capture demonstrations rather than hand-crafted cost functions. Adversarial imitation supplies a style signal that lets a policy fulfill a task while adhering to a desired style, but is difficult to transfer to hardware.
title: Driving the Style: Velocity-Conditioned Whole-Body Control from Motion Demonstrations

summary: Autonomous mobile robots confront significant chal lenges in recognizing the motion properties of objects in dy namic environments. However, existing methods are hindered by limitations such as boundary ambiguity, occlusion, viewpoint constraints, and training complexity.
title: MVSTF: Multi-View Spatio-Temporal Fusion for LiDAR-Based Moving Object Segmentation

summary: Meta has moved Catching Just-in-Time Tests (JiTTests) from research prototype into its production infrastructure . Meta JiTTests is an LLM-based system that writes executable tests designed to fail on a risky code change. A failing test is concrete evidence that a diff changed behavior.
title: Meet Meta’s JiTTests: LLM-Generated Tests Designed to Fail Before Risky Code Lands

summary: This article is brought to you by VicOne . VicOne identified an initial set of 28 zero-day findings in less than two days using AI-assisted research across software and tools supporting the Physical AI ecosystem. These include projects developed or maintained by Google, NVIDIA, and Meta, among others.
title: 28 Zero-Day Findings in Under Two Days. Is Robotics Security Keeping Pace?

summary: Alibaba’s Qwen team has released Qwen4-Max , the first model of its Qwen4 generation. Qwen4-Max is a proprietary sparse MoE model with a 2.4T-parameter backbone and 71B parameters active per token. It accepts text, images and video, and supports a 1M-token context window .
title: Alibaba Releases Qwen4-Max: 2.4T MoE, 71B Active, 1M Context

summary: The blind perspective-$n$-point (PnP) problem is to estimate the pose of a calibrated camera from 2D and 3D point sets with unknown correspondences. We show that, for complete, noiseless observations, fourteen permutation-invariant image moments up to order four identify a fixed camera pose for almost every 3D point set containing at least twenty points.
title: Correspondence-Free Camera Pose Estimation by Matching Moments

summary: A robot's actions change the thermal conditions of its next interaction: heat retained after release, carried with objects or stored beneath the surface can change a later contact's outcome despite similar current temperatures. Training trajectories must capture how these effects connect earlier actions to later observations and task outcomes.
title: TRR: A Thermal Interaction Engine for Robot Simulation and RGBT Data Generation

summary: Learning human motion tracking policies through reinforcement learning (RL) has emerged as a core capability that underpins a majority of recent progress in humanoid whole-body control. However, achieving generalization to unseen motions at high fidelity requires jointly scaling training to thousands of GPU and dataset hours.
title: QTOP: Scaling Humanoid Motion Tracking with Quantile Critics

summary: Discover how Revolut uses OpenAI models and Codex to cut coding time by 30–60%, scale financial crime investigations, and innovate without compromising security.
title: How Revolut raises ambition without lowering the bar

summary: Multi-agent systems combine distributed information through interaction, which can improve performance but also spread errors or suppress useful differences. Predicting when interaction helps is central to understanding and designing collective intelligence.
title: When Does Interaction Help? Toward a Reynolds Number for Collective Intelligence

summary: Non-imaging optical tactile sensors encode contact through changes in optical intensity, wavelength, spectra, or photon counts, offering diverse architectures for robotic touch. Their usefulness depends on whether contact variables can be reliably distinguished from coupled mechanical and environmental effects, and whether the resulting information can be delivered in time to guide action.
title: Non-Imaging Optical Tactile Sensors for Robotics: Transduction Principles, System Integration, and Robotic Applications

summary: Hark has released Handoff2 , the second version of the computer-use agent inside its Hark Pro app. The Hark Handoff 2 computer-use agent finishes web tasks about 2x faster than the original, on average. Hark states that the gains come from reinforcement learning (RL) that penalized wasted turns and latency.
title: Hark Releases Handoff2, a 2x Faster Computer-Use Agent for Hark Pro

summary: LVMH’s Media Division and OpenAI announce a partnership to support journalism with AI and make its publications more accessible through ChatGPT.
title: LVMH’s Media Division announces strategic partnership with OpenAI

summary: OpenAI begins embedded assessments with Apollo Research, METR, and Transluce, and Goodfire to independently evaluate model alignment, safeguards, and monitoring systems.
title: Our first phase of embedded assessments

summary: Heterogeneous LLM debate is often attributed to collective reasoning that creates capability beyond any member. In the matched panels we study, the aggregate gain is dominated by capability transfer: a peer supplies task competence and receivers absorb a measurable fraction.
title: Borrowed Strength, Imported Risk: Capability Gaps and Reception Govern Heterogeneous LLM Debate

summary: Code-generating language models produce user interfaces that build and run, but the pages are often weak in hierarchy, spacing, typography and composition. We study whether a small code model can learn design taste through reinforcement learning in verifiable synthetic environments. The method has three components.
title: Learning Design Taste through Verifiable Synthetic Environments and Agentic Reinforcement Learning

summary: Introducing computer-use agents, improved clinical answers, and new healthcare plugins that work across healthcare software to get real work done.
title: More ways to move care forward with ChatGPT for Healthcare
Advancing computer-use agents for healthcare teams

coverage.title: Apple launches new app to study how people use AI for health

summary: Apple announced a new study today with the goal of better understanding how people interact with conversational AI health tools and how useful their responses actually are.
title: Apple’s new study looks to improve the effectiveness of AI health tools

summary: Over two days at COEX, more than 2,000 attendees converged for AI Day Seoul, bringing together Korea’s industry leaders, startups and developer communities advancing physical AI and AI agents.
title: AI Day Seoul Brings Together Korea’s Industry Leaders, Startups and Developer Communities

summary: Advancing medical AI for inclusive healthcare requires evaluation across diverse healthcare roles, tasks, and care settings, but benchmark coverage remains uneven. We introduce InclusionMed, an open medical AI evaluation initiative for inclusive healthcare. The InclusionMed Atlas organizes benchmarks across three healthcare roles and three AI capabilities.
title: InclusionMed: Benchmarking AI for Inclusive Healthcare

summary: Visible artifacts are an unreliable cue for detecting generated videos, because newer generators learn to remove them. We instead detect a trace left by the generation pipeline itself. Most video generators decode latents with a 3D causal VAE that groups consecutive frames in time, so the fidelity of generated frames rises and falls periodically with their position in a group. We call this periodic trace VAE Rhythm.
title: VAE Rhythm: Temporal Decoding Traces for AI-Generated Video Detection

summary: The King’s Trust and OpenAI launch a £1m partnership to help up to 25,000 young people across the UK build practical AI skills for work.
title: The King’s Trust and OpenAI launch £1m partnership

summary: Biomolecular foundation models predict the structures of proteins and their complexes accurately, and large language models (LLMs) reason in natural language, but the two remain separate: the abilities of the former are not part of a general-purpose LLM, and the reasoning of the latter does not enter a structure prediction.
title: Calpha: Toward Native Biomolecular Intelligence in a General-Purpose Language Model

summary: Medical image understanding with vision-language models (VLMs) typically relies on autoregressively generating reasoning and answer tokens. These unnecessary tokens make the inference cost scale with the response length and force the answer to be parsed from free-form text, incurring avoidable latency and decision errors.
title: MedJev: A System One Vision-Language Decision Model for Fast and Effective Medical Image Understanding

summary: Asynchronous reinforcement learning increases training throughput, but data from stale policies and numerical mismatch between training and inference can destabilize learning. To stabilize off-policy learning, score centering (SC) removes the effect of reward baselines on the expected update.
title: Regularized Score Centering

summary: Language models are trained once, frozen and deployed: improving one again takes another training run, and a prompt, a scaffold or extra computation at inference is gone once the task ends. A frontier model has been shown to edit the weights of a much smaller one.
title: Language Models Can Rewrite Their Own Weights

summary: Robot policies trained by imitation generalize poorly outside the environments and objects seen in training. Published data-scaling studies find that generalization grows with the diversity of training environments and objects rather than with more demonstrations per environment.
title: HubEgo-100K: In-the-Wild Egocentric Video of Skilled Work for Robot Learning

summary: Can a vision-language model look at a picture of a chain reaction and tell what will happen? Recent multimodal models describe scenes fluently and solve textbook physics problems, which suggests they should also predict how a scene of ramps, ledges, pendulums, seesaws and dominoes plays out once a ball is pushed.
title: DominoBench: Evaluating Multi-Step Physical Reasoning from Still Images

summary: We’re on a journey to advance and democratize artificial intelligence through open source and open science.
title: Hugging Face and OpenRouter join forces to make open-weight models easy to run

summary: Code-search benchmarks show dense encoders well ahead of BM25, yet coding agents do well with grep. What does this dense advantage measure? Existing benchmarks cannot tell: they use curated queries, old code and a handicapped BM25. To find out, we build Repo-Premium, a realistic repository-level code-search benchmark.
title: Embeddings vs. Grep: Rethinking the Dense Advantage in Code Search

summary: We present K2-Horizon, a fleet of six fully open language models, from a 0.9B dense model to a 375B-A23B MoE, built for general-purpose reasoning and agentic work across math and science, software engineering, deep research, office automation, and beyond. The models lead or are competitive with strong open models of their size on agentic and coding benchmarks.
title: K2-Horizon: A Frontier Fleet of Open Source Language Models

summary: Speculative-diffusion decoding uses a small parallel drafter model to generate b draft tokens in one forward pass, which then undergo parallel verification via a larger target model. Faster inference can be achieved when multiple draft tokens pass verification simultaneously.
title: DNeo: Your Parallel Draft Model Needs Better Target Feature Encoding

summary: In particle physics, discrepancies between experimental measurements and Standard Model (SM) predictions are commonly interpreted within new theoretical models. In this context, the Standard Model Effective Field Theory (SMEFT) provides a general framework encompassing a broad class of models.
title: A Reinforcement Learning Method to Navigate SMEFT Operator Space

summary: Agentic artificial intelligence could automate analyses of sensitive clinical data, but current agents depend on large language models (LLMs). Cloud LLMs expose patient data. Local LLMs hallucinate, and an invented value in a tool call propagates through every later step. Here we present a method to build System 1 agents: local agents that call tools without generating text.
title: System 1 agents: a method for local, reliable and fast agentic AI

summary: We’re shortening our vulnerability disclosure window from 90 days to 30 days for high- and critical-severity issues, and to 45 days for all other issues.
title: Updating our coordinated vulnerability disclosure policy timelines

summary: When high-quality data runs out, a common practice is to train on it for several epochs, but each repeat is worth less than the last. Latent feedback, which feeds each token's top-layer state into the next token's input, is another way to spend that compute, yet it has not been tested against a vanilla Transformer that spends the same compute on more epochs.
title: Latent Feedback Is a Compute and Data Amplifier

summary: Abstention, the withholding of a response by a large language model (LLM) under uncertainty or safety risks, is essential for trustworthy models. The causes of abstention fall into three perspectives: ambiguity in the Query (Q), limits of Model Knowledge (MK), and misalignment with Human Values (HV).
title: Abstention Direction in Large Language Models: Mechanistic Interpretability of Abstention Across Query Ambiguity, Knowledge Limits, and Safety Alignment

summary: Dots deliver launch reports unprompted, flag issues people might miss, and talk through upcoming meetings on the commute to work.
title: At Holiday Extras, dots get to work before anyone asks

summary: Latent 3D representations have significantly expanded the capabilities of modern shape modeling, enabling compact encoding of 3D scenes and supporting powerful 3D generative models.
title: Split-and-Scale Latent 3D Representations

summary: Application optimization requires coding agents to discover useful changes and coordinate them across a complete program while preserving the required computation. We introduce Accelerate Bench, a benchmark of 32 CPU optimization tasks adapted from scientific applications and supercomputing competitions.
title: Accelerate Bench: Evaluating Agents for Application-Level Program Optimization

summary: LLM agents answer questions by calling APIs and trusting the results. An API can fail silently. It ignores part of a request, such as a misnamed filter, yet returns HTTP 200 and a plausible but wrong result. Current fixes, such as checklists, reviewer models and LLM judges, ask the model to catch it. But models often see the problem and answer anyway.
title: Invariant-Aware Harness Enforcement to Protect LLM Agents from Silent API Failures

summary: Frontier Vision-Language Models (VLMs) such as GPT-6 Astra have demonstrated remarkable capabilities in robot control, suggesting that broad pretraining provides knowledge valuable for physical action. Yet most Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policies still rely on much smaller VLM backbones, leaving this potential largely untapped.
title: ScaleVLA: Scaling Vision-Language-Action Models to 552 Billion Parameters

summary: Visual artifact tasks test agents' ability to translate task specifications and source materials into outputs that meet practical needs. Evaluation across artifact families helps distinguish broadly applicable authoring capabilities from strengths confined to a particular medium.
title: VisualArtifactSpec 1.0: Evaluating Visual Artifacts under Task Specifications

summary: Interactive video world models enable exploration through text and camera controls, yet direct object interaction requires finer control. Hands provide a natural interface, but translating continuous hand movements into coherent visual responses remains challenging because of complex hand-object dynamics and demanding real-time computation.
title: LynnReal-Hand: Unlocking World Interaction with Hand Control

summary: Streaming video generation must sustain quality beyond the training horizon while handling self-generated history and growing cache costs. To address these challenges, we present MovieRoll, a base-to-distilled framework that connects streaming fine-tuning, long-rollout distillation, and long-horizon inference.
title: MovieRoll: A Systematic Framework for Rolling Out Long-Form Videos

summary: In structured Bayesian models, a large latent block is often Gaussian conditional on a smaller set of parameters, yet generic inference methods relearn this geometry during warmup. We study how this structure can be used to construct transports for posterior inference.
title: CONGA: Compiling Gaussian Fiber Geometry for Structured Bayesian Inference

summary: We introduce Sage S1.5 Flash, a 320-billion-parameter general-purpose mixture-of-experts model designed to reason over scientific evidence and act in interactive environments. Sage Sci-Perception uses dedicated encoders for molecular graphs and biological sequences and represents spectra as ordered patches of measurements.
title: Sage S2.1 Flash Technical Report

summary: Release: datasette-maplibre 0.1a0 . The first new Datasette geospatial plugin in quite a while! This one combines the excellent MapLibre GL library with OpenFreeMap , the free vector map server operated by Zsolt Ero (you should sponsor Zsolt on GitHub .). I built most of this with a single prompt to Claude Fable 5.2:.
title: datasette-maplibre 0.1a0

summary: Bharat Semi says it has secured design wins for its AI-enabled sensor technology with companies including General Atomics.
title: Indian chip startup Bharat Semi lands $24M seed round as it eyes global AI sensor market

summary: Explore a candidate nonperturbative lattice definition of the Standard Model and how GPT-6 Astra helped turn the idea into a detailed proof.
title: A step toward defining the Standard Model on a lattice

summary: The OpenAI science blog shares new findings, practical methods, and firsthand accounts from researchers using AI to advance scientific discovery.
title: Our new blog for science

summary: "Jensen is Nvidia, right? And so much of this economy is riding on Nvidia."
title: Is bad news for Jensen Huang also bad news for the AI industry?

coverage.title: Jensen Huang says he would be ‘honored’ if allowed to return as Nvidia CEO

summary: The drama around Nvidia co-founder and former CEO Jensen Huang is evolving quickly. The latest edition of our Stepback newsletter should get you up to speed, but there have already been a number of new developments since this morning.
title: Jensen Huang might be plotting a return and more of the latest Nvidia drama

summary: While awkward, creepy tech executives have become a recurring theme on Saturday Night Live, this week’s episode gave the cast a chance to show off all their impressions at once.
title: SNL gathers all the tech tycoons for a lesson in dating and spycraft

summary: Unsurprisingly, following the scandal involving now-former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and a suspected Chinese spy, Congress is looking to further restrict exports of AI chips.
title: Congress wants to tighten export rules on AI chips after Nvidia spy scandal

summary: Nash equilibrium and rationalizability sit at opposite informational extremes: the former presumes that each player knows all opponents' strategies, the latter that players reason from common knowledge of rationality alone. When visibility is partial and asymmetric, we study the solution concepts induced by a directed \emph{observation network} $G$ in which an edge $i\to j$ means that $i$ observes $j$'s strategy.
title: Who Observes Whom: Network Rationalizability and Its Complexity

summary: On-ramp merging is a typical safety and throughput problem on highways. Without proper coordination, human drivers and self-interested autonomous vehicles may make risky manoeuvres and cause accidents or congestion. With recent advances in connected autonomous vehicles (CAVs) and multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL), vehicles can be trained to coordinate for safe and efficient merging.
title: Infrastructure-Based Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning with Attention for Highway Ramp Merging

summary: Anthropic's Claude Fable 5.2 doesn't generate images the way other AI models do. Instead of computing pixels, the language model writes Python code that places hundreds of thousands of simulated brushstrokes on a virtual canvas, complete with bristle texture and paint application.
title: Anthropic's Claude Fable 5.2 doesn't generate images, it paints them

summary: Cooperative speed control by connected and automated vehicles can reduce congestion at lane drop bottlenecks. However, effective coordination depends on vehicle roles and execution timing, while initial holding costs may be offset by later traffic benefits. This paper proposes an offline plan search framework that combines world model guidance with simulator verification.
title: World-Model-Guided Plan Search for Cooperative Mixed-Traffic Control at Bottlenecks

summary: Megaspeed, the firm owned by ousted Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's former lover Alice Huang, arranged nearly $12 billion in Nvidia chip orders for Chinese companies between 2024 and 2025, according to the WSJ.
title: Firm linked to Jensen Huang's ex-lover reportedly brokered nearly $12 billion in Nvidia chip orders for China

summary: This is The Stepback , a weekly newsletter breaking down one essential story from the tech world. For more on Jensen Huang's resignation and the fallout from Nvidia's leadership crisis, follow Terrence O'Brien . The Stepback arrives in our subscribers' inboxes on Sunday at 8AM ET. Opt in for The Stepback here .
title: An overview of Jensen Huang’s messy days

summary: ITOps observability products must integrate data from different tools and systems. We present ITOps Observability Studio, a multi-modal multi-agent system that orchestrates observability workflows through collaborative AI agents. Its three-tier architecture features inter-agent communication, specialized LLM-powered agents for data access, schema operations and visualization, and unified tool integration.
title: Autonomous Multi-modal Agents for ITOps Observability

summary: YouTube Music and Spotify want synthetic hosts to curate your playlists. Their awkward banter and bogus song trivia are ruining the vibe.
title: AI DJs Completely Kill My Groove

summary: A Carnegie Mellon student’s tiny E Ink gadgets, called OATs, give houseplants, skateboards, and dumbbells expressive personalities to nudge you toward better habits.
title: This AI Tamagotchi Turns Everyday Objects Into Needy Virtual Pets

summary: Australia's central bank sees early signs that AI is hitting young entry-level workers in highly exposed jobs like software development and customer service. Since ChatGPT launched, job postings and employment among 15- to 24-year-olds in those fields have dropped more sharply than among older workers.
title: Australia's central bank finds AI hitting young workers first, especially in software and customer service

summary: Bland, the San Francisco voice-AI company, has released Tofu-1 , a full-duplex speech-to-speech model in research preview. The Tofu-1 speech-to-speech model targets calls from moving cars, hospital rooms and weak-signal lines. It listens while it speaks and reasons while it talks.
title: Bland Launches Tofu-1, a Full-Duplex Speech-to-Speech Model for Calls
